text: Ya know, there's nothing better then going here then if someone else is paying for it. Friends took us out as a thank you- and they like this place as much as we do. It was during the week so the place was not overbooked and it was nice and quiet. We had a table in the corner just as I like it and the service was attentive as always. You usually don't know they are there and just go on talking. I had the lobster bisque, penne pasta with shrimp and the apple crisp with a dollop of vanilla ice cream. I have to say I WAS a tad disappointed in the the lack of flavoring in the lobster bisque. It was just not up to the Kimberton standards that I expect. Boo Hoo.... But the shrimp with pasta was mouth melting devine. I was in heaven. Yeah really. Sorry, I get that way sometimes. And the warm apple crisp, oh how happy I was that I did not order a chocolate dessert. Can you imagine? My husband had the crusted bass with balsamic reduction. The fish alone was good, but the reduction made it pop. My friend had the liver.................liver? who goes to a restaurant and orders liver? It was delicious. With bacon and onions and a potato mash. She also had an open lobster roll for an appetizer that also was mouth watering, but since they were paying for the meal I didn't want to put them to break the bank. Her husband had a steak with tiny shoe string potatoes that was huge. If I were a big meat eater I would have attacked it across the table. The atmosphere makes a big difference in the food here also. It is quiet, relaxing, and you can take your time. I don't come here often because it is a little pricey, but it really is special.
label: POS

text: A few points to be made. Dyer Chiropractic has an attractive office, and is conveniently located... The office has an open concept floor plan, which seemed a little weird at first, but which ended up being okay. Despite these good points, I will not be going back to this office, and I wouldn't recommend it to anyone else either. I first went there because I was suffering from some persistent headaches and chiropractic has helped with those in the past. We had recently moved from out of state and I needed a new chiropractor. I went a handful of times... The first visit was nothing more than a consultation, which was a bit disappointing, as I had hoped to get an adjustment that day. As I said, I was dealing with some pretty bad headaches and I needed relief. He recommended that I go to a hospital to get some spinal x-rays, because I had not had any in a couple of years. I got them that evening, and hand delivered them to their office. One thing that made me a bit uncomfortable was the sense of forced Christianity while I was there. In a professional office, I expect for the interactions to be professional, and kinda surprised by the comments that he would make periodically. For example, at one point, he said to me, "Christ is great, isn't he?" Only, it wasn't a rhetorical question... He asked it again when I didn't respond the first time. This made for an awkward interaction because I feel that spirituality is a private matter and not something I need to be discussing with persons I barely know. Despite this, I made my first appointment, and things went fine enough. The next time I was there, I happened to be scheduled right after a woman who seemed to think that the chiropractor was also her therapist. She was in the next stall over, and talked and talked and talked. This went on for literally half an hour... all while I was sitting there waiting. He finally got to me and made no apologies for making me wait. I was willing to see this as a fluke, but it just so happened that my next appointment was ALSO scheduled just after this woman. This time, he was with her for even LONGER. I considered walking out, as my time is just as valuable as his, and anyone else's. Finally he made it to me, and he did apologise this time, telling me that, "Some people need a little more help." Fine. But we're all customers. I felt that he should have adjusted me first, and gotten me out of the way if he knew that this woman needed more "help" (i.e. time to chit chat.) Fast forward to three weeks ago. Despite tri-weekly visits to their office, no one had ever told me that I had an outstanding balance... but they finally got around to letting me know. My health fund had apparently run out, and the rest would be out-of-pocket. No big deal... But I would have like to be notified BEFORE two months of co-pays had accumulated. A week after that (two weeks ago) we received our first and ONLY bill from them. TODAY... I got a voicemail from their office asking me to take care of the "situation" with my bill, and telling me that they didn't want to have to turn me over to collections. I was floored. I had not had the bill in my hands for more than a couple weeks, and on top of that, I was still waiting to see if the insurance made any more payments before paying my balance. I feel insulted that they brought up turning me over to collections as though I was some sort of criminal. This is especially troubling considering the strong "Christian" message they seem to hold to so dearly. This is clearly another example an entity claiming to embrace Christian values while acting in a way that is contrary to that. As I said, I won't be back.
label: NEG

text: Meh indeed. First - we had a great rate, through Priceline I got our room for $28.00. The room itself was large and clean. End of the positive marks. The toiletries were awful. I usually donate my left-over hotel goodies to a shelter in SF but I wouldn't inflict these on anyone. The noise level was beyond belief. Our next door neighbors were alternately vocally amorous and throwing punches while screaming at the top of their lungs. I literally had to call security because of the fight one night. They put the guy out of the hotel. You know it's bad when you have to wear earplugs to get some shut-eye and you can STILL hear the folks and their "Oooh baby, mm hmm, yes yes you GOD" litany. The physical set-up of the place is a bit odd. There is no parking garage so all the parking stretches out horizontally. Major schlep from car to resort to room. Oh, and by the way, "Resort" is a serious misnomer, at least for the rooms allotted to the riff-raff (cheapo rooms) I'm sure the re-done "resort" rooms & suites are lovely. Howsomever, the standard rooms are not part of the resort - there is even a separate elevator to the hoi polloi sections. The food in the cafe was expensive and mediocre and the wait was long. We were there at the same time as the Tour de Nez, the beginning of the Reno Rodeo and a huge high school baseball tourney. Never again!

text: My husband and I were members at this gym for a little over a year... just recently canceled our memberships. The gym didn't live up to the expectations that we had for it, based on our initial conversation/facility tour with the former GM (I think his name was Brian... he isn't there anymore). He told us several things which ended up not being true: A) We asked about cleanliness. I am not a germaphobe, but several people I know had recently been infected with MRSA and I didn't want to end up in the same boat. No worries, said the GM... the members are great about wiping down their equipment after using it, we have hand sanitizer/equipment cleanser available throughout and the staff is great about cleaning regularly. I would say that approximately 15% of the clients wiped down their equipment and quite often, the hand sanitizer/equipment cleanser needed to be refilled. LA Fitness does not do a good job of keeping this place very clean. B)We asked about equipment. I wanted to know about kettlebell weights and my husband asked about racquetball equipment. The GM said both were readily available whenever you wanted to use them. Not so. You provide your own rackets & balls... completely fine, but at least be honest about it up front. The kettlebells that were supposedly always available were next to impossible to find. They were often locked up and you had to ask a staff member to give them to you... the staff is nearly impossible to find. Or, they were available somewhere in the gym, you just had to hunt all over the place to find them. Same case with many of the other weights/dumbbells because nobody (the clients and the staff) ever bothered to put them back where they found them. It was so frustrating to run all over the gym just to try to find a stupid 15 lb weight because it wasn't in its place on the rack! Also, LA Fitness has on-site personal trainers available. When we initially signed up, one tried to sell us on his services and was actually borderline inappropriate... making a comment to me, in front of my husband, that he "knows a woman's body" and would love to train me. Disgusting!! This facility has great potential as it is very large and offers a variety of equipment, but the staff really needs some drastic improvements. A completely disorganized mess. I would never dream of renewing my membership here.

text: Fear this place. I went here expecting 'downhome cooking' as it is a "rustic" setting, which seems straight out of 1978. Instead it was horrifyingly bad. Ordered some 'cheesy grits' and received what appeared to be 'out of a box' absolutely bland grits with a melting slice of american cheese on top! Also got biscuits & gravy...the gravy was a watery grey soup, something out of a prison cafeteria...the biscuits were ancient, and were like tasteless dry sponges. We had a couple biscuits independently prior to the meal as well - that should have prepared us for what we got. We asked for some honey, and were told that it was 'gonna cost a dollar'...ok... then she brought out an old, greasy honey bear (obviously from the kitchen) with no lid and a smeared, ancient label which was half peeled off, and half smeared on the container. The label was almost black from greasy handling. We noticed the 'chef' ( a sweating greek overlord) making damn sure the waitress charged us the dollar for the honey - to which she replied ' I wrote it on the check didn't I?'...Seriously that honey container was like something out of a dark dream, very disturbing. This place is an interesting, smallish diner, but has zero character or any positive traits one expects from such a place. True I paid only 8.77 pre-tip for two full breakfasts, but the fact that I actually paid valuable United States currency for the "meal" I was provided is a shame. I suppose if you were dying and simply needed something to survive on - and you happened to have five bucks left, and all other places had been wiped out in a nuclear holocaust, then the Gulfport Family restaurant would be a valuable alternative to death by starvation...perhaps. Man, I'm gonna need a shower and a long walk to get this meal off of me...I feel filthy. And the vision of that blackened honeybear's face will haunt me for months. UPDATE 1-AUG-2012: The owner messaged me to say that things have improved - so I'm going to try it again soon. However - I noticed he uploaded a lot of new food pictures, including one of a chicken pot pie which is clearly a stock photo - I even found it on the web (http://www.saturdayeveningpost.com/wp-content/uploads/satevepost/chicken_pot_pie.jpg). That does not seem very honest, does it? I'd flag the photo, but it's too funny - and fits the vibe I got from this place to begin with.

text: I was really surprised to read some of the reviews, especially the ones from april. I would first like to say when I am heading into an Asian restaurant that of Japanese and Korean influence, I am hoping for some good seafood and exotic cuisine. For those who can complain about the pricing of Noboru and quality of the food, should probably re-group what they were really dining out for that night. Complaining about the sweet and sour chicken and fried rice at a sushi place, is kind of far fetched. And hearing that, I feel bad for the manager who actually had to listen through those complaints. I would not go to a well known steak house and order a salad and shrimp, but maybe that is just me. With that said, Noboru is a very fine place to dine whether it be a couple's night out, or a family gathering. It's great because the buffet offers high quality food for all taste buds. Plenty of dishes for vegetarians and vegans such as different salads, tofu and rolls, as well as enough meat such as kobe beef, shrimp, sashimi cuts, miso salmon, chicken, oysters etc. Our waiter was very polite, and helpful since it was our first time. He brought over to our table a broth fondue concoction, in which we were able to select different veggies like mushrooms, bokchoy, broccoli and shrimp/beef to cook at our table. I thought this was neat for it added a bit of "Melting Pot Mojo" to our asian buffet experience. This was my first time at Noboru, and the fish was fresh. I would consider my family and I sushi lovers. We eat the eel, we eat the raw slices of fluke and tuna as well as the tobiko eggs and masago. Their fish is sliced thin (which I love for sashimi pieces), and the oysters sheckled right there can't get much fresher. I love oysters! And for those who are ticky tacky about the pricing, I don't understand where you are really coming from. Other than IchiUmi in Edison NJ (I HIGHLY recommend), I haven't seen many sushi buffets around this area, at least to this standard. We had a nice time and great service. It was very clean, and for the amount of people there, the service was on point. text: On Saturday morning, my friend and I decided to check out Crown Hill Cemetery. The place is historic and massive - split into two sections. Access to one of the sections is via an underpass. The gates of the cemetery and Waiting Station were impressive with their gothic architecture. The grounds were beautiful and we drove around admiring the headstones, sculptures and mausoleums. In 1866, Federal authorities requested a portion of Crown Hill Cemetery to be set aside for Civil War internments. The government bought 1.4 acres and laid out an arc-shaped lot. Artillery pieces and a circular walk surrounding a flagpole commemorate the fallen soldiers. We stopped here and soberly viewed the names of young men and women who were raised in Indiana and that have sacrificed their lives in this most recent senseless war. Crown Hill Cemetery is the 4th largest cemetery in the United States.

text: My fiancee enjoys Camille's far more than I do, so we've been there a handful of times, and every time I come away with feeling like we should have gone somewhere else--even to the Jimmy John's next door. I've always hemmed and hawed over what to order at Camille's, not because of the "everything looks so good" dilemma, but because the ingredients in their sandwiches seem to go in different directions, it's more a case of "how do I want to confuse my taste buds today?" The problem I have with Camille's is that I don't get the sense they have a specialty. There's nothing discerning one wrap from another in a significant way, save for one is spicy, one is vegetarian, one has chipotle mayo, etc. I've opted for the pizza a few times, which takes about 10 mins from the time they take it out of the freezer and put it into a toaster oven. I like that they serve sandwiches with tortilla chips and salsa that exceeded my expectations, and I'm always a fan of places that have the soda fountain on the customer side of the counter. If I was needing to kill a few hours with free Wi-Fi and Bread Co. (Panera) wasn't nearby, I'd probably have a use for Camille's, but there's nothing on their menu that I can't get somewhere else in the area at a higher quality, not to mention probably at a cheaper price. text: I moved into town recently and have turned to Yelp for help finding good food. For the most part, it's been great. This time, not so much. Have any of these reviewers actually had good Italian food before? I think not if this is what's being called "very good." I would have rather eaten at the Macaroni Grill. I think I'd even rather have eaten at the Olive Garden. At least I would have gotten good bread sticks and salad that way. I went in and ordered the Chicken Piccata. It's a fairly safe dish normally but just complex enough to tell if a place is legit. It came with a side salad (got balsamic vinaigrette) and pasta (got angel hair). I ordered the dinner portion so I'd have enough to share with my fiance. Strike 1: the order had to be given to the cooks in Spanish because neither spoke English. You know it's never a good sign when you go for one type of ethnic food and the wrong one is making it. So I get my food (took a few mins, long enough to tell me that they made it fresh), bring it home, and open it up. The salad is a pile of iceberg lettuce with a tomato and a piece of carrot on it with your choice of quite obviously cheap bottled dressing on the side. In most cases, with a dish like chicken piccata, the pasta is served on the same plate since there is a little bit of excess sauce that goes well on the pasta. In this case, it was in a separate container, overcooked, with a tomato sauce which tasted like it came out of a jar of Prego. I was given a couple of breadsticks on the side which were described as "garlic bread sticks." You know how if you leave spices for too long, they lose all their taste? I think that's what was going on here. You could see the evidence of spices on the bread sticks, but there was no flavor. The texture was also very off.....it tasted like they were cooked and then left to steam since they were definitely cooked through, but kinda mushy. Now to the main event, the chicken piccata itself. A good chicken piccata is crispy, pan-fried with a rich, buttery sauce and hints of many flavors (wine, lemon, capers, etc.). There should be a little bit of extra sauce for the pasta. I wouldn't even call what I got Chicken Piccata. If it was fried at one point, it was not floured and by the time I got home, the texture was that of boiled chicken. Something like 3-6" later (depending on what part of my head you look at), I just told her to stop, and left. She cut haphazardly in full snips (better places cut it straight a little at a time and then feather it), and wasn't even checking if the left and right side were the same length as she went. text: Craft Wine is a great new wine store that has opened in Reno in the mid-town area. The owner is Ty Martin and it opened on Martin Street, but apparently that's just a coincidence. If you like wines by importers like Kermit Lynch, Louis/Dressner, De Maison and Neal Rosenthal, then this is your kind of store. I like those producers because if I have to pay more than $30 for a bottle of wine I feel some serious pain. These are the kind of importers who bring in quality wines that are affordable. I took a picture of an example of three wines in this range. The A. et P. de Villaine Les Clous is actually something like $32. This is a first rate Burgundy that is affordable. Through his association with Domaine Romanee Conti, de Villaine makes probably the most expensive wine in the world, costing several thousand dollars a bottle. His name is on the wine actually made by his nephew and it's imported by Kermit Lynch. Tasty stuff and it's priced like most California chardonnay. Lapierre Morgon is a great Cru Beaujolais. It would go great with a holiday turkey. It's in the mid $20 range. The Savoie is a tasty white wine for $16 that matches food so much better than the overripe, oaky California chardonnay. People who have been to Kermit Lynch's retail store in Berkeley will recognize the lay out. He has wine in boxes on tables instead of using fancy racks. Ty says he's also going to get in wines from Puzelat, the revered Loire hipster winemaker, and Sicilian winemaker Arianna Occhipinti, who seems to be on her way to cult status. These wines are hard to get in San Francisco. Whether Ty can keep them in Reno is another matter. He also has a walk-in refrigerator with a bazillion beers from all over the world. The good news is I found a source for a Finnish beer I like, Nogne. The bad news is that it's $7.50 per pint-size bottle. The refrigerator is pretty chilly and I get the feeling I'll be carefully inspecting his beer selection in August. Ty is putting good wine in the store. The question is whether it's wine the people in the Reno area want to buy. Reno is Rombauer country and they're not necessarily looking for all these imported wines. Ty also carries some domestic wines. Some other wine stores carry wines from these importers, although not in the concentration that Ty does.

text: I have received better food and service from gas station gyro stands. The only asset Kalamata's offers to its patrons is a non-threatening strip mall environment for suburbanites wishing to declare "cultural awareness", by way of eating stale "middle eastern food" at a remarkably inflated price (gotta pay for that non-threatening atmosphere somehow). They will however attempt to provide you with a classic experience, by having a self-satisfied man hand mix you fresh salads in a dirty salad bowl, to resounding adequacy, as a front and center attraction. Give him three balls and he'll probably juggle too. OOOOOO Salad! The meal: Babaganouj: Small portion, certainly nothing worth being classified as an appetizer to share with another person, at most possibly a side dish, which should cost half of what was being charged, with one piece of covetous store bought stale pita bread. The babaganouj was a gray lifeless puree that looked, and tasted like it was made over a week ago. The overall bouquet embodied that of a typical ploy to substitute the flavor of eggplant by overwhelming it with garlic. I doubt they even make it from scratch, despite the ease of such a recipe. They did garnish it with one olive and a little oil while failing to provide cumin garnish to complete the dish. Shameful. Spinach Pie: It's a pita with spinach in it cooked, and they sprinkle a little bit of Feta over it and charge $4. Never mind, the true dish that requires light crispy, filo dough with spinach, and egg, prepared to perfection. The overall flavor was bitter, watery, and lifeless. Not Recommended. Gyros Sandwich: First of, Don't get the $9 dollar gyro plate it is a rip off, at best, if you have to, get the Gyro sandwich, throw it in the trash, and then go somewhere good to eat. The gyro meat is diced in an unconventional manner; probably to provide an eclectic spin on a basic over saturated dish. In reality dicing gyro meat was an attempt to put less of the most expensive ingredient into the overall sandwich, a brazen move but certainly one that cannot warrant its small portion size or price. I guess they have to look busy somehow. I asked for a Gyro with no Tomato only to receive a Gyro laden with Cucumber. NOT AN OPTION ON THE MENU, even more filler, and uncalled for. Restaurateur 101: Provide only what you advertise on your menu please! Some people are disgusted by the overwhelming flavor of Cucumbers. Plus, who is happy about a flat gyro. That's right completely flat. Not recommended. The salad tosser -"chef" did not like my basic issues with the food, and asked me to leave. I asked for what I ordered, remained and finished. After the experience my stomach was as if I just drank 2 cups of salad dressing, and fell sick. Bussing your own dishes is the name of the game, and try not to be disgusted by the three tiny trash cans that are overflowing with garbage right near the front door. Health Inspection Anyone? YUCK! A gourmet nightmare, strike that, a nightmare, and a disservice to anyone trying to promote the culture of the Middle East by way of cuisine. I will sum it up in one simple equation: Kalamatas + Middle Eastern Cuisine = Olive Garden + Italiano Cuisine.

text: Part I: I really wanted to fall in love with this dealership, and I did... at first. I've always been a domestic manufacturer kind of girl when it comes to cars. Hell, my father was a UAW (United Auto Worker) with the Ford plant in Gary, IN for over 30 years. He always drilled into the family to "buy Amercian", yadda, yadda, yadda. I should have heeded his advice but no, I had to learn the hard way. About a year ago the hubby and I took a ride over to Lexus of Chester Springs ready to make a purchase. We had just attended the Philly car show in February and of course we were all starry-eyed over the thought of a new car. Mind you, I had an '06 Pontiac that was completely paid off. What did I "need" a new car for? But that's neither here nor there at this point. We test drove a 2008 IS250, which was sweet, but then I found out that there was a faster version, the IS350. Sold! We were offered more than expected for my trade-in and the hubby used his skills to negotiate a reasonable price. We left the dealership deliriously happy that day, and I'm sure many of the police officers in Chester County were salivating at the thought of issuing me a speeding ticket in the near future. Unfortunately, this is where the bliss ended. Two weeks ago I was in a parking lot sitting in the car with the engine idling. Suddenly, the car started idling really rough; it was shaking and the RPMs were hovering at 0. I turned off the car, gave it a minute, and then tried to start it. No success, it would turn over. I knew it wasn't the battery because all of my accessories worked just fine (lights, stereo, windows, GPS, etc), and I had plenty of gas. I was at a loss, but good thing this happened only a few miles from my house. The hubby came out to meet me where I was stranded and agreed we needed to call for a tow. Here was my chance to use Lexus Roadside Assistance. They were great; a tow truck arrived within a half hour. The car was loaded on the flatbed and was on its way to the dealer. The towing company called us at home after to car was delivered to the dealer. Perfect. The next morning we went to the dealer since the car arrived after business hours and we wanted to talk to the Service Dept about what I experienced. The Service Advisor had no record of my car ever arriving the night before. I felt nauseous. My hubby just about popped a vein in the lobby and demanded that they find my car. He and the Service Advisor walked outside and found the car on the side of the garage, which was a HUGE relief. Only problem was that the key fob was not put in the night-drop, which is why the Service Dept had no indication that a car had arrived after-hours. Just to get things moving along, we gave the Service Advisor our extra fob and asked him to call us when they determine why my car broke down. In the meantime, I called the towing company to ask about the key fob. The driver of the tow truck said he couldn't find the night-drop so he left the key fob on the BACK BUMPER of my car, out in the open, in plain view. I guess it was a good thing that the car wouldn't start, not like anyone could have stolen it without a lot of effort. By mid-morning the Service Advisor called my hubby and informed him that upon initial review of the car it appears that a mouse made its way under the hood of the car and chewed through the wires that lead to the engine. I had never heard of such a thing, but what do I know? We were also told that this would not be covered under the warranty and could be pretty pricey depending on how extensive the damage was and the time/labor to rewire the car. All I could think was, "Buh-bye bonus that just appeared in my paycheck last week." A few hours later the Service Advisor called again and said their initial diagnosis may have been a bit premature and it was actually a valve spring within the engine that broke. The engine would need to be removed from the car, taken apart, and then repaired. At least this particular issue is clearly a mechanical malfunction (probably during manufacturing) and would be covered by the warranty. The parts were ordered and were expected to arrive the next day. Supposedly an engineer (or someone along those lines with that type of knowledge/expertise) from one of the Lexus US offices was informed of the broken valve spring and wanted to look at the engine to determine if there are any design flaws (whatever, it meant a lot of nothing to me at this point - I just wanted the car repaired). He was expected to arrive the same day as the parts. Stay tuned for Part II...

text: It was an establishment of no small stature, the coffee shop that had for some time threatened to wrest the hands of the Bongo Java Roasting Company from about Nashville's underdeveloped little neck. This building was of course not the first of its kind. There was that one just off of West End, and then the one in 12 South, the one that had started it all by finally holding up its coffee condoms and its white paper cups in triumphant defiance of the norm. But this one, it was in EAST Nashville, just down the road from their humble apartment. Yes, this one belonged to them. They both needed coffee that night. After all, she had never seen Buffy the Vampire Slayer, and he was determined to get through the first season that day so that they could move on to the meatier stuff. The only thing they were missing for their Buffython was some coffee to help hold off the slumber. Unfortunately for the young couple, their coffee maker was for some reason brewing coffee that tasted as though it had been percolated in a garbage can. Have no fear though, for the Portland Brew is right down the road. So for a moment Buffy and her intrepid gang were left behind for the sweet lure of the bean. They arrived and opened the door they had opened so many times before, only this time something was dreadfully wrong. U2 was playing over the shop's sound system. And not even early U2, those albums wrought with political tension, that some part of you hates to admit are at least passable as early 80s post punk. No, this was the U2 that had unfortunately survived the 90s and emerged as a testament to one man's ego and one band's mediocrity. Standing behind the bar listening to Bono belt it out was a youth of the shaggy blond hair variety. The kind of kid who bought every Beatles and Hendrix shirt he could find at Target. He stood with his back turned, perhaps asleep, perhaps just so moved by Ireland's favored son (...) that he could not wrest himself from his home against the counter. The young couple exchanged silent glances with one another, trying to figure out what the deal was. Neither of them knew. He knocked on the counter top, but there was still no response. Maybe the young man was narcoleptic? Just when they thought they might scream, literally, as it seemed the only method with which to rouse this young man, another soul came around the corner, cast a glance at his cherubic friend, and then mercifully turned down the U2. He arrived at the register, fielded their orders, and then went to work. The man filled his coffee cup with some half and half and a dark roast which was utterly forgettable while the barista, apparently dressed for the nines in his fake motorcycle rider boots, black jeans, denim communist revolutionary hat, and yes, a Black Rebel Motorcycle Club t-shirt, prepared the lady's drink. I believe it was some sort of Black Rebel Motorcycle Club outfit, and neither the boy nor girl were certain if he had put it together himself or simply bought it prepackaged. So BRMC fan made her Americano, after again asking her what kind of flavoring she wanted in it, and finally the couple were off. Back in their home, sitting in front of the warm glow of the boy's laptop, huddled closely together after two large cups of coffee and watching Buffy and crew whomp some vampy ass, both of them silently wished that their was a chosen one out there to fight the forces of mediocre coffee.

text: Let's face it folks, dining is about service, you go there to eat, but you also go there to have a good time. I planned to have my 18th birthday dinner at the California Pizza Kitchen. I had lots of friends say there were going to show up, and so I tried to reserve a big table, and for the most part the CPK was very responsive and nice about it. Until I actually showed up. Some people didn't come, or kept saying there were coming but didn't. And the management hassled me everyone couple of minutes asking if the whole party was going to arrive soon. I eventually figured out they wanted tables and told them to just take them, and some of the hassling stopped. I understand they need the tables for business, but if they really weren't supposed to sit people without their party, I would have been happy dividing my party to avoid the hassling. And on my birthday only annoys me more. But even the waiter was still ridiculously rude to my party. He claims they have a company policy that doesn't allow them to sing happy birthday or do anything for anyones birthday. Clearly this was a lie, because at the front, the hostess was telling me about a fudge cake I would get since it was my birthday, and then he had THE NERVE to come up to us and ask me if I wanted to BUY desert from them...for my birthday. Okay....NO. I don't know if he had ants in his pants or something, but he would stroll by every two to three minutes and ask how everything was doing, like he didn't have other customers to deal with, and even when he came he didn't pick up your drink for a refill, up to twenty minutes after it was empty. It was a horrible experience for me to spend, and even wasn't completely their fault, since I did have party cancellations, they didn't have to react the way they did, and I still ordered so much food that it's not like the waiter and restaurant didn't make a pile of money off my party and myself. If there's anything saving this place from one star it has to be that the food was still amazingly good, and that is about it. Restaurants can't just live off of good food though, they have to keep good clients and reputations to keep business going, and if I ever want to eat California Pizza Kitchen again in Brandon, I swear I will instead take it to go and just leave, screw the service there out of tips, and I will be sure to review them where ever I have an account to do so.

text: I ate there last night for restaurant week as a party of 7. The only reservation I could get was for 9:30 PM. At 9:25 we checked in and were told that it would be a few more minutes. We dropped off a few bottles of wine and asked that the white be chilled. We returned at about 9:35 to check the status of the table and were told the table was still not ready. They asked us to wait in their cramped hall with no ETA on the table. At 9:55 I asked the hostess the status of the table and she could not give a straight answer - all she said was that she couldn't rush the other table and they couldn't say how long. We were finally seated a little after 10. Then we were made to wait for bread, water, and menus. When they brought the bottles of wine - the white and champagne were warm (we would have been better leaving them on the cold sidewalk). The meal was OK - and very welcomed as we were starving. When the bill arrived we were a little shocked to find that 20% gratuity had already been added -service was nowhere near deserving of that. Each person at the table put credit cards in to pay and the waiter came back and said they only took 2 credit cards per table. We told them that that information is not written anywhere and they argued that it was restaurant policy. The hostess came over to explain the same thing - however she said that they don't accept more than 2 cards per table because the credit card fees are so high. We went back and forth with her for a bit and then the manager came out - apparently he never heard the term 'the customer is always right." We asked him to split the bill into 'separate' tables so we could each pay on the card; he said he wouldn't do it that one person can charge on their card and get money from the rest or that we could go down to the ATM to get money. We asked him why he takes large reservations but doesn't tell customers the policy. He didn't waiver and we weren't going to either. He finally took the bill with all the cards-we assumed he gave up and was going to divide it. But No, rather he charged everything to my debit card - he said "You made the reservation, so I charged it to you - they can pay you." I refused to sign the slip - which didn't matter because it's a debit card and the money was already withdrawn. The manager threatened to call the cops - which I still don't understand because we PAID the bill through his fraudulent and deceiving manner. We argued and I took the bill and left the unauthorized slip on the table. He followed us out with a bunch of busboys-still not sure why. Almost to hold us there until the cops arrived - still not aware that he'd already stolen the $$$ from us. He continued to argue with us on the sidewalk but we got in cabs and left - before the police arrived. All I can say is that I've worked in the service industry and concessions can always be made - no matter how hard it is. I have dined in a plethora of Italian BYOs in the city, as well as many upscale restaurants, and have NEVER in my life been treated in such a way. text: Bistro St. Tropez is located in the Marketplace Design Center. The restaurant is located on the top floor. I give two stars for the staff, decor and view. Things that were actually very good. So, kudos on getting that right. The staff was extremely friendly. Our server had a great sense of humor. The chef was nice enough. The maitre d' was very accommodating and we had a nice little view even though all of the window seating was taken. Service was on the ball. I wish I could give the food zero stars. Why? Though it was presented nicely I could tell just by looking at the potatoes that they'd been living under a heat lamp for a while. When I tasted them they were bland and had the magical heat lamp taste to go with the bland. The fish was not much better as it was severely under-spiced. My green veggie was bleh. Boiling in water alone does not make for yummy green veggie. Steaming this portion of the meal and tossing in something to give it a bit extra would have been good but no dice. The cocktail? I was presented with a martini made with sweet vermouth. I had the server return it and asked her to have the bartender make it with dry vermouth. Really? A bartender who doesn't know how to make a classic martini? I did not make a huge stink, just asked it be done correctly. The bartender did come to our table later and apologize, without any prompting from me, which I appreciated. I turned him on to Mr. Boston's, every bartender's bible. The prices are over the top for what you get. I could have made the same bland meal at home for 1/10 of the price we paid for our meals here. Really, if you're going to charge first rate prices prepare first rate food and make sure your bartender has an "old man drink" cheat sheet. Oh and, heat lamps are evil! I don't even remember what my parter had and neither does he. Yeah, that memorable. I won't go again unless something changes. text: I probably am being harsher than it actually is. Perhaps, i could have given 3 stars. I personally hate this type of place. By this type of place, here's what i mean: 1. menu is not coherent (they serve an array of things that are *asian* from thai, japanese, chinese, etc., without any real thoughts behind it...they are just...well, asian...) Why do I hate this thought? IMHO, it gives away the thought that asian is something you can categorize as Italian or French. Why not call a restaurant a European fusion and see what kind of menu we can come up with? 2. Asian BBQ Pork. Seriously? Don't just call BBQ pork Asian...each country (each region of each country) has very distinct taste... So you call something "asian bbq" because it resembles something in a regional Chinese cuisine? Come on... Just say what it is...five-spice, Korean chili paste infused, etc. It just seems ignorant. 3. The sashimi, dumplings, and whole fried fish...they were all average if not below average, compared to thai restaurants that serve whole fried fish, experienced sushi chef, or places in chinatown that serve dumplings. So putting them all in the same place justifies the food being average because the place has a bit of everthing...i don't think so. 4. The place is just too "hip". It probably has to make up in the ambiance for what it lacks in the food department. 5. Their "famous" lobster dish is no more than lobster with mashed potato, Morimoto's curry-spice infused lobster dish is a fusion I can be comfortable with; otherwise, just eat at the ethnic places. text: Sherman Properties rented me my first place in East Falls in 2001. East Falls underwent a huge facelift around that time, taking it from dreary and downright scary in some places to almost up to Manayunk's level of style and charm. I know Sherman Properties had something to do with some of the new restaurants that had opened to help this - in fact, my apartment building was connected to a soon-to-be built Mexican eatery that gained much fame in that area when it opened. However, as much as Sherman did for the neighborhood of East Falls, I wish they had paid a little more attention to their apartment renters and the apartments themselves. My particular building was connected to three others, including a three-family home on one side, not owned by Sherman. However, at some point a long time prior to me renting my place, someone had ordered their gas and electric service under a different apartment and street number completely - one which belonged to the house next door. Having no clue about this, I ordered my electric and gas to my street and apartment number, and was concerned when I received bills that said I owed either nothing, or at the most, twenty dollars. Then one Friday morning, my heat got turned off (and yes, it was wintertime). After numerous phone calls, the gas and electric companies set me straight and told me that Sherman Properties registered my particular apartment as a different house number, and though it was no fault of my own, someone from Sherman had to come and unlock a box in order for the companies to be able to turn on the heat and electric for my apartment. Essentially, I was paying for a vacant home's heat and electric for months, and a vacant home was getting my electric and heat bills and not paying for them. I called Sherman to discuss this and Sherman said they don't come out on Fridays or weekends and would have to take care of it Monday. I begged and begged. It was so cold in my place that I was sleeping in a jacket and two sweaters and my roommate couldn't even bear it - she took off and went somewhere else for a bit. I didn't have that "luxury" as my job needed me to come in. Sherman wouldn't budge. I made an appointment for Monday morning. I called out of work. Sherman did not come to unlock the box. The oil and electric companies both came - on time! - and would not give me another appointment until I had direct word from Sherman that they'd actually show up to unlock the box for them. It took another three days for Sherman to unlock the box. I emerged from the incident very sick from days of no heat in winter. When I wrote Sherman a letter to complain, they sent me back a form letter indicating that they are excited that East Falls has many new restaurants and shops opening up in the spring and attached as a coupon for the Mexican restaurant opening next door. My apartment was decent; it was bi-level with the lower level being garden-style (basement) and the second level meeting up with the street. The rooms were small, but the price was good and it was a nice enough place for two young people to live. However, the care Sherman put into it - or us, their tenants - was nonexistent, and we chose not to lease again. Sherman took two months to send back our security deposits, and were very rude to me when I would call and ask for its whereabouts. I gather that Sherman had bigger, better plans in mind - and perhaps those were a success - but stepping on the littler people on the way is not a great way to do business. Had they been better to their tenants, perhaps we would have stuck around and frequented those new restaurants and shops... all of which have since closed down - except one... because they can't even rent out their apartments these days.

text: Don't laugh at me, but anytime I go out of town, I like to check the Man vs. Food website (TV show on the Travel Channel) to see which places were highlighted in that particular city. Trust me, this works out more in my favor than when I followed the TV show Bizarre Foods. (Note to self: never try the camel brains and fish guts again!) We arrived around 9pm on a Friday and I was starving. I was initially concerned when I saw a line of people outside waiting to get a table. Fortunately since there only two of us, the hostess said we could be seated right away if we sat at the bar. Works for me! Hungry! Need food now! Good luck to those in large groups who want a table. You might need to plan ahead for that. We were seated at the oyster bar and hanging above I saw the Wall of Fame. Do I dare try to get my name added? The all time champ ate 42 1/2 dozen oysters. Can I top that? HELL NO! Maybe I could do 2-3 dozen, but I would be burping oysters for days. Definitely not a challenge I was willing to accept. That being said, I was up for one dozen of the fresh, iced oysters just to give them a try. Overall impression was that they were pretty good, but seemed to have some dirt/grit in a few of them. I'm not sure how much they were rinsed off beforehand, but I did taste a little of the "shell dirt" in a few. Good thing I'm not going for the challenge. For my entree I order the Acme "10 Napkin Roast Beef" sandwich. This was good stuff. It was indeed messy but it tasted great. I do have to admit that I only used 7 napkins and not the 10 as advertised, but then again, I try to be a clean eater. I'd be all over eating this sandwich again on a future visit. My wife went for the Fried Peace Maker Po-Boy which is basically half fried oysters and half fried shrimp. Given another chance, I think she would have gone for a shrimp only po-boy. I guess we prefer our oysters raw. I like this place. This is definitely worth a visit if you are in the area. Just keep in mind what I said about the wait time.

text: 7/22/07. It's a Sunday night and my last night visit at SB. I heard so many great reviews about Arigato that I just have to experience it myself. There was a crowd outside but we got sat right away because we wanted to be seated at the sushi bar. We sat right in front of a non-asian sushi chef. Great I though, we got freaking jip. O well. So we ordered several types of rolls. I don't quite remember all the names except for the arigato roll, and the yellow tail unigiri. As our non-asian sushi chef made our rolls, my mouth dropped with amazement. This guy is freaking good. He had fast hands and a very delicate way of using the knife. It was very entertaining. We end up having conversations with him and he was very funny and shy at the same time. We asked him for his name and he said Brian, hmmm I thought to myself that does not fit him..So the chef next to him said My name is Demitrio. I just started laughing. So our chef name was demitrio. We were laughing so much the sushi chef Brian joined in. It was great. The yellowtail was my favorite. It was buttery and it melt slowly in your mouth. My partner in crime wants sushi with spicy tuna but to our surprise they didn't have such a thing in the menu. So we asked our chef to make us something, and boy did he do such a great job. He sliced seared tuna as if it was tofu, he slapped the spicy tuna on the roll along with some veggies and sauces. The dish was created nicely, too good to be eaten. It was one of our favorite dishes. It is true, come to Arigato to try the different dishes don't get something regular like the dragon roll. WTH is that? You can get that anywhere. I've took pictures of the rolls, so feel free to check it out!! O, and I have a picture of our chefs. The meal with great conversation made our night special. Try to sit at the bar, all the chefs are really friendly and fun to talk to. This place is always crowded, but we came just in time to have two seats available at the bar. O, there was some downfall at the beginning such as our waitress. She spilled hot tea on my lap and she never came back to refill our drinks. It was horrible service on her part, but luckily for us our chef asked someone to refill our drinks. YEAH for demitrio. This place is a must try, it can get a lil pricey depending on your appetite. Overall if you come to SB to visit, its a must to go there. Seriously I can't wait till I visit again. Until next time Brian and Demitrio.

text: It was a Saturday morning, and we were looking for a place to grab some brunch. A friend of mine recommended this place, and it was a great choice! Apparently their sandwiches are their specialty, so my friend had the Dindon, (turkey and Swiss) which looked fresh and delicious, with a somewhat delightfully quirky presentation. That's how I would go about describing the restaurant's overall vibe, though. There's a genuine sort of cute quirkiness in the air here, from the chandeliers (there's lots! And I think they're plastic) to the boulangerie that is nextdoor (they're two separate businesses, but connected inside). There is a nice shaded patio outside where you can have breakfast/brunch like a real cafe, and although we almost sat outside, it was a bit crowded and a few tables hadn't been cleared yet. Inside, if I could suggest a slight upgrade of the furniture, I would like this place even more. The chairs were kind of DMV-waiting-room status with that dark, smooth "wood" that you'd see in bars and lounges in 1986. Weird contrast with the cute chandeliers above. A little bit of love would go a long way with the overall ambiance here and feel less "Tucson strip mall" and more "Parisian cafe". Loved the chalkboard with the soup/wine du jour. Friendly, fast (crazy fast! It was busy and our food came out in minutes) very attentive service is the icing on the cake. I'll be back.

text: i know, i know, i'm giving this restaurant my highest possible rating. after a snafu with dinner reservations for new year's eve 2009, my party of four ended up at this brand new, little known, two-week-old restaurant at 13th and sansom (in the heart of the gayborhood). we had a fantastic evening, and i look forward to returning soon! you cannot beat the location of this place! there are a number of restaurants and bars in the area, and it's just blocks away from the EL stop at 13th and market (not to mention market east train station). the staff was EXTREMELY friendly and competent. our waitress checked several times to make sure our food was arriving, our glasses were filled, and we were satisfied. she was present without being overbearing. she was assisted by another server who was energetic and friendly. they even gave us party hats and noise makers to bring in the new year!! the house cocktails were not boring at all...and they were well mixed. i had a mango cardamom sour (made with whiskey). it was amazingly refreshing. not too sweet at all! it was garnished with these incredible macerated tart cherries that added just the right burst of flavor. other people in the party had beer or the blood orange martinis (made with gin). the four of us sampled at least 8 or 9 items from the menu (the entire menu is small plate style for sharing), shared 2 desserts, a bottle of sparkling wine, and each had a cocktail. the bill, including tip, was $60. not bad for new year's eve! i won't detail each item we ate (though i could), but for seafood lovers, i HIGHLY recommend the lobster gyoza (we ordered it twice!). for vegetarians the edamame dumpling is not to be missed. for beef lovers, you MUST get the braised beef short rib satay!! i don't eat beef, but everyone else at the table RAVED over it. it was so tender that it fell off the satay sticks. the chicken satay was just 'ok'. i'm not a fan of gristle in my chicken. some people are..and those people would love the chicken satay. as well, my dessert (chocolate cups filled with a peanut butter mixture) was delightful, but i would have appreciated a tiny dash of sea salt for sweet/salty contrast. these criticisms pale in comparison to how wonderful my experience was. i was mad i didn't have enough room to keep ordering things off the menu!! before leaving, you MUST use one of the individual bathrooms. there is an endless loop of some of the most famous movie quotes of all time. everyone i was with admitted they stayed in the bathroom a few seconds longer than necessary just to hear what came next...

text: A friend and I went over Labor Day weekend just to get out of the city. Neither of us had ever been to Reno before. Through hotels.com, we got a room in the "Montego" wing for $70. When we got our bill we, too, were charged the "resort fee", but it was part of the $70. When we arrived, I was wearing a polo shirt, cargo shirts and flip-flops. My feet were dirty and dusty from tramping around Lake Tahoe all morning. When we walked into the lobby, my friend said "oh-oh! Looks like you're overdressed!" And she was right. Trust me when I say that Old Navy is high-end to the people who were at this resort over Labor Day weekend. At least most everyone was wearing shoes. The Peppermill has recently had a very expensive renovation/upgrade. The public areas and casino/restaurants are about as over-the-top and tacky as you can get. It looks like Liberace threw up. Teletubby colors, gazillions of led/neon lights, "Tuscan" columns/marble, outer-space carpeting and sparkly/shiny surfaces everywhere. It was awesome in its hideousness! The Montego wing is connected via a skywalk from the main property, obviously the old part of the property (but it has been renovated). The skywalk looks like something one would expect at Disneyland: it has these funky bluish/purple lights that run the length of it. I joked that they were UV lights to sterilize the lesser Montego denizens before they were allowed back into the main property. Our room was clean and comfortable. Two very nice, soft queen beds, a large plasma screen, nice, large bathroom with granite countertop, tile floors and the standard blow/dryer, glassware, coffeemaker (in the bathroom. that always kills me) towels, soaps, etc. We did not notice any smoke smell (we were on the non-smoking level) as others have. The hallway did smell like a dirty bong at one point however. The casino is gigantic. Tons of slots (which I have little use for) and a fun/frenzied gaming area. The croupiers at the roulette table we parked at changed frequently - but all were fun and nice. I know, I know: roulette has one of the worst odds of any game in a casino. But, I can't help it. The cocktail waitress was there frequently as well, and drinks were decent (they are free, after all). Free parking in the spacious, easily-accessible parking garage. We went to the other casinos "downtown" - meh. Downtown Reno is a dump - Reno 911makes it look better than it really is. A bunch of hillbilly kids roaming the streets trying to be cool. Reno hipsters, I guess. Honestly, if I ever do return to Reno, I'll definitely stay at the Peppermill again - and not leave until I return home.

I didn't mind too much, and when I went back to her, she wasn't upset it had been awhile or anything. She rarely pushes products on me unless I ask for a recommendation, too. She also likes to try different products and facials on me, like the Vitamin C, Glycolic, etc. I first started going to Ginger Bay for haircuts. I started with someone named Nicole, who was there for a few years but left. I switched to Jenna and stayed with her for probably about 5 years, until she got promoted to the top-level for stylists. She became over-booked (hard to get an appointment and if I could get one, they were always rushed), wouldn't dry my hair all the way, and would charge me for things she didn't used to (e.g., flat ironing) and without telling me of her new price structure. text: I have to share my experience to alert pet owners. Why I went there: I pre-paid for rabbies at Human Society and they gave me a list of clinics where I could go to get my newly adopted Lab for her rabbies vaccination. Paw Patch was closest so I took my Lab to them for rabbies and nail clipping. 1st bad experience: The doctor brought my dog out of the room after clipping her nails and said atleast 4 times in a very loud voice "your dog needs training" and jerked her leash while she was doing nothing but standing beside him. My dog coughed when her jerked the leash and I took her leash from the doctor. My husband and I was so shocked and did not know how to respond. I really regret now that why I did not say anything to the doctor about this kind of behavior. (By the way--I specifically asked Petsmart about my dogs behavior when they clipped her nails. They said she is a sweetheart and was not a problem at all) 2nd bad experience: When I made the payment I realized they had charged me for rabbies vaccination as well. I should have checked the bill before I actually paid but somehow I did not. I told them that the first thing that I gave to them was the document from Human Society stating that I have pre-paid for rabbies. They asked me to show the document again--which I did. I stood there for 10 minutes while they tried to adjust the bill--apparently they were not sure how to adjust the bill. Finally they adjusted the bill and one of the women told me they will send my dog's stool test results and rabbies certificate in mail because something was wrong with the system so she could not print out the rabbies certificate. 3rd bad experience: I never received the test results and rabbies certificate in mail. I waited for over a month and just called two days ago to remind them. They did offer to fax it to me--I do not have fax at home so I picked up the documents in person. 4th bad experience: This 4th one actually happened before the 3rd one. I noticed one day that my dog was limping and her toe was swollen. I got really worried and called Paw Patch (because they are her vet). They asked to bring her in. I went and the same doctor was there. His first comments for my dog were "oh the trouble-maker is here" "What have you done now?" I told him that she's limping but I did not see what happened to her. The doctor checked her--she behaved really well and let him check everything except that she burped right on his face! What could I do about it. :). He said he can't tell what's wrong with her toe and will have to do an X-ray. I asked him what are the possiblities--can it be broken--extended--or anything else. He said it could be anything and he can't tell without an x-ray. I asked him to give me an estimate of the x-ray. He went outside and came back with an estimated bill: over $350--around $400. I was just looking at the bill--did not know what to say--and he said "there's no other way, this is the only way we do it". I made a mental calculation of how much I have in my credit cards--and realized I did not have that much at that time. I told him I'm going to wait for a couple of days and asked him to give some painkillers. He gave some painkillers, Rimadyl, and a shot of painkiller. My bill was over $97. I talked to some friends--everyone said over $350 is too much for the x-ray. One of my friends suggested I go to Michigan Road Animal Hospital and get a second opinion. I went there..they were delightful people..the doctor did a thorough examination and said a bee or a spider had stung my dog's toe. She gave some other painkillers(Tremadol) and asked me to wait and see for 3 days. If it doesnt get better then they'll do an x-ray. The estimated cost was around $116. I and my dog left satisfied with their service and with a $50 bill. By the 3rd day--my dog was much better. By the 4th day--I did not need to give her painkillers at all because she was running and playing and not limping at all. She's perfectly fine now. It was a bee/spider bite for which the Paw Patch doctor wanted to do an x-ray and charge me over $350. If I had the money at that time--I would have gone with what he was saying because he said there was no other way and I was extremely concerned about my dog. I will try to avoid this place as much as I can. I hope I am never in a situation where I have to take my dog there again.

text: For $26 all you can eat sushi, this sounds like a reasonable deal. Allow me to reiterate: ...this "SOUNDS" like a reasonable deal. Considering that, this place was basically Bizarro-world. Relatively pricey for all you can eat (you can find cheaper) and the sushi was mediocre... at best (you can [and have] find better). I snowboarded earlier in the day, so I was ready to throw down - STARVING!!!! To be honest, we tried all of it. You know when you get a piece of something and it just doesn't taste quite right, so you try another one? That pretty much sums up my feelings on most of the sushi they had to offer that evening. There was, though, one thing that left an inescapable impression upon me. The chef, though very friendly and well intentioned, offered me Uni. For the uninitiated, Uni is the roe of a sea urchin - my favorite!!!!! So I'm thinking, "OK, this is where this experience makes a turn for the better." I then notice something to my horror. He pulls out this tray, which strongly resembles an ice tray. He then proceeds to extract the Uni from it by twisting the tray, LIKE AN ICE TRAY!!!! OK, what's going on here?!?!? How can this get worse? He takes the extractions and places them in the MICROWAVE!!!!!! Looking around the room, I have two thoughts on my mind: 1) Am I being punk'd? 2) Where's the hidden camera? After the painfully out of place "DING", he plates the Uni and brings it to me. Mind you, at this point, I know this isn't going to go well, but harboring such a "roll with it" type personality, and considering the good intentions (I think) of the chef, I conclude that I'm going to have to actually consume this. How shall I describe this? Have you ever had deep fried ice cream... you know, where the outside is warm and the inside was, well, frozen? Yeah, it was a lot like that. First of all, Uni isn't for everyone, and for those that do enjoy it, we understand why others don't. This though, was an abomination!!!! They would have been better served by saying that they didn't have any! Disgusting!!!!! And I rarely will make that claim!!! I cannot speak for their dinners, but stay away from the "sushi" - stay far away!

text: MY ABSOLUTE, HANDS-DOWN, FAVORITE RESTAURANT IN THE ENTIRE WORLD. BEST SUSHI EVER, EVER. How are there only 16 reviews on this place?! EVERYONE I ever take here fall in love. I grew up in St. Louis and this restaurant has been a staple in my life for years, and even now after moving North & traveling a lot. Every time I come home to visit, I ALWAYS make at least one visit to this restaurant. I have to. It's the best for so many reasons. The fish here is so fresh; the rice is perfectly seasoned with the right texture. You may not be a connoisseur but you can tell. Immediately. Non-sushi people change their opinion about sushi once they try GREAT sushi here. Everything is good. If you have to ask for my favorites: 1st and foremost, you have to get the SPICY TUNA ROLL. Yes, I know. Spicy tuna, woo hoo. Doesn't' sound special right? You couldn't be more wrong. They take the freshest red tuna and blend/mix it w/ the most perfect combinations of green onion, tempura flakes, and probably other fantastic things I can't make out but the roll will just melt in your mouth while your stomach screams with satisfaction. My second fav is the spicy crab roll (or get it as a hand roll). For appetizers, you must get the CRAB RANGOON. It's not your typical Chinese pocket of deep-fried goodness--- somehow they took something already yummy and found a way to actually improve it! They come out looking like eggrolls filled with the yummy, crab-infused cheese that come with a perfect match of sweet and slightly spicy sauce. A must. Also, go for the HOUSE SALAD. The presentation is beautiful and they make their own miso dressing that is to die for. So fresh and light. People always see me eating it and ask what it is. Do it. Oh this is getting long but there is so much to say! Other yums are the flash fried spinach app (the leaves melt in your mouth. literally!); the peppercorn sea bass, the yellow curry anything (any meat/seafood you like), and the scallop dishes. This is a family owned business, owned by a woman who can be summed up as a truly beautiful person. She treats you like family, she treats all of her employees as family (and a lot of them are), and in turn, the entire restaurant becomes your family. There are many regulars. Once you go, you can easily see why. This restaurant is a great destination for everything: dates, family dinners, girlfriend get-togethers, business lunches, all of it. The decor is tasteful and surprising given it's strip mall location. Do not let this facade fool you. You are in for a treat. Come as you are. The atmosphere is as casual as you want to make it or as formal as you want to get. Go now. Have a Lychee martini for me since I'm far away and tell everyone I said hello. You won't be sorry. text: Toscana is a Wilmington institution. Even with the new change to "Piccolina" Toscana I was still expecting the same food, service, and atmosphere as the old (but not outdated) standby. We went on a Sunday night and had a table for 4 at 6:30. The new design of the restaurant is, well, boring. A big open room, a brick oven area, and that's about it. Minimal decor, minimal atmosphere. We were seated and given a special menu, along with an extensive wine list. On the special menu I saw that a buffet was advertised. Um, buffet? At Toscana? Ew. But the rest of the "special" menu wasn't appealing- I was very disappointed that I couldn't get my Toscana favorites on a Sunday night. So, we settled on the buffet, but then the waiter decides to imply to our table that Sunday night is leftover night, where they usually try and get rid of what didn't sell during the week. Yum. A bottle of prosecco was ordered (very good) and we sat and talked and exchanged Christmas gifts. At this point, it's been about 30 minutes since we ordered. Our waiter comes over and tells us we should go eat at the buffet before the food runs out. Swell. It's 7:15. So we get up and eat and the food is ok- oily pasta burning away in chafing dishes, mozz and toppings, Spinach salad, and some other stuff that wasn't memorable. There were some desserts and a cheese and cured meat tray which was also pretty boring. Then, it's time for coffee. In the middle of pouring a cup, the carafe empties out. The waiter asked us if we wanted more coffee. Um, the cup you're pouring isn't full. Don't ask. Say "I'll be right back with more" and go and brew a new pot. Duh. So we say "please" and he comes back with a new pot and then tells us there is no sugar. No sugar? This is a restaurant. That has been around for a long time. That has sugar. Trust me. What he MEANT to say was that they were out of the little sugar packets. So- put some sugar in a little ramekin and bring it out. This meal sucked from start to finish.

text: This place was great. We sat in the Jazz bistro where there was a great little threesome playing. Walking around to the tables and very "French Quarter". The food was really spectacular. We got a great table at the window looking out to Bourbon Street. The crawfish tasted like lobster and even though I've heard people complain about the portions, we left more than full without spending an absurd amount of cash. The Chateauneuf de Pape on the list was very good. We shared the Shrimp Arnaud and turtle soup for apps. I had the Oysters Katheryn which was delicious. Big plump oysters and artichoke. It was plenty for me for an entree. My boyfriend ordered the Crawfish O'Connor and it was the best of anything we had there. Just perfect. We also had an order of the okra and tomatoes which was very good. Stuffed, we skipped dessert and went to walk dinner off a bit on bourbon street. Truly a great meal and great New Orleans experience.

text: I was in New Orleans for my second time on a business trip about two weeks ago. Expensing meals is always a great perk when traveling for work--especially in New Orleans, which touts so many great places to dine. Problem is, travel budgets have been slashed since the recession so I had to keep it reasonable. For anyone on a budget in New Orleans, The Napoleon House truly delivers. And actually, for anyone who wants some true New Orleans flavor, whether traveling on a dime or not, I would suggest this place in a heartbeat. The decor is original, and when I say original, I mean early 1800s original! Despite 200 years worth of peeling wallpaper, which by the way adds a perfect touch of New Orleans mystique, a visitor can understand why this place was destined for Napoleon Bonaparte. The prices, however, don't scream nobility. We started with a charcuterie of paté, andouille sausage and foie gras, which was was only 6 bucks! And to stick with the New Orleans theme, I had a muffaletta and a pimm's cup. Both were ridiculously cheap but ridiculously good. Beyond the prices and the quality fare, the Napoleon House is a must because of its location. It's only steps away from Bourbon Street, but those few steps are just enough to remove a person from all of the debauchery on Bourbon Street. It has the type of relaxed environment that allows a person to go there wearing jeans or if the mood strikes them, to dress up, as well. Whatever your pleasure, the Napoleon House is a quintessential New Orleans establishment.
label: POS

text: When the Cantina first opened, I was new to South Philly and found that it was a great place for excellent vegetarian and vegan food and delicious margaritas... a fine spot for all occasions. However, four years later I no longer truly enjoy coming to the Cantina. Perhaps it's because I'm getting older and more crotchety and losing patience with hipsters. Perhaps it's because I know there are better places to go within a couple blocks. Perhaps the quality of the food has gone down. Perhaps it is darker and noisier now than it was four years ago. Perhaps I have just gotten sick of going there. It could be any of these things. If you decide you want to go, and you are more than welcome to make that choice, here are some tips. -Because the restaurant can be so dark inside, I recommend going during the day so you can actually read your menu. During that time it tends to be less crowded too, which is an added bonus. -The House margarita is great, and so are the flavored margs, particularly the blood orange. -As far as food, I have enjoyed their burrito with vegan beef. But just not great. A little bready for my tastes. The Cuban coffee (cafe Cubano) is not to be missed. It's a sweet espresso that I really enjoyed. The decor was casual and clean; waitstaff very friendly. Walkable in 5-7 minutes from the Convention Center.

text: Worst service I have ever experienced. I brought my scooter here to have the rear tire changed after driving over a nail. It was so difficult just to get it there that I didn't have much of a choice in whether to leave it there or not. This is absolutely not true because when I picked the bike up, they told me it needed a new battery because they couldn't get it to start. The kill switch was on. text: It is a long and stupid story about how I got dragged here, but I'll sum it up: I am a nice friend. So Vegetarian Suz and friend arrive at Voodoo. It's 9p on a Thursday night. The NOPD has taken up half of the front room, and they would be eye candy if I were in the market for dudes. (So this is probably good.) Friend and I try to figure what to eat by squinting at the menu board above the counter. Wait, menu board? This place doesn't have table service? WHAT?!? Problem #1: Voodoo is camped out on St. Charles, in a Nice Neighborhood™. This is primo real estate. People in this neighborhood will overpay for just about anything, just because it's a Nice Neighborhood™. But Voodoo has a menu board and no table service? No. If you are going to charge St. Charles prices (and they do) in the LGD (because they are), then you need table service. Or lower prices. Or both. So we're squinting at the menu board, trying to find things that Vegetarian Suz can consume. We've been at it for about 30 seconds, and we're standing over in the corner, out of the way and away from the register so we can figure out our order before bothering the counter girl. The counter girl, however, has begun bothering us. Problem #2: Someone went to a cheap management course and decided that staff at Voodoo need to be PROACTIVE!!!!! in their customer service. Which led to the counter girl yelling at us from 10 feet away, asking if we wanted our food for here or to-go. When we told her that we had no idea what we were going to order, she made a pinch face at us. Instead of yelling across the room to get our order, she should have waited until we approached her. Lay off the coffee juice, lady. Okay. We know what we're going to eat now, and we try to order. Try being the operative word. First, the girl doesn't know if the potato salad has bacon in it (yes). Nor does she even ask. Then she doesn't ask friend about the white vs. dark meat chicken thing. Instead, the cook yells--from the kitchen--about it. Does friend want white or dark meat? Friend doesn't care. Cook thinks this is odd. Friend doesn't care; friend wants chicken instead of awkward conversation about chicken. Why isn't the counter girl having this conversation with friend, re: chicken? Because of... Problem #3: The counter girl didn't finish dealing with her previous customers before taking our order. So while another couple was kicking up a fuss at not getting enough brisket ("I ORDERED HALF A POUND OF BRISKET!"), counter girl was transfixed and ignoring us. For someone who was so interested in "customer service" two minutes ago, this is a swift and unexpected change. So we get to watch the unfolding soap opera about brisket that involves two customers, the manager, and the counter girl. No cups. No little number-on-a-stick. I finally ask for them, receive cups and number-on-a-stick, and retreat to the drink machine. While at the drink machine, another nice young woman approaches friend and I with our food. Would we like it here, at the drink machine? (No, you dipshit, we would like to sit in chairs.) So the food beats us to our table. This is probably a good thing. The food itself wasn't too bad, but I'm pretty sure the potato salad had bacon in it. (Two bites left me with a tummy ache.) The fries and garlic bread were both top notch, and friend reports that her chicken was worth at least four stars. Voodoo reminds me of those trust-fund hipster kids...I'm sure you know the type: ratty clothes in cheap, dingy apartments swilling PBR and bemoaning the demise of their favorite dive bar while getting a four-figure allowance every month from daddy's accountants. Accessibility notes: Dining rooms are accessible for mobility devices, but the bar is a step up. No braille menu or signage. Can get loud at peak hours so potential difficulties for hard-of-hearing customers.
label: NEG

text: I am disappointed every time I go to Laff's. I usually go a couple of months in between visits and say to myself, "OK, maybe last time was a fluke. So what if the service was miserable, and all three comedians could barely muster the intelligence to launch salvos of dick and fart jokes at the crowd? This time will be better, RIGHT?" Of course, it never is. Two item minimum: ok, I get it. That's how they make their money. Fine. Could at least one of the two items not be so mindbendingly terrible that I feel like opening a vein, though? Do not order an alcoholic drink that does not come from a bottle. It will be watered down beyond belief and slapped with a ludicrous price tag. The food (a label which I am using generously) is atrocious. They have even found a way to mess up nachos. Food is greasy, poorly cooked, often burned or messed up in creative ways. They also always seem to be out of some staple item. One night, they were out of salsa. I ordered chips and salsa, and they brought be a basket of chips with nothing else and no explanation. Another night, they had no ground beef. On yet another, they couldn't make any of their wraps because they were out of tortillas. Service is also horrendous. They pack the audience in together like sardines and employ too few waiters. You will likely wait the better part of an hour for a meal. Drinks are the same deal. One time, I only got my drink (a soda) 10ish minutes after my meal had come. The waitstaff will periodically forget about you or misplace your order. The comedians are basically bottom of the barrel, as well. Usually there is a "hungry" local MC of middling quality, followed by a veritable rogues gallery of comedians who will pontificate about their impotence, incontinence, aversion to hygiene, and inability to keep a woman (SHOCKER). Usually, on a night's bill of 3-4 comedians, one MIGHT be kind of amusing (thus, the second star). Funny sidebar - Laff's seems to loooooove comedians who make lots of gratuitous noise in the service of imitating things like airplanes, racecars, and flushing toilets. One night, when there with my girlfriend and a couple of our friends, we were watching a particularly bad comic who seemed to dig making our ears bleed with his impressions. My friend, who had been in the restroom when he came on stage, returned to the table with a shocked look on her face and disclosed that it sounded, from the toilet, as though the club was under attack by the Luftwaffe. Sadly for her, she had confused an air raid with the comic's impression of a fart. I guess the only thing that's *kind of* good about Laff's is that it's easy to get free tickets to the shows. Just sign up with the cards on the tables and you'll get a call every other month or so with a password (I shit you not) to claim your free admittance. That said, I think I'm done with Laff's for the forseeable future.
label: NEG

text: Had a tasty dinner here with a restaurant.com certificate. Service was great. Food was good, but they overcooked my medium-rare steak. It was well done. Sigh. Bread pudding was kickass. If we lived in the 'hood we'd return. But we don't.
