text: Sometimes you really crave good Hong Kong cooking...pristine seafood, outrageously tender beef, squishy sea slugs...well maybe put a hold on the slugs...but especially here in Philly, the good restaurants are the rice shoppes, not the kind of place I would take my mom out for mothers' day. And so, there we were, finally deciding on Ocean City, mostly on the weight of its former glory, they had real table cloths and napkins and because it was close to where I parked. So clear now, so confused then. so on the eve of mother's day, on a Saturday night, we were one of maybe five tables in the downstairs dining area (there was a teen birthday party in one of the private rooms...we heard their "games"). Not a good sign. The service was spotty: we had to flag the head waiter but they couldn't decide who would take our order. But the one who did take it was patient, especially with my mom who was having trouble ordering. From then on they kept the water glasses filled, but the food came out unusually slow, evidence of a reduced staff in the kitchen? the food has degenerated over the years to what we used to call "tourist" food, . The Beijing Pork Chops were sauced decently, but the amount of gristle on the meat was horrifying. The seafood - tofu hot pot lacked the homey comfort that it usually has in more able hands. The sauteed Chinese broccoli was crisp, but a little tough. All things run its course. I hope Ocean City finds another one to run and gets back on top again.

text: My husband dragged me here after hearing about it from various friends and reviews. Plus, it was Julia Child's favorite place to eat. The menu looked very promising. Items we've never heard about and choices galore. I was reading all the fantastic reviews on Yelp on my Iphone while salvating and doing the hungry I can't wait dance. Without going into too much detail the food was very bland. The meats had spices galore but everything really lacked salt. Not that I love salty food but come on! You have to have some salt in meat. text: This place is a real mixed bag. I'm looking at it only as a cinema venue, not a convert venue. First of all, it has no permanent seating. That's fine for lots of what they do there, but for a movie or a "sit down" concert, it sucks. They use ordinary padded folding chairs on a sloped concrete floor that end up making your butt and back really HURT because they are tilted forward, not level. Solving that challenge is going to be huge. I went to a movie there - "Mine with the Iron Door" (or some similar title). It was filmed in the 1920s in 4x3 aspect ratio, but the projectionist showed it as 16x9 on the theater's 16x9 widescreen screen. As a result, a significant portion of the top and bottom of the film was on the masking of the screen. How amateur is that?! And we paid $20 for the admission but were given a $3 bargain matinee show. The projection was bright and well focused and well done in that respect. Then there was the alert window that popped up on the screen in the middle of the movie because they were playing it into the digital projector from a MAC laptop, not a DVD player. Never show a movie from a laptop that is "live" to the internet or a wifi hotspot. Things like that are going to happen, for sure. Professional cinema presentation requires extreme attention to the details. The Rialto staff fell on their sword this time. I love downtown Tucson and the Rialto and the Fox entertainment bookends. There were several noticably browning pieces of lettuce - not slimy or rotten, but clearly not super fresh. That said it tasted good enough. The ribeye came out shortly thereafter. The seasoning on the steak was flavorful, but the steak was far from medium rare. It was medium well in places, and quite well everywhere else. The green beans were clearly from a can and lacked flavor. The mashed potatoes were mostly good, although undermashed with some hard potato pearls mixed in. In a city with so many restaurants delivering top quality food - I can even think of several bars that can deliver a perfectly cooked steak 24 hours a day - these mistakes are inexcusable. Also, I ordered a Bailey's and coffee and was charged 11.75 for the whole thing. The shot of Bailey's was $10. Waaay too expensive for Midcity. That's even overpriced by Bourbon Street standards. Bottom Line: If you like well done steaks and don't partake in alcohol, Neyow's is a pretty decent value. text: First off, I am from Vietnam so I think I have a bit of experience when it come to Vietnamese food. Plus our local Vietnamese restaurants that we frequent is in San Gabriel, Monterey Park, Alhambra and Santa Ana which has some of the best Vietnamese restaurants. So after reviewing all of the yelper's mediocre reviews. We figure we have to try it out for ourselves...and we did. and "In and Out" is what we did. We came in, place our Pho and the Vermicellie noodles with charbroil chicken and started with the spring rolls. Our findings: Spring rolls - very good no complaints there Pho Tai (with rare thin sliced beef) - noodle was good but then again you can't really go wrong with this right? The soup base was very bland. So sad when the soup base is what make it or break it. Wifey had the Vermicellie noodle with charbroil chicken - noodle was hard (slightly undercook, and if they were trying to make it "Al Dente" style...they totally missed the mark) Chicken tasted like teriyaki chicken, a bit on the sweet side (what the what?!!) thought we were in a Vietnamese restaurant. Chicken was very fatty. But the most annoying part was our hot tea. The teas were brought to us in these mini tea pot and mini tea cups which looks cute. In fact, absolutely adorable but totally non-practical nor functional. The mini tea cups only hold a very small sip of tea (think mini sake glasses). So we had to refill our mini itsy bitsy yellow greenie tea cup a gazillion times. Wifey got tired of this tea poring chore and just pour her tea into her water glass. My biggest pet peeves is why does most ethnic restaurant feel like they have to water down their flavors? Why don't they just embrace their ethnicity? You sure don't see the Italian and French restaurants making it more "Americanized" just to appeal it's clientele. Now don't get me wrong here, Saigon is not horrible if you are stuck in an island and need a Vietnamese flavor fixing, you will be taken care of. But they could do alot better, in fact being the first Vietnamese restaurant in Santa Barbara, they really should have set the bar high and create an exceptional menu with the most amazing authentic robust flavors with the best and freshest local produce to help inspire and get the community's palette excited. This is the way to introduce a new flavor in town! So our final verdict, will not go back if there's another Vietnamese restaurant around town. However, for now, we just might return if we really have that craving for some Pho or Spring rolls. Good luck and thread lightly...

text: I've been reading about how New Orleans was voted the number one spot in the nation for flea markets; so how come Yelp is lacking on reviewing them? This is why a NOLA Elite is needed... Of all the stores and spots she recommended, this was my favorite and definitely the best. It was a little difficult to find because their address online says the city's name is Jefferson and my GPS only recognizes Jefferson as a parish. Now I know it's in New Orleans city, and not all the far away at all. It's located literally right by the river, separated by a grassy bank and the levee. The building is HUGE. It's like a warehouse divided into little rooms, all of which are decorated with amazing antiques and thrifty finds for a fairly reasonable price (about 125 for a desk-sized table, 150 for a wardrobe or dresser). It's not the cheapest spot, but the quality of the merchandise makes up for it. They get most of their merchandise from estate sales, apparently, and the eclectic collection certainly reflects that. Several of the rooms are themed: jewelry, records, children's furniture and toys (there was an amazing vintage rocking chair that I would buy just to anticipate having children... except I'm not), books, etc. Outside in a small gated area, they sell specialty Mexican pottery, most of which is large and would be appropriate for a yard, and wrought iron benches and trellises. I purchased a vintage bracelet for $5, and I can't wait to go back and actually purchase furniture, once I'm moved in! text: Idiots. We recently arranged for a rental from this location. So we were an hour outside Tampa, and we called them to let them know we expected to be on-time. The office gave us another number to call, which we did. Got to the station, and soon enough, a Hertz car pulls up. We ride back to the HLE, which turns out to be a desk in the lobby of some hotel. Do all the normal stuff. Get keys. Waiting for car, I'm looking at the invoice more closely, and the rate billed was .. substantially higher. Collar the clerk. Go back to desk. We discovered what happened ... this location wasn't Dale Mabry, and they had sent us to a *different* Hertz HLE, because Dale Mabry didn't want to come pick us up, as the other one was "closer." Unfortunately, the other one's rates were also higher, AND they had to charge a "concession" fee for the hotel, and nobody had mentioned that. I threw a fit and told them to call Dale Mabry to come pick us up. Instead, they very graciously cut their rate to match (which must have hurt, since they essentially had to cover the hotel's fee too). The guys at the hotel HLE were gracious and accommodating under fire, handling a potentially bad situation quite well. They told me to just go and they'd take care of it, and they actually *did* take care of it. Dale Mabry, on the other hand? You get a one star for starting our stay in the Tampa Bay area off poorly.
label: NEG

text: Was at the Marriott right down the street - tried it out on Friday evening for dinner - loved it so much, we had to go back for brunch before our flight out on Sunday afternoon! Dinner on Friday - Beautiful sunset view on the water, listening to an outstanding acoustic artist playing in the bar. It's very relaxing and stress relieving...almost as if you've escaped to the life of pre-arrest Bernie Madoff for an hour or so. Crab cake appetizer - just trust me on this one...do yourself a favor and order it. Hands down among the best crab cakes I've ever had...and my pant size knows I've had more than my share of those deep-fried vices. I had a chicken dish, served with crumbled bleu cheese and crawfish. I ordered it primarily because it was such an original combination to me; I had never heard of such a dish, nor would I have come up with it myself. It was actually really good, the flavors blended amazingly - though the crawfish were a bit tough. I ordered the wedge salad before the meal - great wedge, but not worth $9 - more like $6. My guest ordered grouper and scallops and enjoyed them immensely. My other guest had a filet, however it was ordered well done. I don't feel it's fair to rate any restaurant on a well-done steak. Order crap, get crap. Brunch Don't miss it. $20 prix fixe, buffet line has everything from a omelet station to any breakfast food you can imagine - oh, and also lunch foods including freshly carved roast beef and ham and a pasta chef. A very classy event for $20. This line really does have something for everyone. A problem I run into with my friends when I want to go for brunch is that many aren't interested in breakfast food at 1230 in the afternoon, and others are - reconciling the differences can be a task. Jackson's pleases everyone. I can't wait to go back to Tampa if for nothing more than to eat here again. One of the best a small west-coast Florida city has to offer.

text: I'm shocked, just shocked that I haven't written a review of Saigon In and Out. I certainly ate here enough at my last job. I had dinner here just recently and all the fond memories were relived, and more. I think what I like best about this pho place in Santa Barbara, compared to the others, is the ambiance. I walk in, and it's a sea of green trees. The tiled design on the floor, walls and counter reminds me of the tropics, our own little pho exotica in the Milpas interzone. You can hardly see other tables in amongst the greenery. The food is not expensive, and everything is served on pretty dishes. Piles of lush greens and herbs, big decadent bowls and raised platters, it's such a sensory experience and it can be had for about $10/person for lunch, or $15/person for dinner. That's a bargain to me. My knees also go weak for Vietnamese eggrolls. Ever since I spent a new year with a clan of Vietnamese people and we spent hours making and eating eggrolls I have been a champion of Vietnamese eggrolls over all others. Wrapped up in lettuce with mint and cilantro, dipped in that fish sauce...uh, er, I need to be alone now. Pity the sandwiches have disappeared from the menu. Or maybe they're back, on the lunch menu. I hope so. My old standard is spring rolls, a bowl of dry vermicelli with chargrilled pork and eggrolls, followed up with an iced coffee. And of course, some friends whose company I love. Wish I could take photos, but it's so dark inside, much like the understorey of a tropical forest.

text: I remember it fondly, when Yelp's own Tom Clarke and Meredith Kleiber had a joint art showing at Rembrandts in Fairmount, almost a year ago. I wasnt much of an art fan, but I was a fan of those two talented Yelpers and seeing their work showcased like that, and the fact that I was actually friends with them, was magical. I had mentally noted some favorites, but didnt know if I would ever be able to buy any. At that time, art just wasnt in my budget. Little by little, I was able to put aside some money, to brighten my new home. I purchased a Tom Clarke this fall, and debated which Kleiber photo, to make mine. Also in attendance at that showing last year, was Lulu. She looked radiant as usual and it was very cool to look at the photos with her. She didnt just casually take in the art, like I would. She studied it. She saw the intricacies of the work and each shot moved her. I think this connection to all things was both a blessing and a curse for her, ultimately causing her downfall. At the time, I had made a note of the photographs, that she spent more time with. Fast forward to early 2010. Lulus birthday ws at the end of January, and since I wasnt going to be able to shower her with expensive gifts, like many of her suitors would, I decided to make it personal. With my idea, I was able to honor two of my friends, with one act. I would be able to get a simple, heartfelt gift for one friend, and support the wonderful art of another, Meredith Kleiber. Lulu is an ex-dancer and there was one shot of Meredith's that I felt embodied that principle. Just a simple little shot of a dancer, on her way to...something, in street clothes, doing a plie while waiting for a light to change. I dont know if this is one of the ones that Lulu liked at the show, but I felt it was perfect. After contacting Meredith, and getting a really reasonable price for a small print +frame, I made plans to pick it up, to get it in time for Lulu's Bday. This, was when the fun started. Ill note, that Meredith went above and beyond, to get me the print, but theres just no beating fate and Mother Nature. First, soon after ordering the photo, I had a bout with illness, which put me in the hospital and out of commission for more than a week. Then, when I finally felt good enough to venture out, Snowmeggedon hit Philly, and I was cooped up for another few weeks. Lulu's birthday had come and gone, and I apologized for the belatedness of my gift and promised I would see her and get it to her soon. She understood and was even embarassed that I had even got her anything. Around mid February, the snow had melted (somewhat) and I was feeling good and ready to get this transaction done. Sadly, as many know, and unrelated to this story, Lulu took her own life on Feb 13th. I hadnt got the picture to her yet. It was a few weeks before I was able to think about the picture that I picked out and bought for her. Im not so deluded to think that her getting the pic would have changed anything ( although I wont go on record as saying Meridiths art doesnt save lives) but I really wish she could have seen it and know that there were people who cared about her. I contacted Meredith, who had been so cool and understanding through the whole ordeal, and discussed what I wanted to do about the pic. Even though she had already shelled out her own money for the print and frame, she would have been willing to either cancel the order or even give it to me for free. She offered this not only because she is a good person, but because she is a friend. I wasnt having it though. I decided I still wanted the print, and that I wanted to pay. This goes back to my initial dream, of both owning a piece of her work and supporting her art. One of the things I thought originally was that I was happy to get something for Lulu but was disappointed that I wouldnt have my own Kleiber. I would have had to buy my own eventually anyway. So this past week, I finally got my "Street Ballet". It may be a little girly for me , but I love it. If my daughter ever gets around to cleaning her room, I may give it to her. For now, it hangs below Tom C's "Smiling Buddah" so that I have a wall devoted directly to my talented Yelp friends. I dont know if there is a moral to all of this, besides one where you should go to the website http://kleibography.com/ and get a print of your own. One thing Ive learned , is not to procrastinate and make excuses and when I really want to do something or need to do something, to get up and do it no matter what. There should be no obstacle in my way that I shouldnt just be able to plie right past.
label: POS

text: I joined some friends visiting New Orleans for the first time from up north at the Praline Connection for dinner and it was an utter embarrassment, not just personally, but for our town. They had wanted so much to try Creole food and decided on TPC based in part on the reviews on Yelp. After the few first bites, however, they all had that polite but unmistakably sour look saying "Hm, so this is it??" As reflexively protective as I am about our city's honor I could not defend one iota against the negative impression of some of our mainstay dishes brought on by TPC. First, this place unabashedly caters to tourists so the "friendliness" of the wait staff soon felt contrived and officious. It got tiresome being repeatedly interrupted as we were chatting or eating, with comments like "You know you ain't gonna get that up in New York!" I wanted to say, Oh, I hope not! for the sake of the restaurants that actually do a good job of cooking up Louisiana Creole and Soul. Next, our food was bland mush, possibly days old and then nuked to order. The stuffed bell pepper, pushed by our waiter, had a slight rancid note. When we informed him he quickly pronounced, without so much as eying the plate, that that was because of "how we marinate the peppers down here in New Orleans." Huh? Earlier when one of my friends who has a severe shellfish allergy asked the waiter if the jambalaya contained any shellfish he didn't know(!) and had to go in the kitchen to ask. This after his singing lofty praises about their jambalaya, which turned out to be a scoop of over-hot and otherwise dull and mealy rice with a few decorative coins of dried up sausage. The red beans and rice, which I ordered, was truthfully the worst I've ever had in a place charging for it. An open can of Blue Runner would've made for a more satisfying meal. The gumbo and the shrimp etouffee appetizers tasted OK, although both were thin and served in such stingy portions that they started us on our meals feeling a bit like unwanted company obtruding on someone else's table. Finally, the prices were criminally high for the quality and quantity of the food, and that left us, tourists and native alike, feeling, frankly, ripped off.

text: (3.5 stars, rounded up) I was very excited when I saw that Pure was opening up in Fountain Square. Here's the verdict: - The menu is pretty spare. A few paninis and salads, and a couple of sides. I had a caprese sandwich which was good and fresh, though I couldn't help comparing the $7 I spent on it to the $7 I usually spend on a Batali at Goose the Market. No comparison. The Pure caprese was satisfactory; the Batali is always pure art. - Speaking of art... the art on the walls of Pure is fantastic. Really, it's worth going there just to check out the art. - The decor is pretty cool, although a teeny bit rough around the edge (or maybe it just looked that way since it was empty). The space is huge, and when I was there on a Thursday early evening my husband and I were the only ones there. If I were the proprieters of Pure instead of closing at 7pm I would bring in some live music on Friday and Saturday nights. - They do have wifi, which is always a plus Will I go back? Probably, but not in a hurry to experience it as an eatery again. I'll probably bring my laptop down there one day and see what it feels like as a workspace. I do want them to succeed.

text: Take a good barbecue restaurant that you may find back east ("east" meaning Texas and points east), water down what makes it sepcial and add the sort of contrived junk on the walls (in lieu of thoughtful decor) that really says "this is a chain" and some overly friendly service. That's Famous Dave's. Tucson is not a barbecue town, regardless of what anyone wants to think, and the fact that this is so popular may be a clear sign of that. There are a few places in town that I like better, but they're small, not particularly well-known, and some are just a bit on the scary side, but they're still much better than this. However, as much as I like Tucson, I also really like barbecue, and I've never found anything here that can come close to places in the rest of the country, or even some of the better ones in Phoenix. If you want to sit down, eat and be smiled at and chatted up by a server, then this is your place. If you want to eat good barbecue, you will need to go somewhere else, perhaps outside of Tucson.

text: After the experience that my partner and I had with a really rude and incompetent vet tech at Mt. Airy Animal Hospital today, neither one of our pets will be returning there. So the whole problem was just that this woman was extremely ignorant. She had completely misunderstood the situation, not looked at the chart, and on top of that had created an escalating, chaotic situation. We asked to speak to someone in charge and Dr. Wilkerson simply said he was sorry that we were upset AKA refusing to take any responsibility. He didn't say that his vet tech was out of line, that someone should have read the chart, that he was apologetic for his staff's negligence, etc. Nothing. If anyone has any suggestions of somewhere else to go, I'm now looking.

Seems like the bus drivers run the show, and for the most part, aren't the friendliest - but for saving $40 each way I'll take the 'tude with open arms, sit back, relax, have a short snooze, charge my phone, turn on my ipod and enjoy the ride.

text: As not only a St. Louis native, but a University City Loop native, there is nothing bad I can say about Blueberry Hill. I grew up (and my parents still live) pretty much right around the corner, and when I was a kid, my brothers and I used to love coming to Blueberry Hill to play video games. My grandma always insists on a get-together there whenever any family is in from out-of-town. And now that I've moved away, Blueberry Hill is at (or near) the top of my list for places to eat when I come for a visit. The burger is a must! I always get the smaller, 5 oz., version, cooked medium rare, with cheddar. The cheddar is the soft cheese spread which I think just adds to the greatness that is the Blueberry Hill burger. Whenever I've ventured away from my standard (which hasn't happened in a long time), I've always enjoyed everything that I've ordered. Their toasted ravioli is pretty decent. Their chili is good. The gazpacho is nice and spicy. And the clam chowder, when they have it, is excellent. I'm also a fan of going to Blueberry Hill for drinks. On the weekend nights, it's usually overrun with Wash U kids, but for us locals, it's still fun. Whether you're playing darts, picking cheesy songs on the jukebox, or even chilling at a table and catching up with old friends at a table, it's a good time. They have a great selection of beers, both on tap and by the bottle, and they're very reasonably priced. I don't know if any of the other reviews mentioned it, but in room with the jukebox (which is on the older side of the place), a lot of the 2-person booths have board games under the table-tops. You can rent the pieces at the bar for a $5 deposit, just like the darts. A little bit of history on Blueberry Hill for you. It is the institution of the Loop, as it was one of the first restaurants to come in and really revitalize the area. It originally consisted only of the area to the left of the bar, but became a block-long when it moved into the old Cicero's location. Cicero's is now at the west end of the Loop, on Delmar and Kingsland. Joe Edwards, the owner of Blueberry Hill, also owns the Pin-Up Bowl on the east side of Skinker, used to own the Tivoli Theatre, came up with the St. Louis Walk of Fame, and is pretty much the King of the Loop. The corner window display changes regularly - so make sure to check that out!

text: I don't buy very many cd's anymore. iTunes just makes it too easy to have instant access to many artists. However, when I want to have an actual disk, I head to Hideaway. If I had a record player I would totally buy vinyls here as well as their selection looks pretty sweet. I love that I can almost always find what I'm looking for. And if I can't? They'll order it for me. I prefer the posters that line the Hideaway walls instead of running into grubby guys in Best Buy t-shirts. Check out the Chestnut Hill Coffee Co. up the way too if you're strung out on Starbucks.
label: POS

text: If this place has changed in the past 30-40 years, it doesn't show. White walls, white shirts, white aprons: simple, simple, simple. Very polite staff ("yes, ma'am") and apparently a local legend. I liked the food plenty: quite good without being fancy. I had chicken because I'll probably have to wait until the 5th visit to try anything else and some potato salad. Chicken had some crunchy skin you could really eat on and was moist and delicious. The lemonade was great too. It's not fast and not really too cheap either, but the real-ness more than makes up for it. Great place to stop if you are on your way back downtown from Jazz Fest, or just a couple blocks northwest of the French Quarter anyhow.
label: POS

text: This was the worst experience ever. We had to pay a cover charge to enter. It was late & we were hungry. First after 10 minutes of waiting we were told there was only 1 piece of salmon & we had to choose which one of us would get it. The winner of the meal got a lg piece of salmon, & a very generous portion of asparagus. I, the loser ordered something else. After at least 10 minutes the waitress returned to advise they mysteriously found another piece of salmon, I was shocked, starving & famished after watching the other 4 people at my table consume most to all of their food. I finally received my plate & guess what??? The new found much smaller dry, over cooked salmon & the small portion of asparagus was over cooked, which lead me to believe it was someone elses leftovers re- heated. I wasn't happy in the least but after watching everyone else finish their meals I nibbled a little. I was an unhappy camper. Then to round the evening off it was time to divvy up the bill. Well we couldn't do it evenly because much to my chagrin we discovered that the pitcher of Margarita I was drinking on an empty stomach cost $30.00 + tax + gratuities. I was very surprised, shocked & pissed (on) off. My stomach was empty & I didn't even get a buzz. Yes, I could afford a $30 drink, but I would like to have been given the option of knowing so I could make a more informative decision (not to get the drink). It wasn't worth it. I nor any of my friends will ever go there again to be robbed. PS. I took my horrible meal home in a doggie bag & it stayed in my refridg until it molded, I just couldn't eat it & I wasn't leaving it for the next person who ordered the salmon & asparagus. After all, that's how I ended up getting the booby prize!!!!

text: A wonderful place to relax and spoil yourselves in a very cute, warm, and welcoming B&B. Be sure to relax in the hammock at the end of the day (or after breakfast!). It is highly recommended that your breakfast be served outside in the patio near the fountain. The food is absolutely wonderful. For a person who likes eggs only fully cooked, I was blown away by the delicious flavors of the eggs over easy paired with sauteed vegetables and a cornmeal cake. My only gripe is the early morning sun pours in (even with the window shades closed) and the hen clucking right under my window as she's laying eggs kept me from sleeping in. Free wireless, myriad amenities, and complimentary beverages in the fridge (including fresh tea or lemonade made daily) are all the more reason I want to come back.

text: Ohmigod, this place was delicious! An acquaintance had recommended going to Distrito for their Brunch menu, and let me tell you, they were right! I had a breakfast burrito, which was really really good, my friend got something that I can't remember because I was too absorbed in the deliciousness of my own food, and then the waiter recommended that my dining partner and I split the Torrijas as a dessert. This was just about the best idea ever. Torrijas is their version of french toast - they take tres leches cake, flash-fry it so it's nice and crispy on the outside, and then sprinkle a little powdered sugar and fruit on top. AH-MAY-ZING. I've now been to Amada and Distrito, and I am thoroughly convinced that Jose Garces is a gift from the heavens bestowed upon Philly to bring us (even more) good food. Keep it comin, Jose! :)

text: When I was in New Orleans, I made a point to do some serious eating and this place was definitely one of my favorites. I had gone there for lunch on a previous trip and thought it was good but dinner was great. Yes, this place is busy and I would suggest making a reservation. We had one on a Thursday night and it was packed. They were very accommodating and gladly changed our reservation to a later time when some people in our party were running late. As for the food, I think the menu changes seasonally but if the gnocchi are on the menu then I would get it. One of the more interesting and flavorful versions I have tried. The smoked scallops and the blackened shrimp were also a hit with our group. To finish it off, we got the krispy kreme bread pudding. It was over the top but very tasty. They have a very interesting menu and everything sounds good. I am looking forward to going back soon.
label: POS

text: Natives recommended I try the crab fries, which to me tasted like soft, hot barbecue potato chips. They were pretty good and would have garnered a 3-star review. I added another star though for Play2. Being a huge gamer, I was pretty blown away that this place had big pods to rent out where you and friends can drink and play XBOX on a big screen. I wish there were places like this in Southern California. If there are, there aren't any nearby me so I'll have to stick to my home Rock Band parties/booze fests. As for the atmosphere of Chickie's & Pete's, the front area was to be expected. Very much a sports bar and crab shack sort of feel. However, our hostess led us to the back where the Play2 area is housed. I felt like I walked into a gay dance club. Techno music was thumping loudly from above and I couldn't hear anything my bf was saying sitting across from me at the table. Nonetheless, I enjoyed the atmosphere, as the walls were lit up and club lights sort of flashed around me. It was a little weird to not see people dancing in such an environment, though once a group of girls got trashed enough, they did attempt to get guys to dance with them in front of their table. They were unfortunately unsuccessful in that venture. There were a few big screens on the wall showing camera footage of people dancing or playing plastic instruments from the gaming pods. Cute.

text: Pecks Chicken has the best flame broiled chicken I've ever had - bar none. Large portions of juicy and well seasoned white meat practically slide down your throat. The sides are wonderful - I love their macaroni and cheese and the cole slaw is excellent. Meals also include warm pita bread with honey butter. You haven't experienced life until you've tried it! Pecks Chicken on US 301 in Riverview is fantastic. There are a few restaurants in the area called "Peck's" and I'm not sure if they're the same or not, but this one has a pig on the roof waving. They're also usually pretty fast about getting the food out. I would highly recommend this place to any hungry person.

I've mentioned in other reviews that taqueria coke has a certain flavor to it you can't get anywhere else. I don't know if they overdo the syrup or what the reasoning behind it is - but the coke here was seriously the bomb... that is, until they ran out!! I've always had problems with the staff in some way but they seem friendly enough, and it would be fantastic if they had wifi, but it's still in walking distance for me (and near Himmel Park) and has a decent wine selection so any problems are pretty negligable as far as I'm concerned. text: One of our first dinners in New Orleans was at Cafe Maspero. We were greatly impressed with its location near the riverfront and the prices on the menu compared to other similar restaurants. The atmosphere was very casual and we felt we could just relax our tired bodies there after a long day of walking around the French Quarter. We were seated and served right away. I ordered the muffuletta and my friend ordered the corned beef sandwich. Both were GI-NORMOUS. We each saved half and had them the next night before hitting Bourbon St. The sandwiches were delicious and the service was good, too. (Our server was Australian, I believe.) We decided to return a second night later in the week with our partners who had recently joined us on the visit. Unfortunately, it wasn't as great as an experience. We were seated near the kitchen door and manager's/servers' table where they sat, talked, and worked on paperwork. The $1 glass of house wine was a nice surprise for my partner, but the Shrimp Po Boy he ordered wasn't up to expectations. It came on a big seeded hamburger roll, not on a long French bread, and the shrimp kept falling out. It felt...wrong. So, I'm basing most of my rating on my first experience, as that's what I want to think of as the usual experience one has at the restaurant. Lesson learned: go there once, not twice, and keep your good memories. And, yes, like most restaurants in New Orleans: cash only.

text: Performance Bike, we are breaking up for good. Yes, I've always preferred supporting local shops like Therapy or Trophy. And yes, you often have really great prices on things that no other shops carry and that I need right away. But as of today, I vow to do whatever it takes to not spend another dime on your premises. Here's why. The customer service here has never been that great. Checking out always took longer than necessary, the employees were never particularly knowledgeable, and I've rarely if ever seen a woman working there--small annoyances really in the grand scheme of corporate retail. The big stuff was when we tried to get a broken chain replaced while it was still under warranty and the mechanic straight-up lied about calling and talking to SRAM (on Memorial Day Sunday no less) and claimed that they had told him to just fix the chain instead of replacing it. We later verified with SRAM directly that they were closed and would have never said that anyway. The other dealbreaker is that your employees are incredibly flaky about whether they will allow returns/exchanges for items ordered online. One year, my in-laws bought me about $150 worth of clothes online (none of which fit) and the store happily let me exchange them on store credit. Today my husband tried to return a $3 seatpost shim and was thoroughly rebuffed--which was pretty short-sighted, considering that we had walked in to buy about $30 worth of tubes and maybe a helmet. Don't get me wrong, I will probably still order stuff off the national website on occasion and do in-store pick-up. I might even see your sister store in Wilmington every now and then when I don't feel like paying sales tax. But you and me, Philadelphia store, we're through.

Now, being a first timer, I had no preference for stylist, and had I asked for someone specifically, I probably wouldn't have been able to make an appointment that fast. Blue a Hair Salon is unlike any other. It's an old Inn converted into this really hip/trendy Salon with stations upstairs and down. I checked in and was whisked away upstairs. I had reservations when I told my stylist what color brunette I was looking for precisely and she disappeared to mix my color and didn't offer to show me color swatches. It turned out the right shade of brunette, but I was more psyched about not having the usual rim of brown all around my hair line. text: Ok I admit it fully and whole heartedly... I am a spoiled little zoo brat. I grew up going to an amazing zoo (yes outside of the home I grew up in, though if you ever came to visit my family you would get a true picture of a zoo as well, but back to the topic). I feel the zoo was a little small, the paths were too narrow for the crowds of people that do not understand that the right side goes one way, the left the other direction. I know I am at the zoo, but I HATE strollers... twice as much when the parent is carrying the child and still taking up valuable sidewalk space with the stroller. I know its the zoo, a kid friendly place, I have taken all my nephews, nieces, cousins to the zoo since I was 18 and the youngest was old enough to walk. They don't go until they can walk, because strollers are inconvenient for all but the parent that spoils the child and buys a bunch of crap that the kid doesn't need and then proceeds to carry the kid anyway! Ok that was a bit of a side rant back to your normally scheduled rant... The petting zoo was interesting and extensive, but they don't give you the option of zoo provided treats to try to get the animals over to you, so most stay out of reach and are VERY skittish, like they aren't socialized with people the way petting zoo animals should be. The zoo seems to have a weird bottle neck layout that makes one feel like a cow in a cattle drive, and the animal enclosures are some of the smaller ones I have seen. I waited 4 years before finally getting to go to the Indy zoo and the bright spot in my day was the giraffe licking me as i got to feed it, ok cool, but not enough to save this... really... not even an extensive monkey/primate/ape house?! I thought THAT would be standard.

text: I reviewed this awhile ago and vowed not to go back, but when I saw a Red Lobster commercial this afternoon, I was craving GOOD seafood. RL is about 40 minutes away and I know the wait is always ungodly long, so I took a chance at Mitchell's again. The most recent reviews have been so good, that I thought maybe it was just me that I didn't enjoy it. Yah...I'm not sure what they are eating, but I wish I could have had that!! I feel badly giving it a one star, b/c our server and the hostesses were AWESOME. We brought Max (our 9 month old) and this was our first experience at a "nice" restaurant with him. We always feed him in the restaurant so he doesn't get bored and have some (not too noisy) toys. They graciously sat us in a big booth so we could spread out and also in the back where we would not disturb others. Our server never forgot about us (thanks, Kristin!) and was always on top of our drinks, etc. I really appreciated her efforts and for the service, I give it a big thumbs up... Buuuut, she doesn't cook the food. And, it's a shame, b/c someone new needs to take over that kitchen. They apparently have run out of salt and pepper. All of our food was bland, unseasoned and flat out boring. My shrimp were soggy...and they look to be breaded but they were supposed to be grilled. Our appetizer (the shrimp artichoke dip) was OK. It wasn't blowing me away but it wasn't terrible once we salt and peppered it. My crab cake was OK and my asparagus were just OK as well. I was supremely disappointed in the shrimp. For the money, it should be at least edible. I didn't finish them. I also got "green onion mashed potatoes"...um, they tasted out of a box. I hope they aren't but again, bland and no taste. :( I tried my husband's arctic char, which our server recommended. He got it blackened but it was downright flavorless. He ate everything b/c he can't stand to waste, but I would have probably sent it back. I wanted to speak to the manager, but my hubby was ready to go. He doesn't like it when I complain in public. I just thought he should know, so I filled out the review sheet in our bill. I hope they read it....I don't want anything in return, but I do want them to know that this is not the kind of food you want for that price. Our bill with tip was $81 and I feel like the only thing worth the cash was Kristin. She deserved a tip but I might as well have just caught my money on fire. The last time I said I should have gone to Bonefish. I should have taken my own advice or driven to Red Lobster...yep, that's right. I would have rather eaten Red Lobster than Mitchell's. :( BOOOOO :(. EDITED TO ADD: The comment card was read and the manager called me immediately. They offered me a gift card to come back, so we will be giving it another shot. I really want to have a good experience here. I will let you Yelpers know what happens. I didn't expect anything for free, but it's nice that he is making an effort. For that, I will give it another star. They deserve it. The service and management are outstanding, obviously! I am very happy with that kind of response.

text: We have been using For Paws Philly for the over a year to walk our two dogs on a regular basis. For Paws has also provided house sitting services while we were on vacation and has also had our two dogs at her home. We were supposed to drop them off on 12/21/09 - the Monday after the big snow storm - so that we could catch an overseas flight early in the evening. We ended up being crunched for time and Sarah was able to come over and pick them up with only a few hours notice. They have both been at her house before and enjoy being there. Our one is not so great with other dogs, Pepper, so Sarah keeps him separated from other dogs she is watching but the other, Doctor, had a great time playing with the other dogs that Sarah was watching. While on our trip Pepper has some issues with an ear infection that we thought had cleared up before we left. She arranged to take him to our Vet and got him some additional medication which she applied for the rest of his stay. Sarah also comes over once a week so that my wife and I can go out after work and the dogs are always really excited to see her. Doctor is normally very scared of strangers - she was badly abused before we adopted her - but after a few visits she warmed up to Sarah and is now very happy to see her. Sarah was also great with an older dog that we had to put down earlier this year. Pinkie was only with us for a couple of years but she was a very special dog and Sarah always left very detailed notes about how she was doing on her weekly walks and alerted us when she thought there might be a problem. To sum up - Sarah has always come over to walk our dogs as scheduled, she is open to scheduling last minute walks, and leaves good notes as to results of each walk. text: We drove by Gallo's seafood ( Roosevelt blvd & Solly NE Philly) on our way home and noticed a nice big catchy sign out front. BURGER BAR NOW OPEN. The Burger bar is attached to Gallo's seafood and it's around back on the side. We were hungry and I adore burgers like I adore air. So I figured Gallo's has been there, forever, lets give it a shot. Though I didn't have much hope since it's part of a seafood restaurant. Well I'm amazingly glad we stopped by. The decor is very nice. Modern and something never expected, let alone in the North East. In Center City or Old city yes. Not up here, so near to our house. All ready I was excited and didn't even taste anything yet. The place was empty, ( It just opened a few days ago) but we were greeted warmly and seated right away. The decor really blew me away. We quickly decided on our food. We started with the buffalo wings. They were exccccellent ( as Mr.Burns would say) Perfectly crispy and well coated with a zippy sauce. Very good blue cheese as well. Chunky. The burgers shortly arrived after scarfing the wings down. My wife had the low carb burger wrapped in bib lettuce. She loved it. I had the 5 napkin burger which sat on a house baked brioche bun. WOW it was perfect. Plus bun to meat ratio was spot on. Now the main event, the meat. Again it is house ground sirloin and loosely packed cooked over cast open flame grill. Juicy, perfectly seasoned. The burger was pure perfection. Nothing to nit pick over. The bacon crispy and lots of it. Winner. Cheese gooey and over flowing. The egg I ate separately, not to mask the flavors with the sunny side egg. Even that was great. This burger ranks in my top 2-3 EVER. Did I mention how F**KING AWESOME it was. The garlic Parm fries were tasty, but would have liked a bit more garlic and some grease ( I like fries a tad greasy). Next time I will try the onion rings and maybe one of those tasty sounding shakes. I did speak with the owner on the way out and he was a burger connoisseur as well. Not someone just slapping open a burger spot. He researched and did his homework. Keeping everything in house and doing it right. Thank you so much. Great guy. I would love for this place to have a "challenge" burger. If so sign me up. Also possibly add burger patties as a option. I most definitely will be back, and often. Don't move from the area EVER!
label: POS

text: Finally! Bikram comes to Nashvegas. This location isn't as dressy as trendier studios in California, but once you get in the room, none of that really matters. It's not like you picked the studio so that you could feel so calm and relaxed. Be prepared to sweat out your daily caloric intake, just like any other Bikram studio. Housed in the Cool Springs Ice Hockey arena, the "A Game Sportsplex", the outer studio itself reflects the militant nature of Bikram with its gray cinderblock walls and linoleum flooring and minimalist changing rooms and racks for placing your personal items. Please note, there are no showers or bathrooms in the studio, which is a big bummer, you have to walk down the hall to the main sportsplex bathroom, which can be a little bit awkward when you're running barefoot barely clothed before class. The class itself brings the heat - though the room is small, it's intimacy provides a good energy for the students. Teachers here are less strict than in NY or LA, I think they're making sure people come back for more. I went three times when I was home over break, and found each teacher to be warm. capable and consistent with Bikram. I always appreciate a more stern teacher but nonetheless was not disappointed with these classes. Afterward, grab a coconut water, it's filled with potassium which is a little miracle cure if you're feeling particularly drained. And don't worry, in case you forget mat, towel, water or even shorts - they've got it all there for you to purchase. If you're a beginner, check out my list (http://www.yelp.com/list/you-know-bikram-i-know-his-studios-costa-mesa-2) for tips on how to get into Bikram if you're nervous. Enjoy!

text: Zakes Cakes and Cafe opened as an outpost in the suburbs to serve "light fare" and continues to satisfy the community's collective sweet tooth today. Located in Fort Washington, Zakes (sometimes listed with an apostrophe) resides on the lower floor of a house at the bottom of a hill. To quote directly from another review: "Zakes' salads, sandwiches and soups are all outstanding, but save room for dessert! Many delicious specials to choose from, in addition to a great menu. The only problem here is making a decision. Be prepared to wait for a table around lunchtime..." Unless you arrive early, you'll have to wait at least 15 minutes to get a table. After noon, the place fills up! You'll get to wait on the patio's couch (!) and appreciate the garden outside at least. The main room can seat a reasonably large party. Look around and you'll see regulars from the surrounding area: residents of Ambler and Fort Washington and droves of worker bees from the nearby industrial parks. On a sunny day the place is cheery and well-lit. On cloudy days, the ceiling lighting is well-arranged and doesn't overwhelm. The walls are decorated with framed photographs thrown about. I can't remember any music playing in the background. The menu has Italian, Vietnamese, French, Chinese, and English highlights. Daily specials are available at Zakes. I had a bowl Mediterranean tomato soup with orzo. It was lightly flavored with tomato and herbs and had a light, pleasing taste. Chunky bits of orzo added substance to the dish. The portabello sandwich tasted like pizza and had the consistency of a tomato pie. It was topped with brussel sprouts... I looked forward to taking another bite as soon as I took the first! The mocha gatteau didn't live up to my expectations. I was disappointed that the mocha was not as strong as I would have liked. The level of the baker's expertise is evident in the clean presentation of the cake. Zakes is a comfortable place to go for lunch and a cup of coffee. Next time I go I think I'll get the Saigon salad, summer rolls (with chicken, shrimp) or the bourbon glazed salmon... so many choices...
label: POS

text: This is a fun east-coast bar that is mostly quiet during the day and rocks on the weekend. When we came back on a Saturday night, it was hard to find a place to sit and there didn't seem to be enough servers working for the number of people in the bar. So we went up to the bar to order. The crowds get so thick in here it's a bit hard to walk with beers back to the table. I'd recommend coming early if you're planning an evening at the Trap. Get a table, relax over dinner, then gear up for a night of spirits and East Coast crooning. The band that was performing on the night we went was loud, but good. They really got the crowd going and even had people up dancing in front of them into the wee hours. The space is festooned in fish nets, traps, and other seafaring and East coast nostalgia. This is the place to be for homesick Easterners living in the west, looking for a taste of home.

text: Having worked in restaurants in Philadelphia and knowing some of the crew responsible for this restaurant I will try to be as objective as possible, and in turn knowing that you shouldn't visit a restaurant in it's first week before they've gotten all the kinks worked out, my wife and I couldn't resist checking it out on day 4. We'll of course go back and see the progression in a few weeks if not sooner, especially when we can go back for lunch in the future (inevitable), but I have to say that we thought this restaurant was solid from the minute we walked in the door. To be totally honest this is not a 5 star restaurant, the five stars are there because it wildly exceeded my expectations for the place 4 days in and for the concept as a whole. Host staff was on it from the get go getting us seated right away and most importantly acknowledging our existence before we even crossed the doorway. The decor is somewhat of a cross between a futuristic diner and a starkly minimal Momofuku-esque food bar. Not sure why there aren't more restaurants with open kitchen bars, seeing as in this world full of new "foodies" stuck to their tv sets watching every cooking show in existence, wouldn't they want to recreate that experience live in the restaurants they actually eat in? Maybe this is the future? While we didn't sit at the bar we will in the future and were disappointed that we didn't make that decision this time. Michael Shulson was on hand in the kitchen and despite the place being somewhat empty at 6:30 when we arrived, by 7pm the place was getting packed and the open kitchen was bustling. The LED backlit forest is a very inviting sight from the sidewalk and surely an "open" sign for all those passing by. Anyway, we noticed many familiar staff from stalwart restaurants such as Buddakan and Morimoto surely attributing to the casual, efficient and unobtrusive service style. The menu is set up in an approachable small plate style with great pricing. You could probably get out of here for $25 a person, but it's hard to resist (especially on a first visit) not ordering everything to try and walk out having spent much more(but isn't that the point of the small plate movement:). First things first, Michael Shulson is famous for his edamame dumplings to which he made famous at Buddakan but you won't find the same delicate petite dumplings here but more of a authentic chinese style soft dumpling (read: thicker doughier skin, and in my experience working with Chinese chefs this is the real thing). Many people may dismiss the dumplings as less refined than those of the style he created at Buddakan but it certainly pleased my wife and I to see this style in such a restaurant in Philadelphia and we hope others can appreciate it as well. I also hate to say it but the Philly cheese steak (yet another restaurant twisting Philly's namesake food) with Sriracha was fantastic. AND the Pork Bahn Mi. At $9 I predict this being my lunch on many days headed to work. For what you would pay to eat a sandwich (and I mean this is a cheesesteak sized roll) for almost the same price anywhere in Center City, you can have this instead. We had the lobster gyoza, which wasn't our favorite but was solid with a great presentation and the inclusion of what looked like some sort of dehydrated chili balanced with the sweet and acidic 1-2 combo of apples and miso. Finally we had the shrimp & egg fried rice with Virginia ham, and I have to say that Shulson wins the prize of having the most delicate but fully seasoned fried rice in town. Light but full of flavor! The wine prices are approachable and we had the Jovly Vouvray at $40 (a deal considering it is real Loire Chenin), perfect for the food we had. It arrived less than cold, but possibly had just arrived that day considering how soon after the open we came. Overall a great experience for a concept which we had our eyes on because we are fans of David Chang's Momofuku restaurants in the East Village and wanted something similar in our neighborhood. Next time we'll be hitting up the Ramen and making the comparison. Great new restaurant for Center City.
label: POS

text: This is another casino that went straight down the tube when they expanded, not just for customers, but for their employees as well. It all started around 10 years ago, when no longer content to be a popular first stop casino and blue collar truck stop with good inexpensive food, BOOMTOWN sought to cuten up the place up by expanding the square footage and ringing it in a building a facade that looks like a pastel colored Western Town. But the plan to make more money went deeper than that. They had to raise the cost of their food, and lessen the quality overall. Right away parking, service and gaming all suffered in pursuit of getting the hundred million back that BOOMTOWN spent on its expansion. Truckers and locals were no longer the main customers so employee earnings suffered and so did employee friendliness as longtime BOOMTOWN employees quit or were forced out. But the worst was yet to come. The casino should have refocused and redoubled its efforts to attract back truckers and locals, but they took a left turn instead. In an attempt to combat the big casino that opened in Auburn and usurped BMTWN's position as first casino on the way to Reno, BOOMTOWN sought the installation of a Cabella's sporting goods store as the main instrument to reinvigorate their clientele. This upside down thinking attracted almost no one because BOOMTOWN didn't really understand who its customer was or how to market to that customer. Again, all the good machines were taken out and less and less table games are open. A long time friend 21 dealer quit his job after working here for 10 years because tips were reduced by 80%. I give Boomtown 5 years or less under its current ownership/business plan. The sooner it's sold to someone with a brain, the better. Otherwise, it could well end up going broke.

text: I'm predisposed to like any place that serves goat stew 24 hours a day. On the plus side, this place is inexpensive, and I would recommend the birria. I'm a fan of that style, but I was struck by how bland La Michoacana's were compared to, say, Beto's. I had a similar reaction to their tostada de ceviche (which was passable) and their sope (which was amazingly bland). text: This is an adorable place with a darling kitchen. The menu proudly advertises that they opened in June 2010 then touts their flexible kitchen. Breakfast until they close? Sure! Lunch starting at 11? Okay (I guess). I took my international advisor on all things cute and twee to see if this cafe fit the bill. She was thrilled with the blue chairs, textural art, and all the little "New Orleans" touches tucked around the shop. The prospect of a fruit kebab made her literally squeal. So on the cute and twee side, Lucky Ladle nailed it. Yes! On another reviewer's recommendation, we tried the spinach and three cheese dip. It was good although not addictive. I thought it was a nice break from the pervasive spinach artichoke dip; my dining companion was disappointed because spinach artichoke dip is her favorite thing ever. Were I to return, I'd order it as my entree with a side salad or a piece of pie. For entrees, the veg*n lunch side of the menu is a little slim with only two outright veg*n sandwichs. I suspect everything else could be modified with no pains, but it would go a long way to see that noted on the menu. The veggie quesadilla was better than Juan's, with crisp fresh veg instead of soggy pre-cooked stuff. It was also pretty big. (See picture.) The fruit kebab was a nice touch, too. I made my own sandwich, and that was easy enough. The price was right for me, and everything was good. I enjoy the circle-your-own slips because I know my ideal sandwich won't be lost in translation. And yes, fruit kebab. (Again with the fruit kebabs, you think. Well, it's sufficiently novel, AND the fruit was really good. Better than the standard fruit cup!) Even though I didn't try the soup or pie, I think the Lucky Ladle has a strong concept; and I'm excited to live nearby. I want to keep noshing here and nibbling my way through the menu. This is a worthy lunch stop for businessfolk, and the parking in the area (street) is pretty easy for folks who want to hop over from the CBD. Accessibility notes: Fully accessible for mobility devices. No braille menu or signage.

text: I took my cat here because he had a blocked urethra/couldn't urinate. He was given a catheter and IV for fluids and pain medicine and spasm medicine. He stayed for one night and I spoke with the vet who said his kidney levels were still not good and they wanted to keep him for another night for $1,000 to $1,700. I told her I did not think that was reasonable and I would pick him up after that first night and take him somewhere else. Well, when they knew I was firm the next day about picking him up, all of a sudden, the price was now $450 for another night. Interesting. So he stays another night and I take him home and give him a bath because he was filthy. He continues on his pain med and spasm medication. He just sleeps, doesn't eat, and eventually he starts to wet himself. I take him back in and it turns out that he has a urinary tract infection now and he stayed another two nights and they get $1,150. BUT THEY COULD HAVE AND SHOULD HAVE PRESCRIBED AN ANTIBIOTIC IN THE FIRST PLACE, since they introduced the catheter and IV, and even admitted to me that infection was likely to result. Now my cat is still uncomfortable and not well, taking antibiotics, anorexic, but Ryan has $2,300 of my hard-earned money. They're like a flea market: if you bother to talk them down and say you're taking your pet home, they'll try to bargain to get something out of you. text: Well this little dining gem came out of nowhere. It's like a string of decent businesses are popping up in Conshohocken's most cursed locations. Now, if we can get something in place of the old Philly Pretzel Factory (turning into a Mexican Market, why? no one knows. I hope they serve tacos). Ok, you want reviews on Big T's BYOB. That's what I'm calling it now. This "ex-Bergey's/post-chiquita whatever" joint has been split in two. Theresa's BYOB for fine dining, and M Bar, which is a loungy couch-filled singer songwriter hangout. I can only make that assumption based on the pictures online and the sounds I heard while going to the bathroom in the Theresa's section. You can literally walk from one establishment to the other. I haven't, because this is all about Theresa. They really did a nice job making it look like you're actually in Theresa's basement. And you can only imagine Theresa in the back creating these delicious recipes that come from the kitchen. We were greeted by a pleasant tall fellow with a slight accent. Although, probably a coincidence, I appreciated the accent. Once we were seated, our waiter came over and asked to open our large bottle of wine. He tried to make a funny about the size of our Yellow Tail Riesling, but it came off as awkward. Oh well. Moving on, the bread is fresh and delicious, served with some oil. The oil was also very tasty. Since my lady recently decided she liked calamari, I took this opportunity to order that as an app. It came out quickly and was very flavorful. Some might say a little on the salty side, I say "whatever" to you. It's from the sea, and the sea is salty so order something else. The dippin' sauce was some sort of something. It went well with the calamari and bread so I'm not sure I care what it was. My date ordered the sea scallops with creamy risotto and asparagus. I stole some and it was very good. They were smaller, soft, and succulent scallops. The asparagus was well cooked and the risotto was a nice compliment, making you feel like you're getting your money's worth. Brussels sprouts are cool again!! ?? I went all out and ordered the Grilled 12 oz. NY sirloin with port, peppercorn, and blue cheese. It came with garlic mashed and brussels sprouts. The sauce on the steak was so good I tried to drench all of my sides in it. I also learned that I like peppercorn that day. I'm not sure how they cook the brussels sprouts, but they were very delicious. The texture was different than what I'm used to from this underrated veggie, but damn it worked. I also learned that blue cheese on it's own tastes a little like Brie and I hate Brie. Is that wrong? Oh well, I might ask for no BC next time I order that. Highly recommended meal though. Overall, everything we tried that night seemed to have it's own unique flavor. I hate when everything tastes the same. They seem to have the "Mediterranean" theme down pat. The wait staff may seem a little awkward and throw a couple cheesy one-liners at you, but who cares...the food. Man o' man, the food.

The mac n cheese was to die for according to my wife (globe traveling mac n cheese aficionado). The dessert we could have skipped because we were too full from the meal. text: I read someplace that when you wash your car at home, you waste gallons of water in comparison to a conventional car wash. Whether I'm lazy or believe that this statement is true, I tend to rely on others to wash my car. I've had all of the cars I've owned washed, by different car wash companies, hundreds of times over the years. Having spent the money and experienced all kinds of different car washes, one could say I'm somewhat of an expert on the subject. Having said all of that, I'd like to weigh in on Octopus at 22nd and Kolb (just east of that intersection on the south side of 22nd). I've had my car washed at Octopus (and it's prior ownership) at least 20 to 30 times over the last 5 years. I frequent Octopus, mostly because of convenience...it's on my way home. Most times, Octupus is decent. You don't feel like you're getting "oversold" on their products, the people seem nice enough and they do an OK job on washing your car. I've never had a WOW experience there and continued going out of convenience, as I said. After my visit last week, I'm not going back. Maybe I'm picky. But, I'm a consumer and am allowed that luxury of choice. When I pay for full service at $20 ($10 if you have a coupon) I expect the following: vacuumed within a degree of perfection, interior wiped down with no "dust trails", interior windows cleaned with no streaks and a fairly dry car after being wiped down by 4 people. At Octopus, you get mediocrity. Some say, you get what you pay for. Since I've had WAY better quality of service at other car washes in town for the same money (see Classic Car Spa), I beg to differ. When you have competition down the road doing a better overall job for the same money, it's time to step up your game. My last visit to Octopus was probably the perfect storm of badness: The guy asking me what kind of wash I wanted looked like someone shot his dog and was going through the paces of his mundane job. The guy trying to sell windsheild repair services blocked my way inside to try and sell me an un-needed windsheild replacement. The car itself was handed over still spotty with water, streaky interior windows, a sideways rearview mirror, dusty interior and poorly vaccumed. Overall, for the money, you can do better in Tucson. If you're an eastsider, Octopus is OK. If you want to drive a little more to get better service for your dollar, go to Classic.

A whole place dedicated to making kolaches? I figured it was something new, so why the heck not. I liken this place to an Eastern European Dunkin Donuts. They have kolaches filled with all kinds of different stuff. They have sweet ones (blueberry, pineapple, raspberry) and savory ones (philly cheese steak, pizza, club sandwich, italian chicken). Wanting to get a fair sample, we got one of each of the aforementioned (is that the correct use of the word?) kolaches. These things are not very big, and I can't imagine anyone getting full off of just one. OVERALL- Tried something new, and didn't care for it too much. His charming young wife, Pam, serves as hostess and appears to assist in general managerial duties. She is a model of eager-to-please, cheerful efficiency, as is the young wait-staff. I have visited this place more than a dozen times and found it to be consistently excellent. On each occasion I tried the Soup de Jour, which was always different, always interesting and invariably wonderful. My favorite entrée here is the Fillet of Sole Francese, a very generous portion of perfectly sautéed sole topped with lump crabmeat and an incredible sauce. My late wife doted on the Scaloppini of Veal Marsala. Bacio offers an excellent lineup of meat, seafood, fowl and some very inventive pasta entrees . . . all excellent.. The desserts are varied and sinful, and despite firm convictions to resist, I frequently succumb to the Tiramisu. I try to mitigate the 10,000 calorie hit by sharing, and then work hard on overcoming my hostility toward the "sharee." I'm afraid that some of the other desserts, like the 'Chocolate Obsession' (warm dark chocolate fudge cake with pistachio gelato) and the "Creme Brulee di Bacio" (vanilla creme layered with limoncello custard in a cinnamon-graham cracker crust, topped with fresh berries) aren't much easier to resist and don't offer promising weight-control alternatives. Bacio is located in a small strip-center which provides more than adequate parking, and it is well worth the short drive from Philadelphia.

text: I've had Remington (or, more accurately, Remington has had me) for 5 years. This year, however, I had plans to go away over Christmas and, understandably, had a tough time finding someone who could watch him. Intensely skeptical of boarding him, I started researching and came across Camp Bow Wow, which had newly arrived in Cherry Hill, and was immediately impressed (although not yet sold). After calling and speaking to an associate, my skepticism started to wane - I was impressed by their rigorous requirements for attendance, and then even MORE impressed by their flexibility and understanding when our now infamous 27-inch snowstorm interfered with Remington's interview, just 4 days before I was scheduled to leave. Nervous as any crazy pet mama dropping him off, the staff assured me that he was the cutest pup they'd seen (and, like I do when the vet's office tells me the same thing, I of course believed them) and that he'd do great with the other dogs who were there. (Again, intense skepticism on my part, knowing Rem can be a real jerk sometimes). The tour through the facility was incredibly comforting. Rem had always been anxious in a crate, which of course, made me nervous, but these seemed clean, comfortable and roomy. Again, the staff assured me that there was plenty of out-of-crate time and that they'd keep an eye on him to make sure he was fine. After a 2 hour stay, I picked him up to rave reviews (which I, again, ate up) and a detailed report card. Dropping him off, 4 days later, was easy (I'm speaking logistically, of course, emotionally, it was a completely different story), the staff made me feel completely comfortable and at easy. (Although I admit, I did check in on him on the webcam a couple of times during his stay to ease my guilty mind.) I got a full report on his stay upon picking him up from a counselor who seemed to really know him and care about him. I was shocked (and irrationally proud) to learn that he had enjoyed playing (and nicely!) with the other dogs - an anomoly for my little punk. I would feel absolutely comfortable sending him there again, and would recommend them to anyone who asked. On top of it all, I think it's an incredibly fair price for the quality of care. Huge fan!

text: I can't believe I would give Noble 5 stars but I am because it is just that good--perhaps it was because I had low expectations b/c every time I walked by, I would gawk at the prices. I have seen this place go from a gutted nothing to when the construction guys put in that beautiful wooden staircase to seeing it become one of the busiest restaurants in Philly. The food is outstanding. My bf and I came early (6pm) and although the downstairs was crowded (mostly at the cozy bar), the upstairs was completely empty. (They have this amazing high table facing Sansom which would be very cool for a 8-10 person party.) We weren't seated in the nice, back area that reminds me of every other restaurant in Manhattan (i.e., booth seats on either side, nice chairs facing the booths and servers walk up and down the middle), we were seated overlooking the staircase. It was actually very nice and we got to see all the customers come in and the wait staff bringing various cocktails from the bar downstairs. The place is perfectly lit and there is something about the decor that makes the place subtly elegant and fancy, yet still very comfy. I loved everything from the cups, silverware, to the amazing house-made sourdough bread (served w/ salted butter) that they refilled without asking. Also, my bf's chocolate Yards stoudt was DELICIOUS! We opted for the octopus app over the scallops and I loved it (but my bf who is Greek complained it wasn't octopus-y enough...) There was this delicious olive oil drizzled on it that was so flavorful and although I didn't like the tomato romesco, the squid ink croquettes were out of this world, their creaminess went SO well w/ the chewier octopus, and the paper-thin radish slices were very yummy, their crunchiness added the little something you were looking for. There were also little capers and some arugula, I believe, and the tiny blood orange pieces were amazing. For our main course, we tried the beef cheeks and bison ribeye, both were very tasty but the bison was the clear winner (I found the sauce on the cheeks a little bit too salty and intense). We weren't a huge fan of the chestnuts which didn't seem roasted (were they pan-fried?) but the okinawa sweet potato (mashed) and bluefoot mushrooms were really delicious. The bison came w/ parsnips which were too bitter but the béarnaise sauce was delicious and I always love shiitake mushrooms! We were too full for dessert but I'm sure everything is wonderful. I cannot wait to come here for brunch. I've seen the dishes and they look so delish and comforting (I think mini skillets have that effect)! The general age group of the customers seem 30-50 and the wait staff is extremely professional and attentive (although I'm not a fan of their blue shirted outfits). I will def be back for a drink at the bar as well. It sounded very loud down there, but that was prob b/c of one particularly obnoxious party. Also, this place is not cheap: the octopus is $14, stoudt was $6, bison was $36 and the beef cheeks are $28. p.s. I've read about the pretentious and mean host who I caught a glimpse of several times as he bounded upstairs to the back kitchen several times. text: I'm a big fan of the Royal Tavern. It has been within a few blocks of my house for almost half of the 9 years I've lived in this city, and during that time I've seen it go through many changes. Years ago, it was the best place for some kind of stuffed french toast on a sunday morning. These days, I don't bother with brunch there anymore because it became too popular for it's own good, and the poor servers constantly look overextended and the wait times can be awful. There's a good reason for the popularity, but I'd rather avoid it. I tend to grab dinner here frequently. Partially this has to do with the fact that unlike some local bars who say their kitchens are open late but close them down early if they aren't busy enough, I can always count on the kitchen here to be open until 1am. I work an odd schedule, and so this has saved me from going hungry or going Wawa many, many evenings. The menu always has vegetarian / vegan options, once in awhile the specials menu will as well, and the soups are consistently great. This is good to keep in mind, because they pair well with the grilled cheese and a beer. (an aside about beer: i tend to like darker beers. the fact that the Royal always has bottles of Yuengling porter in the fridge makes me very, very happy. a lot of bars don't carry it, and it's one of my favorites, so kudos to them. now if i could convince them to keep a keg of the Yards Brawler on tap at all times, I'd be content forever.) All that being said, my two true loves at the royal tavern are the popcorn and the tempeh club. the popcorn is so good that sometimes when we're sitting around the house getting ready to throw in a movie, i'll run down the street and grab a few orders of popcorn to bring home and eat with the movie. seriously. and it's a perfect inexpensive bar snack. enough other people have gushed about the tempeh club so i'm not going to, but i will say that even if i wasn't a vegetarian, I'd still be ordering the tempeh club. it's a mess to eat, but 100% delicious. the jukebox can be hit or miss depending on your tastes, but i'm pretty sure there's something in there for everyone. watch out though because sometimes it gets LOUD for no apparent reason when you start picking selections and it's mildly embarrassing because everyone in the bar turns to glare at you as if you turned the volume up to deafening on purpose. and finally, i have to say that the staff is pretty great. I've watched the servers sit and take written tests on the menu and the beer selection, so they definitely know their stuff. they are always very friendly, and i've spent many nights sitting at the bar drinking and being entertained by the bartenders goofing around. good vibes abound. my favorite bar in the city.
