text: So every so often I return to Indianapolis to visit family, and every time I experience severe culture shock. Yes, I truly belong in LA. First, I'll forgive this place for sporting a truly uninspired name. That said, there wasn't much to praise about this place. We arrive, a party of 5. Not an unusual number for a restaurant, no? Well the hostess wants to simply put a 5th chair on the end of a table for 4...and there would have been no room for us to all fit, legs under the table where they belong. An empty table set for 6 is next to the too-small table, and we inquire about using that one. No, the table that is set for six is used for parties of 7 to 8. Yeah I don't get that either, but 15 minutes later the hostess got 3 other people to put 2 other tables together to accommodate us. The place was almost empty, mind you. The table ordered a cornbread skillet to share. While it tasted good, this is way too much food. Seriously, it was like a cornbread birthday cake sliced for 6 slices. Huge. Our party had some serious eaters in it, yet quite a bit went to waste. Simply too much food. My father ordered a salad. It was not what I would call a salad, as it had one long piece of romaine lettuce on it and then some meat. Gross, and definitely a ripoff. Entrees were a mixed bag. While I cannot recall the exact names, the following dishes were ordered: 1) Hot pot fish (x2) 2) Brisket 3) Ribeye** 4) Spicy Penne in a Light Creamy Vodka sauce with chicken Hot pot fish was well-liked. Really good according to the two ladies who had it. My father ordered the ribeye, and he thought it was good, but "adequate." Nothing groundbreaking here, but nothing glaring, either. The brisket was universally panned. Brisket is supposed to be slow-cooked, imparting a very tender, melt-in-your-mouth texture. This "brisket" was deemed to really be sliced pot roast, as it was dry and chewy. The diner and his wife (she had a bite) were not happy. The penne ala vodka with chicken was also not what actually came out. There was no cream added to the sauce at all. This was straight-up red marinara sauce, not the classic pink sauce one would expect from a penne ala vodka dish. It was edible, but not what was ordered. Penne was really small in diameter, a little over-cooked, and the chicken was super dry. The sauce was NOT a "light creamy vodka sauce" as advertised, and instead was a marinara sauce. It wasn't awful, but had I known what I would be served, I would have ordered something else. Note on entrees: if you want to split an entree, they charge you $5+ to split. This is outrageous, even in Los Angeles (it happens, but it's not really common). This place is not of a caliber where this would be expected, and it reeked of pretension. For dessert, several bread puddings were ordered and split. No one was wowed; this is very average bread pudding. It had caramel drizzle on top, and it is honestly too sweet. The whipped cream on the side was loaded with confectioner's sugar and was deemed inedible by everyone. Each order of bread pudding was split by 2 people, though not one plate was finished more than 50%. This portion size was more out-of-control than the cornbread skillet. I don't like places that charge super high prices for mediocre-at-best food, while serving so much of it that much goes to waste. NO ONE could eat the portions at this restaurant as part of a healthy diet. This is also not health food. Service was slow and uneven, prices high, pretentious factor cranked up to level 12...just no. I'll waste my money on a place with better food than what I can make at home, thank you so much. **Edited to correct an inaccuracy. Ribeye is not brisket. Update: I just spoke with a few friends who recently dined here, and they had the same reaction to the penne pasta dish, though theirs didn't have chicken. Like me, they were expecting an item described as having a light, creamy sauce to actually have a light, creamy sauce...but instead they also received a chunky, tomato/marinara sauce. While not bad, it was not what was ordered. Maybe Northside Social needs to educate their chef on the menu, or maybe they should just change the menu to reflect what the chef feels like serving.

text: I really admire and commend the owner of this shop, Jean-Luc Labat.-only open about one week. Frog's is "organic" and "French style." I met a friend there for breakfast this morning about 10. I must say that the renovation of the space (used to be Paradise bakery) is very pleasing. The counter/display area is inviting and the offerings beautiful and very tempting. One orders at the register and either takes the food themselves or it is brought to you. Seating is indoors or out. ( in hindsight I am sorry I did not think to take the time to explain the difference to that young woman. It might have been helpful to her). Having not mastered the art of the French omelet myself, I am always on the lookout for any restaurant that serves them up that way. Otherwise, I really dislike them. So, my friend and I ordered 3 pastries between us and each had coffee which was decent but, for my taste, nothing very special. Despite our having our meal "in" the coffee was offered only in paper cups. There were no pitchers of dairy products, i.e. cream, milk to be had. Instead there were only those little, wasteful, and non-organic 1/2 and 1/2 single serves. Maybe they plan to correct this. The pastry: one plain croissant, one puff-pastry "twirl" with raisins, and and a kind of cake/muffin pastry made with blue corn meal and goat cheese. My friend found the latter to be dry and tasteless. I have to say I liked it a lot but it did lack flavor of the cheese. I could only taste the cornmeal. Serving with a pat of butter might have helped-none of our pastries came with butter or jam (which is $1.00 more). The croissant was okay, not notable. The raisin pastry was better, crispier on the outside and very flavorful. No one came by to ask how everything was. As my friend said, "I wouldn't go out of my way to go back." Now, maybe I will go back after the holidays and after the owners have had a chance to work out the kinks. (the cashier did now know how much a coffee refill was, e.g) They are in their infancy. text: Depending on the night, Denim is just one long, crowded hallway, and the DANCE FLOOR doesn't have lights - no disco lights, no crazy laser shows, only illumination from Walnut Street. There are several bars (three on the lower floor, one upstairs - upstairs is nice) that usually are mobbed during special events. The middle lounge area is moderately well-lit and you can buy a pricey bottle of liquor for $200 (minimum - check with them on current prices) if you want table service. (Last I checked, Tim Quinn was general manager and is willing to coordinate with you if you're interested.) The house DJ (Adam Bomb) can be good depending on the event du jour. Bartenders are friendly and will make whatever you want - I've dealt with Cindy (lower floor) multiple times, and Matthew (on the upper floor) who introduced me to a shot of Windex. The bouncers haven't ever given me a problem, and my friend said she saw one nursing a girl back to health after she harked all over the place. Smoking is a nasty habit, and I saw partygoers lighting up all over the place. Unsure if Denim takes advantage of the loophole that makes them exempt from no-smoking policies (which would be bad) or its patrons are ignorant (which would also be bad), but smelling like an ashtray is NOT what I want to be doing on my time off. It involved an in-town move, plus moving some items to storage, then months later, moving everything 300 miles away. I've used professional movers before and this company's service did not match other big names. And yes, it pains me to write a bad review (see my history, I rarely do it!) Lots of things went wrong: forgetting to pack a closet and drawers; two major billing errors (example: charging personal credit card and not work-issued credit card - yikes!); movers arriving late each of the three times we saw them; lost (and later found - thank goodness) my large living room rug. These are just the events off the top of my head. Yes, the actual movers (college students or recent grads) were friendly and pleasant to work with. My disappointment largely comes from the management/owners who never sincerely apologized for so many glitches throughout the entire four month ordeal. Coffee at these little breakfast places varies widely in quality, but this coffee was good. My omelet with toast and potatoes, plus small coffee, was $5.50 including tax. The upstairs seating area was unexpectedly pleasant, with upholstered chairs and natural light. I don't want to build up this restaurant too much. It was nothing more than it appears to be. I stopped in for quick breakfast and that's what I got. But I had nothing to complain about and the food turned out to be unexpectedly well-executed. text: I truly can't understand the 4 and 5 star reviews that the Old City Asian Bistro has received. I stumbled upon the bistro while trying to satisfy a late afternoon sushi craving- it was that pesky time of day when most of my go-to restaurants were closed to prepare for dinner. To begin with, the menu could be better. It is full of typos ("scollops"), and the chef's special rolls don't have descriptions of what is in them. I started with a bowl of miso soup, which was lukewarm, even though the waitress cautioned us about how hot it was. The soup tasted like it was from an instant miso packet, with a couple slices of green onions tossed in for good measure. For the sushi, I rolled the dice and chose the "spicy girl roll," and an order of ikura sushi. Now, I know it's typical to use the fish scraps or slightly lower quality fish in spicy rolls, but this was just disgraceful. It just did not taste right. The ikura was equally bad - I only ate one of the pieces that I ordered, as it was a bit mushy and tasted as though the ikura was past its prime. My boyfriend also got miso soup, and 2 rolls: a Philadelphia roll and something involving eel- perhaps a "double eel roll"? He reported almost no eel in the rolls, but said he didn't mind because it wasn't very good, either. The rolls that we both got were very small and unattractive, although like he said, neither of us would have wanted them to be larger. I will say that the dragon roll that my mother ordered looked presentable, but that's about the only positive thing I can say about the food. The wall behind the sushi bar was decorated nicely, and the waitress was very friendly, and refilled our water glasses often. Honestly, that's the best I can say for this place. Please give The Old City Asian Bistro a pass, and go to any of the other Asian restaurants within a 4 or 5 restaurants within a 2 block radius of here.

text: The only reason the Millennium gets two stars (instead of just one) is because we got it for pretty cheap. Then again, after we checked in, we knew why. It seems we weren't the only people who felt the Millennium couldn't do anything right. Complaints ranged from mysterious, inappropriate charges being added to bills to staff failing to come through on various requests. Our biggest issue was that the front desk refused to allow my husband to check in because the room was in my name (our last name is the same and the room was booked on a joint credit card that he had with him). Instead of offering a solution, the manager suggested my husband call our travel agent (um, what? we didn't book this with an agent!) and have them straighten it out because there was no way they were letting him into the room. When I was able to drop what I was doing and come over there, they carded me before they'd let me check in. Among the other issues: The garage was a nightmare thanks to the Cardinals game, and parking was pricey at $18/day. After all the hassle at the front desk we finally got up to our room to find that our key cards didn't even work. The room was tiny, old and had nothing but the most basic furnishings. The bathroom was only slightly bigger than the closet. And because the indoor pool is located in the center of the circular south wing, there are screaming children right outside your door all the time. The only positive comment the Millennium gets is the exceptional service we got from Larry the bellman. That guy understands customer service and did everything in his power to make our stay a little better. As a St. Louis native who recently moved to California, I've had the opportunity to come home and stay at a couple downtown hotels for various weddings and events. Do yourself a favor and book the Renaissance or the Crowne Plaza and don't waste a penny on this place.

text: We have been looking forward to eating here ever since we moved to Nashville. After several failed attempts and canceled reservations, we finally went to celebrate a birthday. To cut to the chase, the food was inconsistent. Not all of it was bad, but, at a place like The Standard, you would expect so much more of it to be good. And, unfortunately, the same could be said for the entire dining experience. The only memorable thing about the food was our appetizers. I had the grit cake with crayfish, which was really excellent. It was an imaginative interpretation of Southern cuisine. The grit cake was crispy with a wonderful flourish of corn and a nice sizable portion of crayfish. My dinner companion had the mushrooms in a pastry puff, which was also very good, even for me who does not normally like mushrooms. Now, if we would've stopped here, we would be raving about this restaurant. Unfortunately, we proceeded like normal folk to the entrees. I got their house specialty, Bacon-Bacon, which is supposed to be a bacon wrapped pork loin. However, I wouldn't call it a pork loin or a medallion or anything I would've expected to see bacon wrapped around. It was more like a thin pork chop (reminded me of what I would buy at Aldi or Kroger in bulk meat) with barbecue sauce(!!) on it and plated on top of an unappetizing mix of bacon bits, beans and corn. I guess that's the succotash. And my entrée was better than my dinner companion's, who had the seared duck with a confusing mix of over-seasoned asparagus tips, undercooked black beans and a corn fritter. The duck was also stringy and fatty. Both of us ordered a glass of wine and we both ended up with our second choice since there were no open bottles of our first choices. Okay. The service was fine and polite, and we never felt rushed. However, there seemed to be only 1 or 2 waiters and a bus boy the entire night, resulting in a lot of rushing from table to table and brief queries about our food and if we needed anything. The outside of the restaurant looks very charming with its small courtyard in front. However, the ambiance inside of the restaurant and dining area lacks warmth and intimacy. And I realize I'm being very nit-picky here but I was bothered by their "artwork." Here you have a historic, mid-19th century townhouse and they have a bunch of black-and-white photographs of women's bodies from the neck down. Not nude or erotic in any manner, but just ... really cheesy. It reminded me of a woman's Casual Corner catalog. How about some framed photos of historic sites in Nashville, photos of the restaurant being renovated, or even photos of past and prominent Nashvilleans? The Standard offers itself up to be a fine dining experience, but it just doesn't succeed in enough categories. Call me fastidious or overly critical, but, if you're going to get all gussied up and pony up $100 for two for dinner, wouldn't you expect more?
label: NEG

Dry, tasteless & over priced Atmosphere: awful, horrible Kids: don't take them to this place We also tried Pats which seemed down to earth.
label: NEG

text: Not my absolute favorite bookstore, as I'm a romance reader and they're admittedly on the slim side for romance pickings, but it's a great little bookshop that definitely earns its community support. The staff is knowledgable and supportive and the selection in most genres is excellent -- especially children's, YA, literary fiction. Special ordering is a breeze, and, unless you go on a busy evening, the rear lot provides some parking. They also host a lot of signings and talks.
label: POS

text: My boyfriend and I went to Luna Bella on Friday night. We were on our way somewhere else, drove by and decided to give it a try. The front desk was very friendly. As the hostess led us to our table she encountered a walkway blocked by a server so, she threaded us in and out of a few tables to get us to ours. In doing this we had to sidle by a table of diners and as I squeezed by, one of the gentlemen went to put down his menu and his elbow came in contact with my leg. It was not a soft bump for either of us and he turned and gave me a very angry look as I apologized. What's my point? The tables are too close together in the main dining room! We were seated in a back room that looks out onto the intersection of Fort Lowell and Swan - well it should look out - all of the plantation shutters were closed up tight - giving the effect of being in a banquet hall- While an intersection isn't the best view - it would have taken some of the emphasis off the inside - which was very "golden girls" retirement community dining hallesque. There was also a very strong smell of fish, cheese or something malodorous. I have to say I am not a big fan of restaurants that use carpet in their dining rooms - hardwood or tile are much more appealing from an odor and hygiene perspective. We also noted they are using scented candles on the tables - while I would prefer glade to old fish - it's still a no no. The menu was not quite as varied as I would have liked but, we settled on the fried artichokes to share, a rib eye for him and pasta bolognese for me. I had a nice glass of Guenoc Pinot Grigio - and we waited for the artichokes. We were served a large portion - which is often not a good sign. The breading was pretty heavy, they weren't warm and the accompanying sauce was a bit bland. I actually enjoyed the undressed mixed veggies on the plate more than the artichokes - yellow peppers, some radishes. I was really looking forward to my pasta -the menu had a paragraph about the chef, Steve Schultz, stating that he had worked and trained in Europe and even more specifically, Switzerland. Having travelled and lived in Europe, I thought this was a good sign that I would get a proper bolognese. What I did get was an enormous bowl - huge -monstrous - of pasta with huge chunks of sausage in it. Bolognese when done right has a very fine mix of veal, pork, beef, carrots - no sausage. There are probably a hundred different variations of bolognese, but I have never had it with sausage. The menu stated "chopped beef & veal" - no sausage. Anyway, it wasn't horrible or inedible but it also wasn't pasta bolognese. It had so much sausage and such big chunks it seemed like some of the pieces were still pink inside eww. I almost forgot to mention, some of the pasta was cooked stuck together and hard - pasta faux pas - not al dente. On to the rib eye - my boyfriend thought it was great - the gorgonzola gummy goo, i mean risotto, it was sitting on was not liked by either of us. Conclusion - would I go back? Not for dinner. They told us they have happy hour in the bar and am a lot less picky when I am getting things at half off.
label: NEG

text: Everything here is sexy. The giggling hostesses are sexy. The decor is sexy. The waitress, who set down my appetizer and whispered my order so close to my ear that I could feel her breath, is very sexy. The food was equally sexy. My warm octopus salad with pomegranate sauce (I remember because this is what the waitress recited to me) was, yes, warm, and the sweet sauce was just enough to balance the inherent dryness of octopus. The striped bass I ordered was served with popcorn. I became confused. I tried the dish. The popcorn flavor meshed too well with the other flavors. I became delighted. A strong Riesling complemented everything nicely. Most restaurants tend to either focus on food quality or presentation. The Striped Bass happens to be among the few restaurants that prepares well-made dishes and manages to present them in refreshingly creative ways.
label: POS

text: I agree. This place DOES suck. The atmosphere itself is a little dingy. And the food is spectacularly unimpressive.
label: NEG

text: My friend and I went to First Friday tonight, and this was the ONLY destination I wanted to get to. Turns out I'm a freaking genius about these things. The place was loaded with art ~ and not the freaky, weird local kind that confuses you. There was some really amazing stuff. The best part: the bank has lots of nooks and crannies for you to explore, with individual artists and groups showing work in each place. (There's even a little bookstore, which is awesome since words are important too.) The only reason it's not a 5: we wanted to buy art but couldn't figure out how to do that. Somebody please tell me how to give you my money?!?!?!
label: POS

text: Went here for dinner during a conference with 3 others from work and we all loved this place. The service was amazing. The food was delicious. The charcuterie platter, the deviled eggs, crabcake latke, carrot soup.....loved everything we sampled. Great atmosphere for a relaxing and thoroughly enjoyable dining experience.
label: POS

text: We all know the stereotype of the Irish - Drink, drink, drink. Fight. Rinse. Repeat. It seems the staff at Finnigan's Wake takes this to the next level; they actually just aspire to be the biggest assholes in a 2-mile radius (success!). If you are a bro and looking for a good place to release all that testosterone, give it a go. Otherwise, take heed, my friends.
label: NEG

text: Old people mexican food. Ill stick with the microwavable dinners. Try El Charro downtown or guadalahara grill first.
label: NEG

text: A John Besh Bistro. Very high quality ingredients, expertly executed at reasonable prices. I'd recommend the boudin noir, country pate, rabbit and duck liver pate, Luke salad, beet salad, and, of course, P&J oysters. I didn't care for the hard croutons the rabbit pate was served with though. One of the best values in New Orleans is Happy Hour at Luke from 4 to 6. It's hard to beat $5 martinis and $3 a dozen for gulf oysters. Although we were seated without a reservation on Christmas night, generally for dinner I'd recommend a reservation if you want to be seated at a table. The bar is first come, first served. Service is pleasant enough.
label: POS

text: Wow this place makes me miss Florida. Real pit BBQ and real sauce YUMM Wish they would open one out here
label: POS

text: Unfortunately, I'm not a 72 year old, uber-fabulous old woman in a Chanel suit, dining with my liver-spotted husband at Chez Leon. I don't come from old money, I still have all my tastebuds. I've read nearly everything Anthony Bourdain has written, and I'm not fooled by Chez Leon. My $12 house champagne cocktail was about 2 oz of dry-ish champagne with a sliced strawberry. My duck a l'orange would have made Eric Ripert set fire to his chef's whites because pseudo-French people are still allowed to make food this boring. My friend's bouillabaisse was so dull I think I remember him yawning a lot during the meal. The bread on the table was probably 3 days old, my rice was undercooked, and the highlight of the meal was slicing my duck and cracking duck jokes in my head. However, this place is perfect for the aforementioned Chanel suited lady and her husband. I hope to be her someday, and if I live in St. Louis, I'll probably be here 5 nights a week.
label: NEG

text: When I shower with the D&L "stress relief" soap all my trouble wash down the drain. I love the store. I love the staff. And I love the free samples. At their recent in-store soirée they even had cocktails! Every time I go in there I just can't help but leave with a smile on my face. And their classes (Sunday School or whatever it is) are such fun! I have gotten so many friends and co-workers hooked on this stuff too. Once you try D&L there is no way to go back to regular soap.
label: POS

text: Zama might just be my new favorite sushi joint in Philly. Granted I went with someone who knew Zama, the chef/owner. So we probably got some special treatment. But even so, a great all-around experience. Cool decor, friendly professional service, but with personality. But most importantly, stellar sushi - excellent quality fish, creative rolls, unusual sauces. We also had the tempura vegetable appetizer, a scallop appetizer, the wasabi salt edamame - all delicious. Even the desserts were fantastic - way beyond the traditional green tea ice cream: Fuji apple crisp, molten chocolate cake, creme brulee! We will definitely return...
label: POS

text: I used to love New Samosa, until it broke my heart. Last year, I had a habit of popping by for lunch once a week. It provided a whole buffet and menu full of options, which as a vegetarian, came as a rare treat. Also, the salad bar was always fresh. In recent months I'd found myself too busy to keep up with my New Samosa weekly ritual. When I found myself in the neighborhood yesterday, I had to stop by. What a shocker! They now serve meat and half of the buffet items I had previously enjoyed had been nixed in favor of meat dishes - which were NOT clearly labeled. There was not even any veggie pakora. The lettuce on the salad bar was starting to wilt and brown and the tomatoes were also beginning to go bad. The raita didn't look too hot either. To top it all off, they raised the price of the lunch buffet by $1. I don't know if they are under new management, but this wasn't the same restaurant I made my weekly lunch spot last year. Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be going back. I need to find a new Indian spot with decent veg options and a fresh salad bar.
label: NEG

text: This place is amazing. It's priced very fairly and the portions aren't so big that you're in a food coma when you leave, nor are you still hungry. The quality of fish is crazy awesome -- it's some of the best fish I've had. My boyfriend and I split one of the sushi combos (comes with miso soup & ginger salad) with a California roll, 7 pieces of sushi, and 12 pieces of sashimi for $24.95, and it was totally worth it. We also got a second bowl of miso soup for free. The service was very fast and our waitress and the chefs were super friendly.
label: POS

text: Well, I would have to say its not the greatest Italian restaurant I've been to. It is a nice place with a nice ambiance. We went on a Friday night and there was a nice gentleman playing the accordian, which was nice and pleasant. To start, we had calamari, which was good. The seafood fettucini was pretty good as well. We also had the chicken cacciatore. The chicken was ok, but it was a little dry...but I guess that's expected of a chicken breast. Now, to the downsides. I can't say too much of the service at Viggiano's. The waitress was very slow to serve us. I don't know how long we had to wait just to get our bread and to wait for her to take our order. And the bread...it was a cold piece of bread and it was wrapped in a paper napkin. I would have easily mistaken the paper napkin for trash. And when we asked for more bread, it didn't come for the longest time. Our food took a long time to come out as well. All in all, this is a nice family style joint. We found this restaurant to be on the pricier side for the amount of food we got. And the service needs to be improved upon tremendously. We're sticking with Maggiano's next time.
label: NEG

text: I had a root canal procedure at this dental office under the care of Dr. Lawrence Ufberg. He was extremely unprofessional and I was left with a sore mouth, most of my tooth missing and extremely annoyed. First of all, upon consultation, he gave me the choice of a root canal or pulling the tooth, which would be "faster," he said. My appointment was for a Friday afternoon and apparently Dr. Ufberg was planning to go on vacation immediately after work and seemed genuinely annoyed that my appointment was right before his vacation and kept mentioning how annoyed he was. The entire visit took 4 hours and the care given to my tooth was minimal, and much of that tooth is missing, unlike root canals I had by other endodontists. During my procedure, he cursed- not mild curses- when complaining about other patients to his dental assistant as if I wasn't sitting right there in his chair. Then, when he was finished with me, he exclaimed in an annoyed voice "Well, you really made me work for my money today!" but not in a laughing, it's a joke kind of way. I do not believe this is any way to act to a patient who is in your care and giving you a sizable amount of money, too!
label: NEG

text: I agree with reviewer Dana-il, the hummus is good - and I don't even like hummus that much. I won't say it's the best I've had, but what do I know? Martha Stewart's version with no tahini is my personal fave. That's crazy and perhaps some sort of blasphemery, I know. The baba ganoush was really tasty, though, and I usually never like that stuff. The falafel was tasty but terribly greasy. The Lebanese tea with pine nuts is a curious drink but really satisfying. If the service had been better, my friend would've ordered a second tall one. The service was BAD! We were told to seat ourselves when we walked in, but then no one came to our table for 15 minutes - no drinks, no menus, no nothin. We had to get up and steal some takeout menus from the front counter. It was a slow Wednesday night, so there's just no excuse for that.
label: NEG

text: Big bowl trip to the salad bar for 5 bucks is doable. The noisy games are not. Bring the kids for pizza a fun but you'll get what you pay for at Luigi's and that's not much. I've only been for lunch on week days so I can't comment on what may well be a packed Saturday at noon but weekdays are not slow. That said, the kids behind the counter taking your order seem to want to be anywhere but here. Casual conversations between them (too casual) leave little room to take your order. There's a large game room making more noise though. I suggest you sit in the right side dinning room if you don't want to hear the bells and whistles. The pizza is OK for lunch and the salad bar is what you'd expect, better of both can be found. I'll be back when the mood strikes but only for lunch and never on a weekend and not for take out pie.
label: NEG

text: Circles has been a favorite spot in Apollo Beach since a friend introduced it to me a few years ago. The atmosphere inside is perfect for a romantic dinner and the prices are reasonable for the quality. My tendencies lean toward seafood and Circles does not disappoint. The lobster bisque and Maryland crab cakes are excellent. The crab cakes have a decent amount of back fin meat with just the right amount of seasoning. The wine selection will please most palates. There is outdoor dining that overlooks the water and is nice for having a drink or enjoying the atmosphere if you don't mind the occasional smoker. There are also nights with live bands if you feel like dancing. There is plenty of room for large groups, especially outdoors.
label: POS

text: I have been to many Whole Paycheck stores throughout the nation from the Mothership in Austin to some very third rate locations in Mesa, AZ. On that scale the Tampa store rates at the top of the lower third. Weak bulk section, laughable 'bakery' (all bread in plastic wrap with soft or old crust), very limited flours/grains selection etc...this has been clearly designed for the Tampa population who still has to wake up to gourmet foods. Anyway, as it stands right now, a good Publix location is almost on par with this store, and there is not much reason to venture out to it.
label: NEG

text: Schlafly's is a really popular place in the spring, summer, and fall, probably due to its outdoor patio. It's popularity and unimpressive food is why I'm giving it two stars. It was my choice to come here on a Saturday night, so I put my patience on (I really have none, normally). My bf and I approached the host to put our name on the list. I understood that they were busy, but the guy was a total scrooge. "Why aren't you happy to see me!?" I thought. He barely even looked up to acknowledge our presence. Whatever. The wait was only about 15 minutes because they put us in the corner in a two-seater, next to two other couples within breathing room. Frickin' hate those. I would have asked for a different spot, but there really were none. Another thing: this place is ridiculously LOUD. I don't know why everyone was screaming at each other, but I had to repeat everything I said to the significant other. I am not exaggerating. The food was okay. Rather plain. I had the black bean burger which was served with artificially dyed tortilla chips. Nothing exciting. Our server was alright. We didn't see him much because of how busy it was. We tried to scarff the food down as quick as possible so that we could get as far away from the sensory overload as possible...I don't think I'll be back to visit anytime soon, and if I do, I'll make sure it's not on a busy Saturday night. p.s. the parking here is a bitch.
label: NEG

text: Short and sweet - this place is terrific! Go for the lobster bisque and grab one of the chef specials. You can't go wrong! Call ahead as it is busy during the season.
label: POS

text: Have you ever known that having a good meal would soon be difficult to come by. So you have the opportunity, on your last day for a few to have something you love.. this was my situation when I decided to go to el fuego. Today ( I went yesterday ) I'm getting my last 2 wisdom teeth removed. So I decided to have one of my favorite foods ever, a vegetarian burrito! Instead of going to one of my usual places I yelped burritos and saw that el fuego was around the corner. I went in . . It happened to be happy hour. Which meant 2$ chips & Guac , which was actually terrible, the chips were lackluster and the guacamole was missing something. The Burrito was OK, they don't know how to wrap a burrito so it doesn't close properly. I stood in line. was asked the type of beans I wanted and then the girl behind the counter just decided that I of course wanted chicken so that's what she gave me.. So I said I didnt ask for chicken... she said " YOU don't want chicken?" I said NO, so she said sorry what kind of burrito you want, I said vegetarian, and you know she had the nerve to try the chicken off the tortilla and make me a vegetarian burrito with that? Then I had to tell her I DONT eat meat, and even if I did that's not acceptable . At that point you'd think I'd cut my losses and walk out, but for some reason I did not. HA! I get to the end the guy says for here or to go I say to go because I knew I wasn't going to eat the entire thing so I wanted a bag, I then ordered a strawberry margarita. The guy who you pay said we only make the margaritas for eat in customers, I said I am eating in, and he said oh I thought you said to go.. blah blah.. he got all pissy because he couldnt understand why someone would want a bag. It was mediocre. 4$ frozen eh not bad I'll get over it . In general their service is terrible, their prices are cheap, and their food is mediocre at best. none of those are reasons for me to go back.
label: NEG

text: Shangri La is such a disappointment. It started out good enough, but the last few times I was there over the past year or two it's been a pretty awful experience. Service took an absurdly long time and we were one of three couples in the restaurant...and there were at least two servers. 15 minutes to get drinks, our starter was totally forgotten about, they were out of almost every one of the side options, and our server totally seemed like she was on drugs. It took us 50 minutes to get our food (two sandwiches) and both of them were wrong. I always get their veggie ruben but it's really slipped in quality and they're always out of the asian slaw i used to get it with. Their other food sounds good on the menu but is never put together well and always seems soggy. The veggie burger I had there awhile ago was good though and I suppose there's a chance I've just caught them on off days on my past few visits. I really want to like Shangri La. I live nearby, don't eat meat, and love the idea of being able to walk to a reasonably priced veggie food joint for a quick bite, but I'm not sure I'll be back to give them another chance after the last time.
label: NEG

text: I've been to the Pub many many times in my 8 years of working in Conshy. For birthday parties, going away dinners, happy hours...you name it and we've celebrated it at the Pub. They've done a good job of expanding the bar to 3 levels over the years and able to accommodate large crowds of people. They even have an upstairs that was part of the original establishment that I don't think they ever use except for private parties As Carrie E mentions, parking in the area can be a bitch (be extra careful of meters and timed parking spaces...they give out tickets very quickly after your time expires). I recommend parking a few blocks up off of Fayette on 3rd or 4th and walk down the hill. It's an easy walk down the hill when sober and an easier walk back up it when you have a few in you. The beer selection on tap is average. They have the standards plus a few atypical Belgian brews from time to time. Food is consistent and good. I'd recommend this place more for lunch because the menu reads more like a lunch menu with alot of sandwiches and pasta dishes. I'm a big fan of the Fayette Chicken and also the Lobster Ravioli. Kristine like the Eggplant Parm sandwich with the "buttery buns", as she calls them. They offer a lunch and dinner size on all of the pastas, so you are able to portion your meal if you so desire.
label: POS

text: Noodle city is very homely. You can always get a table. Offers vegetarian dishes and Chinese dishes too. You get a good amount of food and the price is decent. The owner has a really deep voice and she tries to be funny but most of the time you just don't know what she is saying. One time she rushed my friend and I out cause they were close to closing.
label: POS

text: i Have been to mad river many times before its Huge with like 2 rooms and is always packed. With great music,strong drinks i always end up sweating it out through whatever funny t shirt or blazer i am wearing at the time..always a good time in manayunk.........WAIT....the other mad River ....in olde city?? oh....yea t.....hat a very different story.. II ll admit a few things here, 1) Its not favorite my place in olde city,2)i was fooled into going there thinking that the mad river in manayunk is pretty damn good so i cant wrong ,right?...The only good thing about this bar are the bartenders. They really keep the drinks flowing to an often unruly crowd of college people,flowing and strong. Otherwise this bar is OK at best. If you are looking to hang out with your friends in a large group (like i am) then this is the place for you. But if you are looking for anything else ,be it good music (not really),Girls(Sausage party) or just nice setting (pretty dark and dank) its not for you. It pretty good to get black out drunk really quick and move on. Its a bar crawl bar...you certain wouldnt post up there for the night at any point. Unless of course it was at the end of the night lol
label: NEG

text: Love Brandy. I have gotten pedicures at another place that was supposed to be "chic" but instead was uncomfortable, rushed, and expensive for the service given. Brandy is absolutely wonderful, takes her time, and does an amazing job no matter if you get gels or just polish. Even if the atmosphere is more spa than chic, I'll take a good pedicure over a modern atmosphere any day!
label: POS

text: I have been a fan devoted to the success of this restaurant. I have eaten there many times from the place on Veterans Blvd. in Kenner to the Citrus Ave store in Elmwood and now to the Harahan place. But it seems to be deteriating, primarily in service and to a significant degree in food preparation.. The wait staff is "new high school drop-out" types and untrained; their training is probably dinning out at the Red Lobster...arriving in their pickups. You get the picture. The last meal I ordered was a pasta special which arrived cold as a corpse. We ordered a coconut cream pie which was dry as a bone and the merange was hard as a rock. The waitress said that is the way it is supposed to be tha that she had sold this pie all day and had no complaints. Quiet customers or just wanting to get back to their pickup trucks parked outside? Regretfully, I have to say this is a "pass" and I don't believe it is long for this world as a restaurant. If you plan to go there, check and see if it is still open.
label: NEG

text: This place was great. Stopped here on a cross country trip from California to Virginia. I was with my dad and we were sketchy about where to eat. We obviously were'nt familiar with the area and weren't sure where a good place to eat was. We pulled into downtown and headed to this place. I found it on Yelp. It was awesome. Some of the best BBQ I've had in a while. IF I was ever back in Nashville I would come back to this restaurant. No matter what you order you can't go wrong. Everything is a safe bet. So eat to your hearts content.
label: POS

text: We were out with friends who were starving and we were on the north end of State Street. The outside of State & A made it look good. I was sooo wrong. The service was actually pretty average. No real complaints there. They were also not busy though. I think most of the complaints were in the interior decor and the food. We sat outside and that was just okay. My fish and chips were bland and below average. My boyfriend got the nachos with chicken and he got food poisoning from them. I would say that I don't plan on going back.
label: NEG

text: Okay here's the deal. I don't live in New Orleans but I wish I did purely to be closer to Sweet Pea and Tulip! I've never left empty handed and usually save up for weeks before a visit. LOVE is the word that comes to mind. It's like Sweet Pea is the fresher, newer version of my closet. The owner is always darling. I only come about once a year but he recognizes me right away. Maybe it's because I've tried on the entire store several times. Anyway, he's incredibly helpful and will pull merchandise for you. If you're like me, you'll try on everything you even mildly like which makes your fellow accomplices bored. They have a really comfy couch to just plop yourself down on. I can't think of anything bad to say about this place! Please go, and shop in this wonderful boutique. Besides, spending money rebuilds the city and helps the economy. Fun Fact: Sweet Pea is his cheeky Chihuahua
label: POS

text: as an out of towner, if you look at what a Po Boy really is - a sandwich, then it may or may not sound very exciting. but the real exciting part is when you consider some of the magical things they can put INTO your Po Boy, Fried Catfish, Fried Shrimp, Sausage Pork or Alligator Links, Roast Beef with Gravy, and on and on. our mini group tried stopping by on Tuesday of the week that i was there. oops. closed. so we stopped by again Wednesday, because our worksite was a few minutes from here, and this place was poppin. they have a fairly good sized seating area, indoor and outdoor, but it was lunchtime and it was packed. I ordered a Fried Catfish Po Boy with a side of Sweet Potato Fries, and they have Glass Bottled Barq's~! the food came out promptly and i couldn't wait to dig in. the Sweet Potato Fries were pretty good (i kinda wished some of the pieces were a bit thicker) and the Po Boy was equally as good. added a couple squirts of Louisiana Hot Sauce and i was in heaven. now since they serve Po Boys in practically every restaurant, corner market, gas station, and even Popeye's, there has to be some factors that vary, in order to compare which ones are "better" than others. of course, this is Yelp, i'll be the first to admit that taste is subjective and can easily hinge on one's personal preferences. with that in mind, when it comes to bread for my sandwiches, i like French rolls that have a light, flaky crust on the outside, but soft and pillowey, yet lightly toasted on the inside. they have good rolls at Parkway, but they have a slightly chewier crust on the outside. this is good by itself, but it's not my favorite because if you don't bite into your Po Boy with the right technique, it'll squeeze all your Po Boy fixins out onto your tray. this did happen a little towards the end of my Po Boy, but it wasn't a huge problem. so that was a long winded version of "yea the bread has a flaky crust but it's a little more chewy here" stop by! it's good! the bottle opener is under the front counter :)
label: POS

text: I've never come here for the standard lunch that's getting bad reviews here, but regularly stop on the other side of the counter where they have the prepared spinach pies and sweets. The spinach & cheese pie (spanikopita style) is perfect for a quick, hearty snack and is extremely tasty. They also occasionally have samosas, which are absolutely fabulous. Finally, I recommend any of the sweets. They have baklava, kataifi and homemade havalah. All absolutely delicious. As for the service, I've had mixed service, but it's generally been a more positive experience than negative experience.
label: POS

text: If this place isn't a divey hole in the wall restaurant then it's a glorified taco stand. There are three inside tables that are about as big as the 'kitchen' (it's so small!) and a much bigger plastic-awning-covered patio area. If it's crowded, and it will be, you might have to wait for a table that you then wipe down yourself. I lead with that because it seems enough people go there with different expectations only to walk out somewhat dismayed. With that said and hopefully understood....La Super-Rica rocks!!! I won't name specific menu items (ok, I will mention one, a special - the Tamals are filled with veggies and covered in a creme sauce and are so fresh and tasty) because there are so many great options. I was there with a 'local' (can one be considered local if they weren't born there and don't live there now?) who picked out a few of their faves, all of which were delish, but I am sure that anything would have been good. Everything, including the tortillas, is prepared right in front of you. It's all very fresh (the place does serious bizness and is small so there's literally no room for stuff to sit around) and ultimately I walked out feeling like I had gotten a great deal on a bunch of great food (and a beer). I would say that without a doubt I will hit up Super-Rica the next time I'm in SB.
label: POS

text: I haven't a clue how this place has gotten a single good review. Perhaps it's the location because it's in the Central West End, a popular hub of activity in St. Louis but that's about all it has going for it and even that is bit questionable. When I ate there recently, it was a beautiful Autumn day, and we sat outside. Here are a few things about atmosphere, some, admittedly, not their fault or circumstantial. The sidewalk seating is street side and against the exterior of the building leaving a thoroughfare of sidewalk traffic constantly streaming by. There is construction going on across the street and at one point a large box came off the 4th story and hit a car driving by. There is also a good deal of street noise, construction noise and cell phone talkers walking past. All of that is somewhat forgivable. Now let me tell you about the unbelievable unforgivably BAD interpretation of "Mexican" food. They have a fixed menu of 40 items ranging from burritos, enchiladas, tacos, appetizers and so on. Your dining experience begins with commercially manufactured tortilla chips (one would think that perhaps an establishment named "Tortillaria" might consider, oh, I don't know, making their own tortilla chips - not the case - or if they did make them they failed miserably) and "salsa". The salsa was some sort of redish-pink water with bits of what I assume was tomato in it. It would have served me better to have dipped my bland chip in water than the salsa. They do have a salsa bar with other varieties of condiments. We picked up the "hot" salsa. It's not hot. And a green version that I can't quite place the flavor. I didn't hate it but I certainly didn't like it. My dinning partner and I described it as "unusual" and we both thought that perhaps there was a hint of mustard in it??? Mustard + salsa = shame on you. Perhaps it wasn't mustard so we'll leave that one at "unusual". I ordered the "Enchiladas Rojas" : Corn tortillas filled with chicken tinga and cheese, then baked in an earthy ancho chile sauce... Again, the corn tortillas were not homemade. I see a pattern emerging. The chicken was flavorless and tasted as if it were boiled, dried under a heat lamp and then shredded. And the "earthy ancho chile sauce" simply tasted earthy. It was red. They got that right. My dinning companion ordered the "Barbocoa Burrito". I sampled it. It was big. Massive even. It's flavor profile was better and it was edible. However, I still feel the beef was under-seasoned and frankly, you could save yourself a few dollars, walk a block away and have a better barbocoa experience at Qdoba (and do not, dear reader, think that that is an endorsement of Qdoba). I know this is the mid-west and my too many years of authentic Mexican food in both California and Texas have spoiled me - hey... I still crave Taco Johns now and then, but Tortillaria is simply lacking in anything near authentic. My advice: drive down to Cherokee Street, find a place with a Spanish sounding name, if no one there speaks English even better and order something you can't pronounce correctly (it will probably cost somewhere between $1-3) and you'll be truly satisfied.

text: L'Oca's open kitchen comes through time and again with consistently well-balanced and executed dishes. They've done a nice job in rehabbing a corner beer distributor space across from Eastern State Pen. with large windows that open out in summer and recessed and pendant lighting. The chef and his staff are committed to taking great care with their ingredients, from the deftly-handled salads to the richness of their game or pasta (half of which are homemade) preparations. On more than one occasion I've been blown away by the quiet perfection of their soups-- which are always simple, but manage to clarify the savory pleasure of a fresh young leek or humble beans in a minestrone. The owner Jack is always there, vigilantly supervising the service, which is pleasant in its tidy coordination of various servers looking after your needs. Most Philly BYOs fall off in quality after their initial year in business, but it's nice to see that in its commitment to standards, L'Oca manages to bilk the trend. What I've loved: valeriana and crescione/rughetta salads, gnocchetti armenville with sage butter, seasonal soups, saffron spaghetti with scallops and prosciutto, fresh pappardelle with goose ragu (only seasonal), and rabbit loin braised in milk. Mr. Chiu in Columbia, IL was excellent, however, too far for this South Saint Louis resident. That said, I highly suggest you consider Bo Fung for your next Chinese food meal. Everything seemed fresh. As I mentioned above, the Crab Rangoon are sweet; you may not need that red sweet and sour sauce for these. I had egg rolls, pork fried rice, crab rangoon, and a sampling of broccoli beef, which was probably the freshest I have had. I don't get broccoli beef too often, but was quite pleased with this one. Something I did want to mention, if you order more than $16 worth of items, you get a bag of Crab Rangoon. I didn't know this, so I went home with THREE bags of Crab Rangoon. Yeah, I got my taste cup and boy am I glad I did - took one bite of the so-called green tea and wondered if there even WAS a flavor aside from 'cold' to it. Seriously, it didn't taste like anything. Their Reese's flavor tasted like peanuty chemicals and their chocolate had that bad chemical aftertaste (although of all the flavors it seemed like the creamiest of the bunch). The only decent flavor is their plain tart, but that one has an icy consistency that melts pretty quickly. Do I recommend this place? HELLS NO! I realize there's only one other place in Philadelphia that offers froyo, and its waaaay down on South Street, but seriously people, don't waste your money on froyo that tastes horrible - go get some gelato or ice cream at the many other fabulous locations. text: I am floored, floored, floored by the bad reviews of this place. It is absolutely the real deal. The authentic New Orleans/Creole cooking experience. How do I know? Well, I was treated to dinner here by a friend who is a New Orleans native and a fairly prominent resident and we had the meal of life. Of all the places he could have chosen, he chose Olivier's for a reason, and it's because Olivier's is New Orleans. In all my visits to New Orleans, pre and post-Katrina, this is the best meal I've ever had in town. We started with the quintessential New Orleans drink -- the Sazerac. Rye Whiskey, Absinthe and Bitters? This is a grown folks drink. You've been warned. Great way to cleanse your palate before the meal. Then we had the gumbo sampler, which was sublime. I'm not sure I knew there were different types of gumbo, and Olivier's gives you three, including a file gumbo that was passed down by the owner's mother. Also, try the eggplant appetizer -- lightly breaded and absolutely delicious. Our entrees ranged from rabbit to shrimp creole and it was outstanding. My only "complaint" is that I thought my shrimp creole could have been a little spicier but it was still great. Outside of the food, I loved the atmosphere. The owner himself comes out to every table to greet guests, thank them for coming and makes menu recommendations. You definitely "feel" the love when you're at Olivier's. THIS is the kind of New Orleans establishment we should be patronizing. Get off of Bourbon Street, stay out of Emeril's and come support a native who is doing this food better than anything you'll see on TV. When I'm back in New Orleans, Olivier's will be one of my first stops!

text: Went there on a Saturday evening around 5:30 or 6 for dinner with the boyf. We walked in, and because there was no hostess, a waitress standing at the bar told us we could sit wherever we like. The building itself is really cool looking. But not cool enough for me to sit there for ten minute still waiting for MENUS. We were going to get up to go somewhere else. There were at least five waiters/waitresses walking around, some just leaning on the bar, who completely ignored us. I finally had to ask a waitress for one! As she was bringing the menus over, another waitress was asking her something, and she stopped in front of our table having the conversation, just holding the menus. For the love of god, JUST GIVE US THE MENUS SO WE CAN PAY YOU MONEY. After we got our menus, a waitress (no introduction, no welcome to Dock Street, no how are you doing...) asked what we'd like to drink, and came back a minute later to take our order. I asked for the vegan pizza with pesto. I asked her if the pesto WAS, in fact, vegan, and if there was any parmesan cheese in it. "No, it's vegan... well... the last week... I'll double check for you." She passed us a few times and brought out our appetizers, and I had to ask HER if she double checked. "Yeah, it is (vegan)." The hummus I got was very good. It was topped with kalamata olives (yuuuummmm), red peppers, and walnuts. I was hoping the walnuts would actually be mixed in with the hummus, but it was still really good. It had a nice zesty spice to it, which I really liked. And I don't usually like red peppers, but these were marinated and roasted juuuust enough. About three minutes later our personal pizzas were brought out, as well. We hadn't even halfway finished the appetizers! There was barely enough room for our things on the table! It's a good thing we were sitting on a ledge near the food prep, because we had to put some of our plates on there. The pizzas were ok. The vegan pizza could have used some olives for fat, but the pesto was very good. I couldn't detect any cheese in it (the only reason I bring this up is because of a previous review about parm in the pesto). My boyfriend got the marghertia pizza. He said it was ok. The best part of my meal was the hummus. I'll NEVER be back here. It's a shame, because we reeeaaallly love microbrews. We didn't get to sample any beer this trip, and we had hoped it would be worth it to come by for a night out. If the service is that crappy on a Saturday evening when it's half EMPTY, I can only imagine out long it would take on a Saturday night when it's full of drunk people. On a related note, if anyone can recommend some good microbreweries in Philadelphia (other than Triumph) with some decent vegan and omnivore options, as well as servers who don't seem bothered that you'd actually like to EAT at a restaurant (the horror!), holla at ya girl.

text: OK, I admit it: I'm an Indian food noob. My first experience with Indian was in college, and I didn't really start to acquire a taste until I lived in Ireland / UK about 15 years ago. While it is a fusion restaurant, presenting Indian and Thai dishes (and mixes in between), the food is most definitely authentic. On a night out with my wife's brother and his wife, we walked into a restaurant with very much a new-agey "fusion" vibe. Decorated in deep hues of red and orange, with a low level of lighting that I expect at a restaurant. Very clean, and a place that invited me to come in and eat. We had a bread selection to start off, which is an enormous plate of various kinds of naan. As a chili-head, I definitely liked the potato naan, which had a very spicy kick. For the entree, I went with my old favorite: Lamb Vindaloo. For those who haven't had it, its a SPICY Lamb and tomato dish. Its presented at Spice in a small copper pot (best way I can describe it) with a nice side of jasmine rice. Definitely spicy, but not so much that I couldn't enjoy the burn. As for prices, I disagree heartily with the earlier Yelper who said this is a place only for lunch. The most expensive entree was $23, with our entrees costing around $18 each. I consider that VERY inexpensive, particularly for the quality of the food. Service was OK - They were efficient, but didn't really stop to talk much. But, I was never left wanting for water or if I needed something, so as far as covering the important stuff they did fine. We will definitely be going back when we have an urge for a bit of Indian cuisine. Another fine entry into the restaurant boom in West Chester (which again begs the question from me: where the heck were all of these awesome places when I went to school there 20 years ago???)

text: A buffet place that doesn't quite match up... A private party on a Sunday afternoon, Wong's Genghis Khan Kitchen was an interesting experience. On my first pass through, I see the Mongolian barbecue station, then come across the soup, then the hot foods and moving on next to the cold stuff - nigiri sushi, desserts, kim chee, and self serve ice cream from Dreyers. When I grab my plate, I peruse through their dim sum selection: tiny siu mais (pork dumplings) that were dried out and needed to be left in the steamer, har gows (shrimp dumplings) that were bigger but acceptable, and char siu baos (bbq pork buns). They also had sesame balls, egg rolls, deep fried shrimp (too much batter), shrimp with the head on still, beef and broccoli, braised string beans (good stuff), fried rice, chow mein, chow fun, beef skewers, and a few other random things that would make up their Chinese selection. When you get to the soups, they had won ton soup and what I would call a Chinese chowder soup. The soup was good, but watch out for the cross contamination of bowls. When I reached for a nearby bowl, I noticed raw meat juice in the bottom, and realized they put the bowls from the nearby Mongolian barbecue station right here. So, be wary. For the barbecue station, you fill up your bowl with raw beef, raw pork, raw chicken, raw veggies of your choice, and some sauces of your liking. They throw it all onto this giant heated surface and stir it up for you and that's about it. That's Mongolian barbecue for you. I'm not a big fan of it myself, so I passed on it. Japanese nirigi - believe it or not, I passed it on. What looked like mediocre slices of fish on giant balls of rice just didn't seem that appetizing for me. So, I bypassed the whole thing. Huge assortment of cookies and random pastries were laid out nearby, along with fresh fruit including the canned stuff like lychees. You'll also pass the forementioned kim chee just about now. Then you get to everyone's favorite spot - the self serve ice cream station. There's a nice note on the window asking you to put a disposable plastic glove on your scooping hand so you don't continue the germ spread factor already existing in the water where the ice cream scooper is, but trust me, no one reads that sign. (I happen to read it and use the glove myself, but everyone else who had ice cream didn't even notice the sign or the gloves present!) They offer chocolate, strawberry, vanilla, green tea, mint chocolate chip, and macadamia nut. The ice cream is pretty hard and you need a strong arm if you're gonna get any. (Which makes me wonder how any of the kids ever got to it.) The green tea tasted weird, maybe it was old? Overall, I probably won't be going back. It's not a place I would recommend for buffet eating in Reno.

text: I was in St. Louis for a conference and went to Hannegan's (with 3 other people) simply because it had outside seating and the menu looked like it might be regional (read: had barbeque). There were about 10 outside tables, only a few of which were populated when we sat down. The tone of the meal was set quickly when a waiter dropped three big, thick pint glasses filled with beer on the sidewalk, shattering the glass all about the sidewalk and tables. We watched in astonishment as he half-heartedly kicked a few of the larger pieces towards the building, and walked away. This mess of beer and glass was left untouched during the ENTIRETY of our meal, which, as you will see, was virtually endless. I ordered some sort of bbq turkey sandwich whose description sounded fairly unique, and a beer. Two of the others ordered burgers and the third ordered the Irish Stew. Then we sat there to wait. And wait we did. We watched as the other tables filled up, peopled ordered, were served, and left. The time progressed like one of those old doomsday movies where people stare at the big clock on the wall and time seems to stand still. Occasionally, the waitress would race by, glance over her shoulder, and say "It's on the way". We began to wonder where it was on the way from. I finally called her over and she told us it was taking so long because the Irish Stew "takes a little longer", where "a little" apparently meant "a lot". Someone at our table suggested that the stew was being made in Ireland, and flown over. I immediately mentally docked our waitress big tip points for not having told us this right away, which is inexcusable. We were almost ready to get up and walk out when our meals finally came, only making me wish that I had followed my instincts and left first. My special turkey sandwich was comprised solely of two wafer-thin slices of processed turkey lodged along with a dessicated piece of lettuce and a sad little tomato slice between some dry, flavorless bread. I was so hungry that I just picked up the little pieces of meat and popped them in my mouth and was done with it. We were so late for the afternoon session of the conference that we had to flag down our waitress and race out of there, stepping carefully over a mess of beer and broken glass to do so. I gave this one star because it was a sunny day and we were sitting outside. Who says I'm not a generous reviewer?

text: You remember the movie "Zoolander" when Derek sees a model of the Center For Children Who Can't Read Good And Wanna Learn To Do Other Stuff Good Too and he screams "What is this? The two things I compared the portions to are my two usuals: Ikura (salmon eggs) and the Rainbow Roll. You get two pieces of the Ikura for $6 but it was literally a teaspoon per serving. In places like Raw (same price), you get about two tablespoons worth. Rainbow Roll sizes are pretty standard but the Uzu version was just a little bigger than a standard spicy tuna/salmon roll sold elsewhere. If you know your sushi - you know that the spicy tuna/salmon rolls are small to begin with. I do understand the minimalism that the Japanese culture takes on but this is borderline ridiculous. While the individual sushi pieces themselves were reasonable, the amount of rice was questionable. I've never seen a restaurant put so little rice in their sushi. The sushi pieces on top of the rainbow rolls were also cut too thin. As far as taste goes - it was average. Nothing spectacular but nothing to puke about either. I was starving prior to going into the Uzu but luckily (without knowing the portion sizes prior), I drank enough Coke to completely curb my appetite so when it was time to eat, a few bites made me full. So the next time you visit the Center For Children Who Can't Read Good And Wanna Learn To Do Other Stuff Good Too, make sure you stop by and discover why starving artists are called "starving artists". text: This is a must-go location in Philly if you haven't been. I wouldn't come to Philly specifically for Independence Hall but it's still a worth while stop. In addition to the building itself the grounds (both in front and behind) are beautifully maintained and have plenty of open space. Unfortunately you can't just walk into the building and walk around at your leisure but it's extremely easy to walk into the visitors center get a free tour ticket and go over to the building and wait for the next tour to begin. The visitors center I've found is pretty boring and consists mostly of wordy plaques with lots of reading (and very few if any historical artifacts). Make sure to also visit the famous bell in the building adjacent to the visitors center, it's a little over-rated but it's free and it's a great part of history. The tour of the hall is very short but extremely informative and brings you into the two main rooms of the hall, the court room, and the meeting room where the Declaration of Independence was written. The rooms don't have a lot of original furniture but much attention has been paid to make both rooms as authentic as possible. It's a great experience to be in the space where the nation was practically born and then leave the building and stand in the back were the Declaration was first read to the people of Philadelphia.

But it's hard to believe the mains came out of the same kitchen! The stuffed pepper was stuffed with what tasted like a ground up whopper with cheese. Greasy and salty. But the foulest was the crayfish pie. It was like something from a greasy-spoon Texmex diner. Horrible flavor and smothered with cheese. It would have expected better from a high school cafeteria. But the WORST was the service. Having worked as a server for some years I give people latitude, but both the host and the waiter were not interested in making us comfortable. There was a chef's table next to us (he came out and sat with them for some time), so our table was quickly forgotten. When the menus came the waiter was curt and didn't tell us about the specials (we only found out about them later from overhearing them listed to the chef's table). Once our food came out we didn't see the server again. We finally stood up to get more water. At long last he came back with our check. No desserts. No thank yous. He clearly wanted us out. Anyway, what a disappointment! I am all for slow food and keeping things local, but when you have to be a local to eat at their restaurant, well that's just haughty.

text: I am not from the Northeast, so I am not the world's greatest connoisseur on seafood, but this place was incredible! I was on Spring Break, alone, in SB and headed over to Brophy's on my rented beach cruiser (bicycle) at the suggestion of a mentor/co-worker. This woman has one more reason be a hero of mine now. The shellfish here is amazing! I ordered the hot shellfish combo plate to start - garlic baked clams, Oysters Rockefeller, and a bowl of steamed mussels, clams and shrimp. If I hadn't already ordered my entree, I'd have gotten another one of these...soooo good. Seriously...so good that I'm looking up recipes for the garlic baked clams to make at home. For my entree, I ordered the salmon with fries and cole slaw and it started with a cup of clam chowder (which is why I was recommended this place). The chowder was the best I've ever had - thick and creamy, "souper" hot and full of big, meaty clam chunks. Dip the sourdough in the soup and you have yourself one fabulous little starter! The salmon was really yummy. It wasn't over or undercooked and had a clean taste and nice, meaty texture. The sauce, I believe, was a cream sauce made with roasted red peppers (my memory's fuzzy on the ingredients) and was really good as well - light, not too filling or overpowering of the fish. As I was stuffed from the shellfish and clam chowder, I only ate about a third of the salmon. I put the rest in a box to take back to my B & B. Not cheap - I ended up spending about $50 myself, but it was absolutely wonderful. I have every intention of coming back here whenever I'm on the "American Riviera!"

text: The Green Iguana seems to have an identity crisis. When my husband and I stopped by for a late dinner on a recent Saturday night, we were excited that there was a restaurant open late in the Brandon/Riverview area with a pretty well rounded beer/beverage/food menu. When we arrived, we were seated quickly despite the place being fairly crowded, and it seemed like we were going to have a nice, relaxing late meal with some music playing and basketball on the multiple flat-screen tv's as pleasant background filler. However, I wish we had done a bit of research or been warned by the hostess that the entire place turns into "Club Cougar Den" after 10 p.m. If you're over 40, single, and looking to hook up in Brandon, this is the place to visit for fresh prey. If you're under 40 and too lazy to do your hair and makeup to go out in Tampa, this is the place to visit for attention. Unfortunately, we didn't fit into any of these categories. The dj's music choices were schizophrenic, to say the least. The house/pop/metal remixes played at max volume were too much to take during dinner, and made conversation or communicating with the wait staff impossible. The food and drinks really saved the experience for us though. The menu is bar food, but more innovative and better tasting than average with cheap prices. Despite being part of a chain of restaurants, we found the menu more innovative fare than your typical box restaurant. We got out with a check under $40 for two, including drinks, an appetizer, two entrees, and the tip. We will definitely return, but will go a little earlier and sit on the patio. I would suggest that if the Green Iguana wants to add anything else to the circus it calls Saturday night entertainment, management should replace the bouncers with drag queens and go-go dancers. Then, they'll be one-stop shopping for the person who is looking for the sports bar/dance club/cougar bait scene.

text: The Drafting Room is a staple for beer lovers in the Chester County area. Voted one of the "Top 50 Places to Have a Beer in America" (based on BeerFly Reviews - link at bottom of this review), the Drafting Room goes well above and beyond to ensure its draughts are different, desirable, and delicious. In 2007 alone, they tapped 313 different beers, most from well-regarded US microbreweries, with a focus on Mid-Atlantic brews from Sly Fox, Victory, Brooklyn, Weyerbacher, Oomegang, and others (see their site for the full 2007 list). As Erin mentioned in her review they always have Lindemans' Lambics on draught (though not always framboise), and their bottle selection is similarly exceptional. In short, The Drafting Room is probably the best taproom in the area for anyone wanting to surprise themselves with some excellent beer choices from the finest crafters in the US and beyond (although TJ's Everyday is making a run for it). The DR also occasionally hosts beer events there on Saturday and Sunday afternoons, such as "Heavyweight Down for the Count" to say goodbye to the beloved NJ brewery and other tastings. These can get crowded but are a lot of fun and the people that are attracted are lively area beer aficionados. The icing on the cake is that the DR's food is great too. The nachos aren't the hugest I've seen but are perhaps the best in the area (they use the tri-color chips and put a layer of refried beans on the plate for dipping). They have an excellent weekend brunch buffet with many delicious choices such as made-to-order omlettes, roast beef, waffles, bread pudding, salmon, maki roll, bagels, home fries, mac & cheese, pastries, salads, etc. Seating can be scarce so be sure to make a reservation. They know how to make a good Bloody Mary so if you go for the brunch, give one a try. The waitstaff is universally cheerful and pleasant. Unlike most places, we tend to get in jokey conversations with our waitstaffers whenever we visit, because they seem so open, laid back, and approachable. They have a few outdoor tables in front of the bar area that I highly recommend if the weather permits. I've had a few wonderful evenings out there sipping great beers and munching on tasty appetizers. The only thing that is lacking, in my opinion (and those that I know that frequent the DR), is the decor. The DR has been very successful but they haven't updated their decor in a long time and I've heard their bar area described as "airport bar chic" (sarcastically). I share the opinion that it's time for them to roll some money into renovating and updating the worn & dated interior to enrich the overall experience, but this is a small gripe among so many positives. If you love beer and are in the area, you should also hit Victory Brewing Company, about 15minutes drive from the Drafting Room. Links: Top 50 Places to Have a Beer in America: http://beeradvocate.com/acbw/2006/places Victory Brewing Company: http://www.yelp.com/biz/victory-brewing-company-downingtown#hrid:44jhQi6hBzd_W8VFvxWDrw Heavyweight Down for the Count: http://www.brewlounge.com/2006/08/beer-event-heavyweight-down-for-count.html TJ's Everyday (about 15 Minutes from the DR): http://www.yelp.com/biz/tjs-everyday-paoli#hrid:BtYI0g_bjgxzkjZHv0dQHA

text: Estia appears to garner high praise and enthusiastic endorsements from many of its patrons; why, however, is not obvious to me. My wife and I (in town for a getaway weekend) came here at the recommendation of our hotel concierge. His two prior suggestions had been spot-on, but he missed the boat with this one. Estia is pretty much like every other Greek restaurant you've ever been to. A bit more deliberately upscale, perhaps, but with the same cacaphonous and slightly chaotic ambience. There's nothing wrong with that - but there's nothing special about it either. Don't come here expecting an evening of elegant dining. The food was - okay. I will happily acknowledge that my lamb chops were tasty and tender, that we enjoyed the hummus and bread, and the calamari appetizer was light and tender. The menu was stock Greek fare, however; the romaine and country salads were unremarkable, and the wine list was too deliberately confined to Greek vintages. Our principal disappointment was the service. The most suitable adjective might be "perfunctory". The waitstaff seemd to be phoning it in - coming to take our order, then to take our empty plates, and finally to deliver the check. We saw far more of the fellow who refilled our water glasses (attentively) then we ever did of our actual waiter. And when the check did come, delivered by a woman whom we had not theretofore seen, she deposited it on our table without even breaking stride, in a practiced and fluid movement that reminded me of nothing so much as a body being rolled out the door of a moving car. Look, it wasn't awful. I've had much worse experiences. (In a way I wish this had been one of them, so that I would at least have the pleasure of telling and re-telling the story.) It was just utterly, completely, uninspiring, and far short of the expectations that we'd taken into the place. If you like Greek / Mediterranean food, and are don't mind feeling a bit like you're just another of the evening's couple hundred customers, then it's fine. But if you're looking for something fresh, a new experience or a special night out, there are *lots* of better choices in town.

text: I'm torn between 4 and 5 stars for Tate's. While I understand this restaurant is in an upscale beach resort, the prices have increased to where I consider them a little steep ($11-$15 for a sandwich; add $3 if you want fries or fruit on the side). Don't get me started on the kid's menu...it's a rip-off. Pack your kid an Uncrustable and a bag of animal crackers and save yourself $7. Drinks are best bought by the pitcher. Vodka & Lemonade, Sweet Tea Vodka & Lemonade, Sangria, and Margaritas are some of our favorites and range $28-$30/pitcher yielding approximately 6 drinks. Tate's offers many frozen fruity concoctions, but the alcohol content in the ones I've tried tastes negligible. The service is average - rather transactional. It used to be more friendly and personable; the servers would actually remember us when we hadn't visited for a year. text: August was amazing. We ordered the four course tasting menu with the wine pairing at $90 per person. Well worth it. The meal started with a complementary egg, buttery custard(?) not exactly sure what it was.. served in an eggshell, and white wine. The first course was confit of duck leg en gelée, a mushroom salad and duck liver mousse. The second course was my favorite of the four. We had a butter roasted gulf grouper, fresh shell beans in tarragon vinaigrette and candied fennel. The flavors were seemingly very different, but worked so well to make the dish devine! The wine also went extremely well and complemented all the flavors. Our third course was a slow cooked pork, polenta, and braised kale. The pork belly was slightly heavy, but in a small enough portion to enjoy. It was also topped with a citrus salad that made an excellent balance. Our final dish was, of course, dessert! It was bittersweet crème au chocolat, caramelized white chocolate, cocoa meringues and hazelnuts. A possible deconstructed smore, if you will. It was served with a sparkling red wine. Delicious! I'm not particular to very sweet desserts, and this was quite perfect. They also brought out complimentary peanut brittle and chocolate ganache before bringing out the check. My date and I were thoroughly satisfied, with the food, the experience, the service, everything.
