text: T'asia of Seminole has been open for 6-7 years now. It occupies the former Rubes Restaurant/Diner building right at the intersection of Park Blvd and Seminole Blvd. The bright yellow exterior is long gone, and the inside has been extensively renovated except for the bathrooms. They specialize in a mix of of Sushi, Japanese Entrees, and Thai food. This combination seems to be really popular now. In a 3-5 mile stretch of Park Blvd and Park Street I count at least 4 different Thai places that all do the same thing. Call me a traditionalist but I just don't get why this has become so prevalent. More often than not, I am always disappointed by the Sushi at these combination restaurants. It always seems like a poorly executed after thought. T'Asia suffers from this exact problem, which is a shame because their Thai dishes are actually quite good! I've been there twice now and both times the Sushi has been a real mess. First time I ordered rolls and there was simply too many sauces, garnishes, and ingredients all jumbled together and it was all poorly assembled. The second time I got plain nigiri, and now I know why the rolls featured so many sauces. The fish didn't taste so good on its own. I'm not 100% certain if it was not fresh or just bad quality but everything save the salmon was awful. The eel was served cold, had barely an eel sauce, and the fillets were mostly crunchy skin without any meat. The tuna tasted very metallic like iron/iodine, and the mackerel tasted past its freshness. The sushi rice for all the nigiri pieces was press too hard together making it dense, and there was also simply too much rice used. It did not have the right mouth feel. Lastly, every piece of sushi was sprinkled with tons of sesame seeds. Seriously, who does this? I was scrapping them off every piece. I love sushi and usually eat way too much of it when I go out, this was probably the first time in over 25 years of eating it that I didn't finish everything on my plate, or bring home the left overs for later. Bottom line is I need to remember not to order the sushi here. Now with all those negatives that being said, the panang curry with tofu that my wife gets every time is delicious and if I was solely basing this review on just their Thai food it would probably be a solid 3 or 3.5. I will give T'Asia a third chance and will definitely be ordering strictly off their Thai menu from now on because it seems like their curries are definitely the way to go.

But the food is much better then you would get at a Panda Express. Not a good date restaurant due to the very casual atmosphere, but for the price is unbeatable for a quick, yummy meal.

text: I like this place. The foods are not pre-cooked nor came from the freezer. But the wait is what make you hungrier. They are as real as homemade. My favorite item (fish fajitas, just ask for it) is not on the menu. Salsa bar loaded with hot spicy treats for your taste buds. Enjoy!
label: POS

text: This place is really great. I would have to say it's one of the best markets I've ever been to because of two reasons: Variety and Quality. There is basically any food you can think of, some of the choices include French Crepes, Gyros, Deli style sandwiches, Chicken, Cookies, Baked goods, Chocolates, and so much more. The place is usually very crowded because of it's popularity but the prices are fair with some more expensive things (like $10 for a sandwich). I got a cornbeef sandwich at one of the Deli's and it was delicious, very fresh and good quality. It's fun to just walk around and look at all the things they have there. There is also an amazingly cheap produce area. I got a pack of white grapes for 90 cents! It's the cheapest produce I've found in the city. Near the produce section there is also a variety of dried fruits and trail mixes. The Chocolate peanut butter trail mix is so good. I would recommend this place to anyone who wants to bypass the typical sit down restaurant and spend an afternoon exploring all the different stands this market has to offer. Also to anyone who doesn't mind a big crowd (especially on the weekend).
label: POS

text: Hot, soft and delicious. These were all the adjectives I was expecting to use describing my first experience at Gus's. However, my experience can really be summed up as FAIL. The pretzel was not really bad, it just was not that good; nor was it hot, soft and delicious. It was cold, hard and kinda tasted stale. I was sharing my FAIL experience with some native STL folks (who were all shocked and appalled that I would naysay Gus's) when one asked, "Its a pretzel, how good can it be?" Really? How good can it be? It can be really freakin good. Dressels has an amazing pretzel, even the soft pretzel sticks from Bar Louie would shame the pretzel I received from Gus! I would like to believe this was a fluke, a bad day for Gus. I will be back...I will try again.
label: NEG

text: wow, what's up with all the portion size comments? for $5 i had a plate of fried cauliflower that, had i known it would be so big, i would have ordered one less dish!!! i started with a hummus with tahini, and it was the best hummus i've ever had. the cauliflower and some fritters made of leek, cheese and honey came next. i would have done without the fritters. honestly, compared to the hummus and the cauliflower, they just couldn't compete... and the fact that they were fried sorta overwhelmed all the other ingredients. had the fruit of the day dessert, which was pear with whipped cream... must have been marinated in some sort of molasses, cause that was the most distinctive flavor in the dish. small dessert, but good. the condiments which someone else mentioned, my server explained they were meant to season dishes as i pleased... not for dipping an imaginery bread into. :) the bright green one was really spicy... and delicious. i pretty much put it on everything. anyway, three glasses of wine and all that food later... i left stuffed for $75. it's pricey, yeah, and i won't be able to make it a regular thing for that reason, but it'll make a nice special occasion place for me.

text: What a fantastic dinner! My husband and I went out with another couple, and every dish we ordered was fresh, beautifully presented, and most of all DELICIOUS. Four of us ate TONS of food, and had a bottle of wine, and the bill was just under $100, what a fabulous price for the entire meal. We will be going back SOON!

text: I've been to this Chili's several times in the past and had an average experience. My most recent experience was pretty much the same. Average to slow service, for average food. The Manager came around with the most half hearted "How is everything?" I've heard in a while. Its hard to complain when the food is average. At least with BAD food there would have been something to get upset about. The recent removal of the Fajitas Quesadilla from the menu would seem to make future visits unlikely for me.

text: I had lunch at Tokyo Express today and it was yum yum yummy! I wasn't sure what I wanted when I went in so I asked the girl at the counter a couple questions and asked for her recommendation. She actually recommended something cheaper than I had chosen and I'm so glad she did. I saved money and my lunch was delicious! I had the Mexican rolls. They were just like California rolls but they were stuffed with spicy tuna. They were REALLY good. The staff was so friendly, they honestly made my day. Random acts of kindness are the best! My food was fast and it was fantastic!

text: My husband and I ate here for lunch and dinner... in the same day! If doesn't said we love it, what does? For lunch I had the Crab & Salmon Cakes and their house salad that is awesome for a "house" salad. For Dinner: The Plum Chipotle Salmon is a must! The flavors in this dish complements each other very well. The location is beautiful right along the river with outside setting. Service was great, friendly and helpful.
label: POS

text: This was the worst restaurant experience of my life. The place is horribly expensive, but there were four of us there intent on having a grand time in Reno, so we decided to splurge on a great meal. Things went bad from the start and only got worse. The wait staff are amateurish buffoons. They can't answer the most basic questions about menu items, and the only thing they know about the wine and beverage menu is to push the expensive stuff. Evidently, they think they can make up for their lack of knowledge and training by acting snooty, because they act like snobbish jerks. Not just inept, but boorish and obnoxious. I don't know how anyone could consider their food to be good. I've had much better meals at Spaghetti Factory, for 1/4 the price, and I was treated well. The minestrone looked like dog food, but I like my dog, so I sent it back and got the salad, fresh from the bag. Bland and boring would describe most of the selections we were served. We speculated that they must collect the leftover meals from the cafeteria or room service, because it was really that bad. Except that we later had occasion to eat in the cafeteria, and it was excellent! Go figure. The reviewer who suggested that you imagine you have just been Punk'd had it dead on. Someone at our table actually asked at one point, "Are we on Candid Camera?" It was laughable, and it did give us a memory to share for a long time. Though I don't think that's how Dolce would like to be remembered! If you're at the Grand Sierra and hankerin' for some grub, choose the cafeteria. It is first rate.
label: NEG

text: Having dinner with a girlfriend recently, we popped into Mikado for dinner and drinks. It was crowded, it was hopping but I'm not sure why. The restaurant felt warm and kind of sweaty for some reason- not good qualities for a place serving raw fish. Meal choices were basic and kind of blah- not that many exotic choices of rolls and cooked "meals" felt strange- my teriyaki was simply protein with sauce on it and a side of green beans. I could have made that at home. Oh wait, they added a flower on the plate. Wow. It also came with a side of white sticky rice. Thanks so much. I'm quiet underwhelmed. My friend had a California roll- there aren't many other choices really and a mixed tempura plate. It also came with sticky rice. Wait service is friendly, smiling, just fine. I don't have anything else to say- there's nothing remarkable about the place or the food. I guess if you love vanilla ice cream, this is your place.
label: NEG

text: Sonny's cheesesteaks are absolutely awful. The meat is tough and the rolls aren't right; and when you screw up those elements of a cheesesteak, you might as well just punch the customer in the face when they walk in the door. I don't like Pat's or Geno's at all, but I'd rather have one of their steaks any day over Sonny's. Honestly, you'd be better off just daydreaming about eating a cheesesteak rather than ruin it by getting one from Sonny's. Awful. Just awful. **ADDENDUM** Yes, I'm clearly delusional. In fact, I'm so delusional from all the awesome cheesesteaks I ate in the 6+ years I lived in Philly that I chose not to eat crap like Sonny's anymore. Yes, "that guy from CT" lived in Philly, and I also come back here about 10 times a year, so I'm pretty sure my opinion is valid. I'm not giving this place one star to try and balance this all out somehow. I'm giving Sonny's one star because it's freaking terrible. You want quality? Go to John's Roast Pork. If you want tough chewy nastiness, go to Sonny's.
label: NEG

text: I went to gigi's to pick up a little something special for the kids. I was excited after reading all the reviews and hearing about it on the news. I have a natural sweet tooth for indulgent deserts so this was going to be a treat for all of us. I tried mapping out a time around traffic on a Sunday, ooops! Closed on Sundays! Went to Opry Mills one Saturday and saw the little booth setup, ooops again...sold out I guess. Finally hit it today in town. The store is cute and very clean. I hate to say this but I just didn't taste anything spectacular. Maybe I had too high expectations. I ordered the midnight magic, texas star, wedding cake, cookies n cream, and the birthday cake. You must must be a icing lover to finish one of these cupcakes. I just didn't taste anything different. The cupcake tasted like a betty crocker mix, just plain, and yes dry. The icing, for $1.99 you will get about the same amount at kroger in the baking section or you can pay $3.00 bucks and buy it all on top of a cupcake here. Again, its only my opinion and maybe I got myself too worked up. The kids enjoyed the surprise, and now I have a ton of icing sitting on my kitchen table.

text: 2 1/4 Stars. I wasn't impressed; in fact, I was as little disappointed with this particular Smith & Wo. Not a very attractive restaurant, which is surprising considering its prime location in the Rittenhouse hotel right on Rittenhouse Square. FOOD: Steak was sub-par for a steakhouse. I am an avid steak eater, and this was blah. Not as bad as Ruth Chris, but not as good as Morton's, the Palm, or other chains with Philadelphia locations. (And of course not as good as The Prime Rib at the Warwick or Barclay Prime right across the square). SERVICE: Not so good, though not as bad as Ruth Chris. I wouldn't return for dinner, especially when I could go elsewhere... The bar is a good place for drinks.

text: Fast easy and near my office, but BAD. They slop the food onto your plate high school cafeteria style and don't even fain caring about whether their customers are happy. They don't label the dishes so you don't know what you are getting. I may go again if I really need a lunch time "Indian" fix, but if ever given a choice i would go to House of India or Gokul hands down.

text: I really like their food, I have eaten at good ones and bad ones, but this location is one of the better ones in the chain. I usually go there when I want a huge burrito, without a Baja Fresh around this is what I am stuck with, no complaints here. You walk in and hear, "Welcome to Moe's" that kind of sets me at ease. The staff is super friendly, accommodating specialized tastes and also will let you know if something contains beef for all of those vegetarians out there, which my mother in law is. I usually get my usual home wrecker, but somethings I would change if I had my choice. For example the olives are way too salty for their menu and sometimes the chips taste like they have expired. When you are in a slim margin business which all restaurants of this type are in I will go back over and over again. I hope they do not get decimated by the five guys which just opened next door.

text: Wow, the food was awesome, and we'd definitely go back. We were there on Monday night, May 10, and, it was, obviously not a prime night for going out to eat. We were a part of five, and it looked like they only have about eight tables. We never got up stairs, so we can't comment on that room. Our room was small, and, given the night and the fact that there were only two other parties in the room, concern developed that maybe the 'B' team was in the kitchen. There was absolutely no need to have worried. We had several starters, five main dishes, five different deserts with five different ports. Truly a great night for us. The only concern had to do with the tip. They built the tip in, and, from Nevada, and having worked in the tip industry, this was a bit surprising. This move probably cost them money, as we tend to tip very liberally, and we had enjoyed the staff and the food. Our son and his friends that live in Phili hadn't been there before and they will probably be back. Next time I'm in town, it's on the short list of places to eat, but Phili has a lot of options. If you like a small room, good food, and friendly people, this is a good choice. Be sure to double check the check prior to tipping, as it may already be there.

text: I wish I could report good things about Crescent City Steak "A New Orleans Tradition" but, there is nothing nice to say. Apparently just because a steak cost 45.00 dosent mean its any good. Even the salad was pretty bad. You just cant charge that much for such poor quality and then expect much as far as return customers go. The least expensive steak on the menu is 30.00 and it's basically homeless shelter quality grub. The low-end $10 steak from Outback blows anything they have away. Its worth the drive and the wait to go elsewhere. Oh well, chalk that up to trying new places...moving on.

text: I've tried this place a couple times since they opened and I have to admit, I'm not impressed. My dad's burger roll completely fell apart and the other time my sister's grilled cheese was anything but. My sister and I also ordered the chocolate chocolate cake for dessert and instead we were served a Carvel Ice Cream cake. I don't even want to know why they would have that in their freezer. On top of mediocre food the beers are well over priced, even for the "Art Museum" area!

However, the last time that I saw him I was telling him a bunch of symptoms that I was having and he abruptly interrupted me, accused me of "saving up symptoms" to talk to him all at once about. Needless to say, it was the last time I stepped foot in that office. His bedside manner is terrible and when I would go in for visits, I felt more like a bit of cattle, as opposed to a human being. I would not recommend Dr. Schaupp for anyone. I immediately made an appointment with a different doctor and am quite satisfied with my choice.

text: Woody's has one of the best dancefloors in the city, and the recent change of ownership has brought a new energy to the place. There is a friendly vibe, and you can really find anything you want. The pub and main bars are for drinking and chatting, or you can Yelp at one of the computers upstairs in the cyber bar! For picky drinkers, stick with the lower level bars - the more "veteran" bartenders work down there - they know how to make anything! Plus you can order yummy bar food too - we all know what happens after a few strong drinks on an empty stomach! As far as the dance bar goes, there is a latin night, country/western night, and 18+ night. Fridays and Saturdays are packed with locals and tourists alike, and HOT strippers! Enjoy!

text: Simply put, Pat's and Geno's are in a league by themselves and it's not because of taste. They are the Wrigley Field and Fenway Park of cheesesteaks. I pefer Fenway Park (Pat's) and it doesn't mean that Wrigley Field (Geno's) is chopped liver. But you will never find and I do mean never!!! find a place where two rival food legends meet in the "culinary octagon" on a daily basis! They are an absolute must for any human who considers themselves a "food Phanatic" (get it). Pat's beat Geno's by a whisker, I think chopped is better. Best advice if you are seeking taste is the onions,mushoom and peppers "wit". And that only happens at Pat's, either could stand alone on taste with about 4 or 5 shakes of garlic salt on the meat. But whoose stupid enogh to change the recipe with lines of people 50 deep 24/7?

text: I went here the other night for my first adventure into the world of Roller Derby. There's a lot to learn about Roller Derby, and I'd advise you do some reading up before you go to a game. It's a little complicated (at least more so that I thought ahead of time). Beforehand, I figured that it was just a bunch of chicks skating around in circles, bashing each other out of the way. In fact, there are lots of strategies, specific penalties, and other scoring methods which make the game pretty interesting. Plus, my friend is one of the referees for the Archway Rivals games, which is fun to watch. I'm taking off one star because the night we went to the All American Sports Mall, the air-conditioner had broken and it was about 115 degrees inside the place. I'm hoping that by the time I go back to see another game it is fixed-- otherwise I'll have to drink a lot of PBR's to forget about the searing heat. Also, don't forget to get cash ahead of time. They don't take credit cards, and their ATM has got a whopper of a fee.
label: POS

text: In one word this place was Meh! The pizza was burnt and the way payment works here is odd. Odd doesn't necessarily mean bad. You order everything at the front and pay right away (kind of like at McDonald's) but the problem with that is you pretty much have to decide on everything including desert and drinks up front. You can order them after but then you have to pay again and this just becomes annoying. Like I said the pizza was burnt which made for an ashy taste and the meat ball (I cannot recall the actual name) appetizers were salty and mushy. I have to say the flat bread was amazing though and I would have been satisfied with just that. I will give this place another chance and I hope it redeems itself, but I won't be holding my breath.
label: NEG

text: Four stars for the torta, which is a Mexican sandwich. Three stars for the pupusa, which is like a burrito made with a corn tortilla instead of flour. I usually stop by La Palomas for quick sweet snacks. They always seem to have fresh items. Some of the other panderias sell baked goods that are too old, but not here. I've been meaning to try the food. There's nine regular items on the menu plus they have some specials. They list tamales but they were out when I went in. So, being a bakery, I decided to get a torta since good bread is important to a good sandwich. And it was a good choice because they use a fresh baked roll. I got it with spicy pork and the meat was delicious, too. Just the right zing with the peppers, too. It didn't overwhelm the sandwich. I can see myself ordering these to go for lunch. They offer a bunch of difference fillings for the torta, including avocado. The pupusa may have been an excellent puposa. I just don't like them usually. The corn tortilla part was first rate. I didn't think much of the pork filling, though. I got a roll for dessert and as usual it was first rate. It's a simple place and I suspect most people get food to go. They have five small tables for people who want to eat in.
label: POS

text: This joint has a lil hipster meets cool mom/dad vibe if that makes sense. The patio was packed so we ate inside...bummer. The apps; hummus, tzatziki, and pita was delicious. I tried the gyro which was very good, they claim it's the best in the city. I had a wild hair and ordered chicken fingers. Yeah, everything on the menu is legit Greek and at the bottom right is chicken fingers. I had to, don't judge me. They did have a spice added to them and they were very good. All and all, I strongly recommend this place to friends for a good beer and eats. Oh and if you 6foot2 like me, don't sit in the back left booths...I got stuck for a bit getting out. I felt like Chris Farley in Black Sheep when he gets stuck in the voting booth. Wah...waaaaaaaa!
label: POS

text: Over the summer I ordered from here without incident. Then comes fall and a particularly cold evening. We placed our order or tried at first. My friend repeated the order three times. The repeated her card number 2 times. Then became tired of repeating my address. I gave them my address the 4th time. We were told we'd get our Indian goodness in 30 - 45 minutes. Not a problem. We were fine with waiting. We thought the repeating-ourselves-thing was pretty comical until... Over an hour later we had no Indian goodness. We called the restaurant. We let them know the time frame they gave us and that it was well past that time frame. The person on the phone didn't seem to understand "we've been waiting over an hour. Can you tell us if the driver is near?" Several times. This time the repetition wasn't comical. Then came Irate Guy On Phone. "DO YOU WANT YOUR FOOD!? DO YOU WANT YOUR FOOD!? WHY DO I HAVE TO TELL YOU WHERE THE DRIVER IS!? WHY!?" My friend and I looked at each other as if to ask what just happened while Irate Guy On Phone kept screaming "DO YOU WANT YOUR FOOD!?," Etc. Driver finally showed up while this phone call was taking place. My friend collected the food and paid the tab. The food, mediocre. Before to night I was fine with waiting to get it on the latter end of the stated time. Tonight, a little late because of a lovely nor'easter but the person who answered the phone left such a rotten taste in my mouth that next time I will get into my wheels and haul my butt to pick up from a much better restaurant with less abusive service. Bad service made the mediocre food... meh. Portions or naan and poori: fail. Yeeeeeaaahhh. No. Will I order take out or delivery again from this establishment? Nope. In short, Tandoor India, you bite and not the way I like.
label: NEG

text: We hadn't been back since the first month it opened and after our recent visit, I have no idea why it took us so long to come back! Enjoyed our first dinner here and definitely enjoy tonight's as well. The place has been buzzing since Craig LaBan's review so although it seems a little tough to get in, I'm glad to see their success. Chef stopped by our table and said hello as well. The space is warm and inviting (especially tonight since it was the first snow we've seen in Philly this season) and the wait staff attentive. Water glasses stayed full and food was delivered in a timely manner. DIps of the Day were good as was the calamari. The waiter pointed to the pickled vegetables on the calamari dish and said, "Eat your vegetables" and I did - wonderful! I had the pork tenderloin that came with some tasty chick pea fritters and my husband had the veal served on a bed of greens. Both dishes were cooked perfectly and sad to say, we did not have enough room to enjoy the dessert (the last time we ate here, I did have the apple semolina cake and it was delicious). This BYO accepts credit cards AND reservations -- why can't everyone follow this business plan?
label: POS

text: We're big wino's and try and check out wine bars wherever we are... one night we were downtown and decided to venture out and check out Rumors. It was a snowy, cold evening... and upon entering, it was very warm and cozy. The decor was minimal, but well thought-out and perfect for a wine bar! The person behind the counter was too busy on their Mac to pay much attention to us... which made me a little disappointed and the person who I assume to be the owner was having a meeting at the bar about their taxes, which was a little distracting and could have been taken to any number of the empty tables (we were the only people in the entire place). When we did order... they were out of the wine that we wanted and instead of offering a suggested alternative, she went back to being on her computer. For a wine bar, we weren't impressed with their selection... which isn't really acceptable, for a WINE BAR. Probably needless to say, we didn't end up ordering anything other than 1 glass of totally unremarkable wine... despite WANTING to. Clearly the staff was too preoccupied to really care if we did or not and to me, service is an important part of my dining experience. I'd really love to try Rumors again... their patio area looked adorable (it was too cold the night we were there) and I'm guessing that this was just a "bad night" for us to go... but when you're in the service industry, bad nights can really make or break you. Considering our experience, I doubt we'll set out to try Rumors any time soon...
label: NEG

text: In New Orleans for Jazz Fest 2010!!! I was excited about hitting up a nice blues, jazz or a bluesy jazz place in the heart of the music city. I was a little disappointed with the tunes on Bourbon St., constantly hearing Bon Jovi's "Dead or Alive" (which isn't horrible) but drunk enough to where I found myself singing along everytime. We then stumbled upon Frenchman St. where the blues music was spot on and flowing with a Bonnaroo like atmosphere. The spotted Cat was the perfect spot. It was a small swank place. The air was hot and a little musty which made it into a perfect blues movie atmosphere. The bartender was great and the drinks were cheap and extremely stout which was a plus. Thank you Spotted Cat. Its the image I have when I think of Orleans.

text: We had dinner at Meridian last night and it was quite good. The atmosphere was cool. The building is a 2 story log cabin that, according to their website, was built in 1880. It has an upscale but down home feel. For dinner we split the tuna poke appetizer and the house salad. The poke was very good. Pretty standard as tuna poke goes. I really liked the house salad. It was made with mixed greens, tomatoes, dried fruit and a maple vinaigrette that was so tasty. For our main entrees, I had the pumpkin swordfish that was delicious. It was grilled and on top of a hash made of sweet potatoes, brussel sprout leaves, pearl onions & bacon and surrounded by a romesco sauce. So so good. Allegedly pumpkin swordfish is a rare version of swordfish that has an orange tinge to it & is supposedly sweeter than regular swordfish. Whatever it was, it was tasty. My bfriend had the lamb loin. text: In the dead of winter, I wanted soup dumplings, and yelp led me to them, at Dim Sum Garden. It is to yelp I return to sing their praises. A soup dumpling is exactly what it sounds like: it's a fresh dumpling with soup and a nugget of dumpling filling, usually pork or seafood or some combo of the two, inside. It's dumpling soup turned inside out. On a blustery, cold day, it is heaven. Go to Dim Sum Garden - as far as I know they make the only soup dumplings in Philadelphia. Ignore the total lack of atmosphere and the dingy floors. Pay no attention to the eau de bus emanating from the idling Chinatown bus just outside. Order the #2 Steamed Buns w/ Pork & Crab Meat ($5.75). There will be a longish pause, and then a tray of eight soup dumplings will appear. Have both chopsticks and spoon at the ready. Use the chopsticks to gently, carefully lift a dumpling. The hot dough will stick to the dumpling beside it; the chopstick points will threaten to tear the thin membrane. Do not let this happen. Settle the intact dumpling on the spoon. Delicately nip off the top of the dumpling and at the same time slurp out some soup. It is hot and very rich. There is a covered blue and white cup on the table labelled vinegar. Drip a little of this dark vinegar into the dumpling. Its acid will cut and complement the rich broth. Eat the dumpling in two or three more bites. Repeat. I had assumed soup dumplings were an eat at the restaurant kind of food, but tonight I couldn't quite bear the lousy atmosphere, so I performed the to-go experiment. I also ordered scallion pancakes ($2.50) and Beef Brisket Noodle ($5.50). All made it home intact and quite tasty. The pancakes were acceptable, if nothing to write home about. The Beef Brisket Noodle was almost fantastic. I swear the noodles were fresh, and the brisket was tender and deeply flavorful. But the brown sauce, while yummy, was far too salty. I still ate it, of course, but the salt flavor lingers in my mouth.

text: Best Vietnamese in Philly, hands down. I know precisely why this place consistently scores worse than Vietnam Restaurant across the street: it's not as "pretty" (the owners have updated some of the decorations but it doesn't have the hip feel of VR). Also, it features authentic flavors: hot, sweet, sour, grilled, smoky. VR does not--it features the Vietnamese equivalent of American Chinese take-out: tamed ghosts of flavors that used to exist. Back to the Palace. I've been coming to this place since 2001, and I've seen its transformation from hole-in-the-wall to better-heeled. That being said, there are three things that keep me coming back, when normally I'm difficult to please: impeccably fresh and tasty food every single time, exceptionally cheerful, polite wait staff, and a fantastic value for your dollar. Whether you're new to Viet food or a seasoned pro, you'll find something here for you. Their spring rolls are fantastic and a great way to ease nervous eaters in: everyone loves them. The crepe is also awesome (ground pork, shrimp, and bean sprouts). I almost always get the raw beef and lime: tender, perfectly spiced, and amazing on a hot day. For mains, they also have plenty to please: their bo luc lac is fantastic (tender cubes of seasoned tenderloin), as is their salt-battered seafood (a mix of shrimp, scallops, and squid in an air-light crust), whole fried fish, and just about anything in a clay pot (I usually urge my vegetarian friends to try the eggplant in clay pot--delicious). If it's something cold and refreshing you crave, try the bun (layered rice noodles, salad, herbs, and grilled meats), especially the "vermicelli deluxe". For soups, prepare to share: the portions are massive (not even my dad could polish a whole bowl off). Tripe pho is super tasty, as is the roast pork and wonton soup (my go-to on a blustery winter day). Desserts are fairly limited, but all very good: try the coconut ice cream, the taro pudding, or the fabulous rainbow ice. They have a full bar (the lychee cocktail is very tasty), but I don't tend to get alcohol when I'm here, short of a beer. I tend to go for the Thai iced tea or the Vietnamese coffee, both of which are awesome. Give these guys a try. Be a little open-minded and step out of your comfort zone. I think you'll find that you've discovered a new comfort food in its own right.

text: Location, location, location. That is the only possible reason this place is still in business. All of their customers must get drawn in once, get treated poorly, and never return. Hopefully, word of mouth from places like Yelp can prevent other suckers like me from having a crappy experience here. My friend and I arrived just before 11am. I'm talking two or three minutes. The menu said breakfast would be served til 11. My friend wanted the crab cakes off the lunch menu, but was told that only breakfast was being served. He wasn't pleased, but he accepted it and chose the southern omelet instead. I ordered the creole omelet. An auspicious beginning, and it only went downhill from there. The omelets took over HALF AN HOUR to be served. It wasn't like the place was packed; far from it. There were a few tables taken, but it was with diners who arrived AFTER we did. It wasn't like the kitchen was in the weeds. I had a direct view of the kitchen entrance, and it sure didn't look like anyone was scrambling. In fact, I had to concentrate to detect motion. Our server, while nice enough, only appeared once during that time to apologize for the delay, then disappeared, leaving us sitting there with just our waters. Another server stopped by our table and asked if we'd been helped! That's how bad the situation was. Since we had only had water, I wanted to just up and leave, but my friend wanted to at least inform the server. I argued that she had only stopped by to look in on us once in all the time we'd been there, and who knows how long it would be before she would return. He finally acquiesced, and we were just about to leave when our server arrived with the food. The food itself was decent, but in no way should have taken that long to be served. My plate consisted of a couple of scrambled eggs with creole ingredients ladeled over the top, with a scoop of grits and a halved slice of toast. The server added a couple of strips of bacon to make up for the long wait, which was a nice gesture. However, all of the food was on the cold side, which means the plates were probably just sitting there (and NOT under a heat lamp) for some time. The bacon was cooked well before we even sat down. The excuse given to other diners for the delay at their tables (only one table had been served soup) was that the kitchen was transitioning from breakfast to lunch. At least we weren't the only ones being treated badly. By the time we were leaving, no one else was eating. They were all just sitting there like we had been. If it's that big of a hassle to change from breakfast to lunch, then they should just open at 10 without the breakfast menu and hit the ground running. If you live in New Orleans, then I'm sure you're well aware of the problems here. If you're visiting like I was, please take my advice and avoid this place. Despite the great location, there are numerous places within easy walking distance where you won't be treated like an afterthought. This place doesn't deserve your business.

text: So I'm all dolled up in my Easter best, because of course it is Easter, and we head for our reservation at Herbie's for brunch. Upon arriving, I was immediately overwhelmed by the number of pastel-clad Easter folks scurring around the buffet. I felt like I was in Driving Ms.Daisy, and some member of the clan was about to come out of the corner and serve me up some grits. The buffet was a disaster by the time we got there. Our reservation was for 1:30, and being the descent sort of church-going folk that we are (descent I mean, in that we go once a year... actually I hadn't been back since the last Easter...I guess that makes us descent and hypocrites at the same time) Anyway-- our reservation was late because we went to church to celebrate the resurrection, darn it. I didn't expect to get punished later by a brutally torn apart compilation of a 'once was' breakfast smorgasboard. By the time I got a warmed plate into my hands, the filet of salmon was barely recognizable as such, the salad was gone, the dressing was a smeared mess all over the table, hot pans of egg dishes were over steamed and miserable, and my dear, poor, stomach particularly unhappy. I did manage to down some cocktails, though. Two grapefruit and vodkas and a glass of pinot grigio. Our waiter was attentive but seemed stressed, which made my boyfriend stressed out too because he is a waiter and knows what it's like to be over-worked. I felt like the whole thing was just a little out of hand. Perhaps they needed more staff, perhaps they should've made more food. Either way-- it was a pretty under-par experience. I have been to Herbie's when it was really good-- and I'll probably go back again. I certainly won't get suckered into one of their holiday buffets, though.
label: NEG

text: My husband & I went here this weekend for our one year anniversary dinner - and had a great time! We came an hour early and sat in the bar. First of all, the atmosphere was just so cool. The bartenders were exceptional. And the Mademoiselle was deeelish! I'm a sucker for the elderflower liqueur. We tried the rose flight as well, and their special drink. We tried some cheese & olives that were good, and then we were on our way to the table. We had a white flight (contained Gewürztraminer - the others were very fruity, floral as well), and the bubbly flight. Yum! We tried the mushroom garden - stuffed morels, tempura beech clusters & shiitake, and the green tea cream put it completely over the edge!! I wanted a second of this!!! We had a soup flight of carrot-habanero, tom ka, and spring onion. Tom ka was by far the best! I suppose our server told the chef it was our anniversary, so we got a delicious small spoonful each of an effervescent tangerine-ish palate cleanser before dinner! I had the halibut & my husband had the duck. Both dishes were great, on the small side, but with everything else we had they were perfect portions. Then for dessert, our server brought us two glasses of bubbly on the house - we felt so special :) - along with our saffron ice cream dessert. There were several other confections on the plate but I was way-to-full to even go there. Loved the coffee in our own french press - coffee was wonderful. So, summing up our night here, it was fantastic! The service was great, the food was great, and the wine was awesome. We will definitely come back here again for another special occasion. It's a bit pricey for an every day place, but definitely worth it for a special night!!

text: I haven't eaten at too many thai places in philly. In matter of fact, I have no idea where to get good Thai food in philly. The few places I have tried have been subpar, but this place is definitely the worst I have tried. I was thinking of giving them one star, but I wanna reserve one star reviews for places you should never even step foot into even if you were lost and starving and the next place may be miles down the road. I mean how could i give them 1 star. At least their service was kinda attentive. It's not like they told me to get lost or were talking bad things about customers in thai. Firstly, it should be noted I am thai. I can cook more than half the menu in my home at this very moment so I know thai food. This place is definitely not authentic. The food is kind of bland and too sweet. Not many flavors going on. Me and my buddy tried some pretty standard fare. We had the green curry, tod mun (fish cakes), their sausage appetizer, and yum ped (duck salad). The green curry had all these weird flavors and vegetables that I wouldn't want in my curry. Thai green curry is simple; beef, eggplant, maybe bamboo shoots and top it off with kaffir lime leaves. The salad was decent but wasnt spicy enough for me, even though I spoke to them in thai and asked them to make it spicy. Maybe it wasn't spicy enough because my friend was a white dude but still I told them that he could eat spicy food. The fish cakes and sausage were good but it's really hard to mess those up. I've heard good things about siam lotus on spring garden. My roommate says he likes it and our opinions of tamarind are about the same so I wouldn't mind giving it a try the next time I don't feel like cooking and want thai food.

I have to admit I'm from Boston so I don't take kindly to provel, which is in a number of their sandwiches (actually I f**kin hate it - it makes me sick and want to throw up when I'm around it - how does anyone eat that garbage?) So if you're from out of town be sure to replace provel with mozz or cheddar or your favorite. The great news is these guys will do anything for you, so don't let provel in the description keep you away. The main reason I go here all the time is for their meats - ribs, pork steaks and brats are my standards. There is no reason to try anything else because these are so freakin good. The pork steaks are usually extra lean, but they melt in your mouth like a filet mignon (if you cook it right). The ribs are excellent. And the brats are by far the best I've ever tasted. I get at least 2 every time I go here. I will soon probably start to branch out and try their chickens and steaks. I'm sure they'll be just as good as the standards. The LeGrand brothers are the nicest people behind a deli counter that I have ever met. Twice I've been given 2 free brats, and this was before I started frequenting the place. I forgot to mention their sides are amazing as well. The regular coleslaw is some of the best slaw I've ever tasted. You can also select from a decent variety of beer (for the size of the store) and get simple veggies, like peppers and onions, to throw on the grill. Awesome place, awesome meats, awesome experience, awesome service, awesome sandwiches, every time!

text: I visited there the night of the Colts loss on 1/3/2009. We were there at 6:15 (wanted to wrap up early to watch the Colts later.) The place was dead. Nobody goes out when the Colts play... We were seated right away. We had 5 in our group. One showed up late. The interior is very nice, tables are nicely spaced, seems to have the right mix of privacy and intimacy for a bistro. Art from local galleries is on the walls. There is a beautiful bar area to the left of the entry way. If you go to Carmel to peruse the galleries, duck in for a drink. The food was excellent. For starters I would recommend the Foie Gras (my friend let me try his - excellent). I had the Lobster Bisque ($7) special and I highly recommend that at well. My fellow diners also enjoyed the Salade Au Asparagus, and the Salade Organique mixee'. Our entries were also excellent. My wife had the massive and rich Poulet Wellington. My friend had the Lamb Chop (perfectly prepared to a rare/medium rare). I had the Bistro (Veal Medallions served over Yukon Gold Potatoes, Coldwater Lobster Tail, Beurre Vert and Mushroom Demi Glace). It was $40, which I thought was perfectly reasonably priced (it had to cost them $20 in ingredients to put this on the table.) It too, was excellent. I thought the restaurant has sufficient "bistro" credibility, if such a thing exists. I personally did not find the food to be pretentious (e.g. Steak Fritte? Pork Chop with Butternut Squash?) Perhaps my sensitivity to pricing is numbed (living in NJ/NY) but I found the food and the ambiance easily worthy of the prices. Regarding price range, I would say you are going to spend $30-$60 per person. We easily crushed that, because we were on a luxury night out with friends and had cocktails and two $80 bottles of wine on the bill. Desserts were decent. We had a nice creme brule, which is really not that difficult to execute. We didn't try anything else. I downed a Grand Marnier. My only reservation with Bistro de Paris was the service. The young waiter was attentive and almost overly so. We were willing to sit and talk with old friends while we waited for the 5th to join us and he seemed over anxious to process our appetizer and drink orders. In summary, if you are looking for authentic/credible/well executed French bistro food, in an intimate and romantic setting, and aren't afraid of spending $30-$60 per head - this is a nice way to go. If that price point is too steep - look elsewhere.

text: Anyone who knows what over priced, over done and over hyped clothing stores and fashion look like will no doubt find evidence of it at any Blue Bee store (Blue Bee Jeans, Blue Beetle, Blue Bee shoes, ect.) Side note: Blue Bee is famous for having bi-annual, entire store sales that last 3 or more days, with discounts ranging from 50-80%, that many poor suckers will set a 5am alarm for and continue to stalk and camp outside the store until it opens. No hurt feelings intended, but the victims are usually Montecito mothers with nothing else to do but waste their time buying their undeserving, spoiled, teenage daughters new wardrobes every other weekend. You know, something to occupy all there free time. Anyone with half a brain would realize that in order to mark down an entire season's worth of clothing at such outstanding discounts the store has initially overpriced every thing you see more than what is retail norm. So it's really a big joke. Clothing stores only mark down stock that is not selling well and that could become another financial burden if not sold at all. When a store discounts clothes at such rates it usually means they are going out business, unless, like Blue Bee of course, they can still make a growing profit on all those suckers out there and even afford to do it every single passing season. So, please, take caution remember that you (your husband, your parents or maybe even your great grandparents) worked too hard for you to allow yourself to waste your cash in a place that doesn't even appreciate what it is worth.

text: I boarded my dog at Zeus' Place after reading such great reviews from various sources. My husband toured the facilities, and was informed that our dog would be given frequent walks and allowed to play in the yard during the day. As our dog is high-energy and extremely playful, we were excited by this prospect. The first time we viewed our dog on the web cam, we observed a sheet covering his door. While strange, I thought nothing of it. I repeatedly checked on him throughout the day, and each time he was inside his kennel. I understand that it is a boarding facility, and constant human interaction cannot be expected. However, as the human/fellow-dog interaction was one of Zeus' selling points, this was quite disappointing. That night, I again viewed our dog on the web cam. To my horror, he was unattended in his kennel with his pinch collar was around his neck. I was extremely upset, and emailed the facility immediately stating the potential dangers of leaving a dog unattended with a pinch collar. I received a response the following day that took no responsibility for the occurrence, and failed to even attempt an apology. I frequently checked on our dog via the web feed. Two days later, "after hours", I viewed our dog unattended wearing his pinch collar. I was livid. I again emailed, and received an insensitive reply. Once I was home, and had my dog safely in my care, I visited the Zeus Place web cam. There was my dog, still on their feed! It is safe to say, I do not recommend this establishment for boarding.

text: We had a tower room for $150. This hotel offers pretty poor value for that price. If you can get a room for $50, then you're welcome to add a star. The TV was a tiny tube model with a poor picture--NBC was unwatchable. The remote control had no batteries (quickly remedied by maintenance), but one would think that housekeeping would have discovered the flaw. In addition, the clock was flashing the wrong time, another thing one would think housekeeping would fix. A call to housekeeping for an extra set of towels was promptly answered. However, the washcloths were threadbare. The towels were absorbent, if small. Pillows are cheap and thin and extras weren't provided in the room. Decor was unremarkable, but our view of Reno was nice. The pool is okay. We chose this place because they keep the pool open until 10 pm; most casinos close it way too early to force customers into the casinos. Unfortunately, the construction of the new tower means that there are only two relatively small and plain pools, one for kiddies and slightly deeper one. Valet parking was efficient and courteous, but we checked in and out when crowds were low. I'd have rated this place with three stars except that the price was high, and they tried to tack on a nearly $4 "energy surcharge" at check-out, a despicable practice that more and more hotels try to sneak past their customers. The desk clerk removed it when I protested. ("You didn't see the notice on the PIN pad when you checked in?") READ YOUR STATEMENTS, FOLKS! Avoid the automated checkout if you don't want to get ripped off! We ate at the Buffet. The food is average buffet fare, but the price is pretty reasonable, especially if you use a coupon. We got ours buy joining their benefit program. My wife did all the gambling on this trip and she thought the casino was excessively smoky and there weren't enough quarter slots.

The spicy beef enchiladas looked good when they came(Nice presentation). The blue refried beans weren't that great. I ended up putting a bunch of hot sauce to give them some sort of kick. The rice they gave me wasn't remotely mexican or spanish like. It was just regular white rice with some butter or oil on it. The enchiladas were topped with a red sauce and sour cream as well as some queso fresco. However, the red sauce was not spicy at all. The beef was chewy and not tender or for that matter spicy. I ended up pouring a bunch of hot sauce on it to give it a little kick. Sadly, the best parts of the meal was the smile of the waitress and the churro sundae. The churros were nice and crispy and full of cinnamon and the cinnamon ice cream was nice. My service was pretty good. My waitress checked up a couple of times to make sure everything was ok. text: I have a lot of makeup but I didn't know how to really put it on, so I have complaining to my husband that I really wanted someone to teach me how to put on my makeup without looking like an ad for makeup. What if this lesson was like the "lessons" I got at the MAC makeup counter or the Lancome makeup counter? The ones where they make you look like a Rock of Love tramp and then expect you to buy everything. I made the appointment and packed some of my own makeup just in case she wanted to see what I've been using. I arrived at her studio and she was so welcoming. She took my coat and it was as if we were old college friends. She asked me what type of look I was going for and I told her I wanted an everyday look that I can do without a million products and under 10 minutes. This is her speciality. She began by cleansing and moisturing my skin with her own natural products. Makeup and facial products don't have to be made with crazy chemicals and they shouldn't be and Ursula gets that. She's a pro and has been in the entertainment biz so she knows what's good and what's so so bad. The lesson was 90 minutes and she showed me how to use products in many ways. She loves the "two birds with one stone" products so you don't need lots of stuff in your makeup bag. As she was putting in my look on one half of my face, she would carefully explain each step and after she was done, I would put the product on the other half while she coached me through it. While I was afraid of color, brow pencil, blush, and bronzerI am a true convert now. I even got a step by step how-to written down for me with an almost color by number picture I can use when I reproduce the look tomorrow. She is friendly, knowledgeable, and professional. Her studio is so relaxing and I kinda want to go back just so I can hang out and talk. Her products are great too and she totally doesn't push you to buy them (which is so great). Bottom line: go! They have makeovers, facials, sugaring, and quality products (I got the brow pencil and concealer).

text: Food is simple yet very tasty. We came here for lunch and left very happy. We started with a dozen raw oysters, a staple of our meals in New Orleans. Luke sources them from P&J, so they were on par with those at Deanie's and Acme's. For our main course, we split a bowl of the seafood gumbo and the pressed sandwich of whole roast "cochon de lait" (pork). The portion of gumbo wasn't very big, but it was filled with seafood, including a whole chunk of shell-on crab in the middle. The sandwich was much bigger, and featured some of the best sandwich bread I've ever had - very crispy yet buttered thoroughly. The meat was tender though a teeny bit dry - I got over this by slathering copious amounts of delicious cherry mustard onto it. The sandwich came with cones of hot and crispy fries. Service is very good. When we told them we were splitting the food, they split the sandwich and fries for us in the kitchen so we got separate plates. The french press coffee was so good that I had two pots. Prices for lunch are reasonable. They have a great $15 lunch prix fixe menu as well.

Decor: Some people care about this, and I like a nice environment, which All India Cafe has. text: On paper, this sounds like everything I want in a restaurant: local, organic, vegan and vegetarian friendly. I went here with a group of four, three of us arriving late due to the shoddy location and signage. Once we sat down, we had to wait ten minutes for our server to show her face and another thirty-five minutes to receive our food, even though there were only four other tables full when we ordered. The appetizer we ordered never came, and once our meals arrived, we were As others have stated, the portions are incredibly small. In fact, not only are they small, they're almost selfish. I envisioned my raw marrakesh as a decadent pile of ripe organic veggies with a pile of creamy hummus, so when it came - four tiny avocado slices on a slim layer of veggies, the hummus spread frugally over a single romaine leaf - I wondered if it was an elaborate vegan joke. My companions' plates were similarly anemic, and though all the food was tasty enough, not one was worth the price. Sabrina's Favorite Sandwich had tasty onion bread and hummus, but aside from that it was almost entirely lettuce. $16 for flatbread, hummus, untestable "sheeze" and that most generously priced vegetable. The most carnivorous ordered the ginger chickun, and said that while it tasted fine, he would have rather gotten twice the amount for half the price at the food court. I wonder if the meal had been cheaper or more generous if they might have won a convert willing to admit that meat isn't necessary at every meal? That would be out of line with the unspoken motto of the restaurant: "We don't just hate meat," Grassroots seems to say. "We hate food." Even looked at as an exercise in vegan food, they fall short. Where on the menu are the savory nuts, the valiant eggplant, the humble bean and the wonderful-when-done-right tofu? (There's teriyaki tofu listed online, but it didn't appear on the physical menu.) And for goodness sake, would it kill them to give freely of the avocado, since it's local produce, and hummus, since it's so damn cheap to make? This restaurant does nothing to refute the notion that vegs are rich, lettuce-nibbling wimps, incapable of creating food to satisfy the masses, either in a culinary or satiating sense. I believe the only reason Grass Root has survived is that they are the only game in town, a sort of vegan restaurant mafia. My advice? Next time you're craving a nice vegan meal, look up a recipe you've never tried before and do it yourself. Sure, that defeats the purpose of going out to eat, but since one companion could easily point out the bits of decor available at Wal-Mart, you're not missing out on much in the way of ambiance. Plus, you'll always be able to find your server.

text: Right off the bat, this review is more so about the way this theater is mismanaged than it is a review of the theater itself. First, let's talk about the theater. It is a truly beautiful facility inside. I absolutely love the decor and style. It is a unique fixture on a street that I wish could find a way to jump start. Even though it seems to have cost a ton to restore, I think it was worth it (one could however, provide a reasonable argument otherwise). In the decade or so that I have lived in Tucson, it showed me that at least some things could find a way to reach completion (Rio Nuevo anyone??). Another plus is that they sell Nimbus Beer. Nice to see them vending local brew. Also, the staff really does seem to try to be helpful, courteous, and professional. At least that was the feeling I got from the handful of shows I have seen here. That all said, there really are no good shows that come to this theater. It is simply not used for live performances as much as it should be. Instead, it is a glorified movie theater for re-airing old classics. Yeah, this has it's place, but really, why spend that much money restoring a theater to only really use it more or less as a clubhouse for you and your aging friends to "relive the glory days" of theater. And that, sadly, seems to be what the committee that operates the Fox is intent on doing. I believe they have fallen into the fear that if they allow live acts to dominate the stage, then the place will be torn apart. So instead, they have a beautiful theater that is really under-used. Sad in my opinion. But to leave on a positive note: if you do decide to maybe take a date down to the Fox for, say, an airing of Casablanca, make sure to head to the balcony to settle in to one of the love seat-style chairs. What a great touch for a balcony!

text: I really didn't want my very first Yelp review to be a bad one. I have a list of about 5 amazing places that I'd like to carve out the time to review, including Amis and Sampan, but it just seems like words of disappointment and frustration are easier to write. I went with three of my friends to the Brauhaus on Saturday. We got there at 7 and put our name on the list. The hostess told us it would be an hour, so we settled down in a couple of chairs and a bench behind the bar area, ordered a couple of rounds of beer, and hung out. At around 7:45, we checked in with the hostess again, and she mentioned that we were still fifth on the list, and that it would be about 35 more minutes, for a total wait of about 1:20. Still fine by us. Some of us got some more beer (all told, we spent over $60 on beer while waiting). Shortly after that, we watched a party of no less than twenty filing up the stairs. I turned to my friends and said, "There's no way they'll be able to seat us in half an hour. They just sat a quarter of their dining room in one shot." At around 8:40, from upstairs, the hostess made eye contact with us. She came down the stairs and made a beeline toward us. "Finally," we said among ourselves. She then demanded -- without any "please" or pleasantries at all -- that we give up the chairs we'd been sitting in, because another table needed them. She also told us that we were still third on the list, behind a party of six and a party of four. Fast forward to 9:00, when we had been waiting for two hours. A gentleman (owner? manager?) who had previously been seating people was then standing right across from us, having a beer with his friend. At that time, we learned from the hostess that, even though I could eyeball three empty tables, we were no closer to being sat than we were twenty minutes previously. The gentleman heard us complaining among ourselves and engaged us -- not to apologize, or smooth our ruffled feathers, but to say, "What do you expect us to do? Demand people leave?" I think we were pretty patient as we explained that our issue was largely that no one was managing our expectations, and that the only time anyone actively reached out to us was to demand we give up our seats. I told the gentleman that, having been in the business, I found it unrealistic for them to quote an hour wait when they knew they'd be seating a party of 20+ on a Saturday night, and that if we'd known it would have been more than a 2 hour wait, we would have gone somewhere else and hit the Brauhaus another time. The establishment's failure to properly manage its seating process cost us (and a bunch of other grumbling would-be patrons) a nice Saturday evening. text: We went downtown to look for furniture at Macy's, Niche, and Atom (great contemporary things, BTW) and happened to run across this place. What a good find. It's not the best Asian food in the world, but it's pretty damn good. First of all, it's not a Chinese restaurant - it's sort of fusion Asian - a little Chinese (lemon chicken, beef brocoli), a little Vietnamese (fresh spring rolls), a little Thai (tom yum soup, pad thai), a little Japanese (chicken teriyaki, tempura shrimp), a little Malaysian/Singaporean (satay and mee) - but all good. I like buffets and they have a moderately sized buffet. We went on Friday for lunch ($9.95) and the place was full by noon. It's clean and upscale with Asian servers in the front of the house and Latin American cooks in the kitchen (it's a midwest thing). The fried fish (pollack) was especially good, like they used the breading from good calamari and dipped the fish in that and fried it. Very good. And Asian buffets (especially of the Chinese type) are not known for their desserts. You get the jello/jelly (usually red) and almond cookies and some canned and, if you are lucky, fresh fruit. Well they had a nice little coconut cake and and a very good tiramisu and something they call "honey pineapple" which is in a ball and deep fried and sweet. Surprisingly good. Oh, and one more thing, the teriyaki chicken was very good too, they actually grilled the chicken over a flame with some smoky and charcoal tastes before adding the teriyaki sauce. Tasty. If you're downtown and want a good Asian buffet, this is your place and it's right across the street from 400 Olive - a good martini bar. So, go there for a few drinks and walk across the street to the Bamboo Bistro for some very good Asian fusion food. It's worth it.

text: Having to write this review for Stella is very upsetting for me. I had an amazing time in New Orleans and tasted some of the most wonderful foods I have yet to encounter (having been to many countries in Asia and Europe). However, Stella definitely did not make my list of memorable dinning experiences. My friend and I did some research prior to our trip and decided that we would splurge one evening and treat ourselves to a high end restaurant. We read through several menus and reviews and decided that Stella looks like an innovative fine dining restaurant with a creative menu. We made reservations in person as we explore the French Quarters and after we saw the venue (very pretty!) we were really excited about our dinner the next night. Upon arrival we felt a extreme stiffness in the air, unlike everywhere else we have been in New Orleans. Note that we are from Boston, so we are used to uptight, stiffy environments but this was way worse. After the long almost ceremonial services the wait staff provide to get you started on dinner, we finally decided that the tasting menu (our original plan) looked dull and we would order: (1) Louisiana Gulf Shrimp and Chanterelle and Lobster Mushroom Risotto with English Peas, Local Scallions and Virgin Olive Oil (2) Lobster, Eggs and Truffles ~ Canadian Lobster, Clyde's Farm Araucana Egg and Italian Summer Truffles (3) Salad with lump crab meat and avocado salsa. (4) Duck Five Ways ~ Szechwan Seared Breast, Lacquered Leg and Thigh, Moo Shoo Pancake Stir-Fry, Duck Miso Broth, Foie Gras Won Tons and Currant Cassis Reduction (5)Miso and Sake Glazed Japanese Mero Seabass with Udon, Green Tea and Soba Noodles, Petite Asian Greens and Shark's Fin, Crab and Lobster Broth The risotto was delicious, good portion for appetizer and I was highly satisfied. However, everything started going downhill from there on. The lobster/egg/truffle dish was very original and appealing but the semi-cooked egg and truffle over powers the whole thing and I didn't even know what I was eating--it was rather confusing, not in a very good way. The crab meat salad had decent amount of crab in it, but almost no "salad"--it was taken over by an army avocado (I love avocados btw, but that was way too much) and didn't have the crisp refreshing lightness a salad should have. The entrees turn out to be the most disappointing of the evening. Duck Five Ways felt like a waste of a perfect opportunity for the chef to do some cool tricks and the Seafood Udon was just...common. The seared breast (tender) and the Foie Gras Won Tons (juicy/tasty) were the only part of the dish that we thought was done at a reasonable standard but nothing extraordinary. The duck miso soup tasted nothing like miso soup and was way too salty and weirdly sweet. The Lacquered Leg and Thigh was a complete waste a good piece of duck meat, it was all black and hard and I seriously cannot describe how strange it was. The Udon was nothing special, I thought it was a disservice to the amazing ingredient involved. ****For all those people out there impatient to read my super long review, read this part**** Other than the not-so-impressive foods, Stella's service was ceremonial and CREEPY! I enjoy high end fine dining service but it was different this time. The wait staff literally would not "leave you alone" standing at every corner of the room, STARING as you eat and drink...watching your every move... while they "WHISPER" into each others ears chit-chatting about who knows what. So, were we being spied? I don't know, but it sure felt like it. I hope they read yelp and will try to improve their restaurant, it has so much potential but it was so disappointing.

text: Oh, Yelp, why do you make me give a star to the lowliest of businesses? Reece Builders sells "Magic Glass" windows through in-home installations. Let me say up front that my husband and I were entirely confident that theirs were likely the best windows we would find anywhere. However, we will never purchase anything from this company and for good reason. Anyone who has ever gotten an in-home estimate for any product or service knows that there are two types of salesmen: the one who has evolved and understands that high pressure tactics just don't cut it anymore; and the one who still drags a club trying to scare you into submission. Take one guess as to which salesman rang my doorbell. After 45 minutes of reading the individual warranties of competitor companies, and making my husband read portions of them aloud, we learned the prices of their windows reached into the thousands. This being our first home and never having purchased windows before, we had grossly underestimated the cost. We stopped him there and, being the good Samaritans that we are, explained that we didn't want to waste his time since we could already tell we weren't going to purchase anything. To make a long story short, he insinuated the very real possibility that he could lose his job if he left earlier than the length of the presentation. In hindsight, I see that we should have said, "Tough cookies," and sent him packing. Who doesn't love hindsight? But being the kind young couple we are, we sucked it up and said he could finish, but made it clear that we couldn't afford the windows. To be honest, the thought of spending thousands of dollars on windows, when the ones I have still open and close with good old fashioned elbow grease, was absurd. But to alleviate his perception of a failed pitch, and to discourage his high pressure routine, we explained that, in addition to being newlyweds, we were both full-time students in our first house. This insight, coupled with a quick inventory of our home, led him to make incorrect inferences about our financial situation. After a few phone calls to his supervisor in which he explained our unwillingness to make a purchase, he relayed inappropriate questions to us in an unmistakable attempt at bullying us into submission. The final attempt was a blatantly sarcastic question as to how much the value of our home was increased by the purchase of our 40" flat screen TV. (Although I didn't say it at the time, I think my husband would agree that particular living room staple has brought countless hours of priceless high definition joy to both our lives.) Before my ordinarily patient husband could take a swing, I politely ended the conversation while grinding my molars to stubs. Once the longest 2 hours of my life had ended and the devil's minion had finally retreated into his $40,000.00 car, we each took a shot of whiskey and waited for our respective blood pressures to return to normal. The representatives of this company are rude, unprofessional, and manipulative. Save yourselves!

Whatever. What I can't understand is why they would then have hotel rooms on the first floor? Why?! There is a door dividing the lobby and the hotel, but that door has no knob or keyed entry. Anyone can pass through and hang out. And that's what's happening right now. I've called the front desk twice to beg them to clear out the people that are in the hallway. At one point I personally walked the hotel manager back to my room to show her what was going on. She was pissed at these people, but nothing changed. I actually got yelled at by one of the people she was kicking out. It's like the hotel is being run by a bunch of teenagers. I never do crap like this, but I'm calling the hotel manger tomorrow as well as the guest services director. And just in case you're wondering, it's not convenient to downtown Philly and while it is close to the airport I would hate for you to be booked into a room on the bottom floor as I was because you checked in late and then be kept awake all night. How pleasant would that be?

text: LOVE this place! We've taken two sets of out-of-town guests here because we were looking for a vegetarian place in NOLA. A bit hard to come by. I found it on Yelp and had a great experience both times as did all of our guests. The servers/chefs/owners are personable and extremely knowledgeable, with great recommendations on things to try. The food (in traditional New Orleans style) is truly unique and delicious but doesn't leave you with that heavy feeling many places around here do. It's pretty fusion-tastic with ingredients like corn fungus, but I have yet to try anything bad off the menu and I sampled off of almost everyone's plates! The meat dishes are as good as the veggie ones. Things to be aware of: It's quite small. We did easily fit a group of 8, but it was pure luck that the only two large tables (which are next to one another) were both open (tho I think there is a back room and during nice weather, there is outdoor seating); the portions are not huge; it's a little pricey (about $15/plate); the menu is small but changes regularly (or so I hear). I love it's location, a true hole-in-the-wall. I hope it stays a local secret for a while longer! Check it out, you'll love it!

text: I'm again conflicted about giving this identity crisis Japanese & Korean restaurant only one star, so I'm settling on two STARS. It seems that any time I show up at a Japanese/Korean restaurant, something isn't quite right. See my other review on Daruma in Jersey (see: http://www.yelp.com/biz/I67MQNC8sYjqIjsz-8bwkg#hrid:zpP1pY81x-NmF6YELUMVgQ ). I came here with extremely, high expectations. At Kabuki, I concur with Chris L. and Dave H., service is too slow. On a Sunday night there was only one server and it took almost 30 minutes for us to order after we sat down tonight at 7:00PM. (-2 STARS) I ordered two items: 1) Crunchy Spicy Tuna - nice portion and nice presentation. Excellent fresh flavor. This Spicy Tuna is not pre-made. It seemed made to order and was good quality tuna. The crunch was a nice touch. I would definitely have this again. Oddly enough, a normal spicy tuna roll is $7.00, yet a crunchy spicy tuna is only $6.50. I should have concluded my meal with this item. Unfortunately, I didn't and ordered an entree. The sushi rolls and sashmi all seemed excellent and probably warrant a higher rating. 2) Curry Rice with Chicken : This dish was a BIG disappointment. The only plus was that the Curry was good flavor and nice and spicy. Otherwise, the curry was too watery and runny. The portion was extremely generous with chicken breast meat however it sucks to have huge portions of mediocre food. That's more like a punishment. In addition, this Curry Rice had slices of napa cabbage, red pepper, and way too many sliced onions. I've never seen a curry plate like this before. I'm used to having just potatoes and carrots with Beef in my Curry Rice. Comes with White Rice and even this was poor!!! It was a little too dry and tasted old (ie not fresh) like it was made many hours earlier. The little details matter. The hot entrees come with Miso Soup and a Chilled Salad with a Ginger dressing. I would NOT recommend this dish. (-1 STAR) Final verdict: - Don't go for Korean food, there are no traditional items like Bulgogi, Kalbi, Tofu Soups, or Bi Bim Bop. - Don't go for hot Japanese dishes. - The ONLY safe bet is the fresh and tasty sushi and/or sashimi. + 1 STAR for friendly sushi chef Kenny. pix laters...

text: So, this place has been open for all of two weeks, and we have been four times, twice for brunch (Sat. and Sun.) and twice for dinner. We have learned that when a kitchen kicks out such high level food like this, you go as often as possible while you can still get in. This chef's food (Chef Nick) is perfect--the flavors sing, and there is the right balance of elements and portions that you leave full and happy, but not overwhelmed. He has a full crew back there, and they take pride in their work. Highlights so far--pork, chicken entree, the braised lamb shank, perfect Fritata at brunch (light and delicious), awesome eggs benedict with a nice (but not overwhelming) truffle flavor, and, if that weren't enough, a savory bread pudding on top of chorizo sausage. All at an excellent value. Knowledgeable servers include Zack, who could probably host his own food (or wine) show, and the front of the house run by Hector, who is enthusiastic about the entire experience. This is a true gem, with the added benefit of neighborhood flair.

text: My wife hails from Norristown, so to her, this is an institution. For an outsider like myself, it's a trip back in time....and I'm big into time travel. Located on Main Street, this is a place that seemingly hasn't changed since it opened some sixty years ago. The wood booths are classic, and very tight (made for 1950's people who were much smaller) and the atmosphere is right out of a Scorcese flick. Lots of banter and bustle, and the food is brought out quick and fresh. And the food...well let's just say you'd kill your Weight Watchers point total for the week here before you finished your Zep. And what's a zep? It's pure heaven, that's what it is. Or hell, if you care about cholesterol and longevity. A zep is simply a sandwich on a Conshohocken round roll that's jam packed with cold cuts, cheese, condiments, etc. I had the cheesesteak zep which, if my doctor was there, would have ordered an angioplasty on the spot. A cheesesteak WITH cold cuts between the bun. Man was it good. Lou's also serves breakfast, but I've never had it. The zeps are just too tasty. Inexpensive, a lot of local Norristown flavor, and honest food that will lead you to an early grave, this is a must! What, you want to live forever??

text: There's no place like produce junction if you're looking to stock up on good, cheap fruits and vegetables. They also sell quite a bit of flowering plants at exceptionally reasonable prices. When I say cheap, I mean vegetable and fruit for a family of four for a week for under $20. There are a few things to keep in mind. Go early. This place gets packed. It's nothing to stand behind twenty people in line. Seriously. This food is not organic. For the prices, I don't ask a lot of questions. I'm using this in soups or cooking it with other products (or squeezing it into a beverage), so I'm not too picky about the fact that it's probably grown on top of a jersey landfill. I have yet to find anything that glowed in the dark, but for the prices, I wouldn't be terribly surprised. This food is cheap. I mean like a dollar for five pounds of carrots, or a whole watermelon, or a dozen limes! This is 'Uncle Jimmy that works for the you know who' cheap. If you're on a budget, you can't beat the prices anywhere. The other day was a dozen oranges for a dollar, two pounds of strawberries for a dollar, and two dozen eggs for a dollar. Can't beat that. Oh - they sell eggs too. The food is good. It's not organic, but it's not crap either. Some items are more perishable than what you may get at the supermarket (I've found tomatoes have a shelf life of two or three days). So go early, don't get caught up in the cheapness and overbuy, and enjoy!
