text: Thumbs down on Breakfast at Brennan's. It wasn't just overpriced; the food was substantially worse than what you'd get at a diner or coffee shop. It was heavy and bland. I do not recommend eating here. If, despite all the warnings, you really need to have Flaming Bananas for breakfast, note that you do NOT have to order the 3-course breakfast. The menu doesn't say this, but just ask and you can order a la carte. The details: I'm a big fan of corned beef hash, so the Eggs Owen sounded promising. Alas, the hash was a too-salty stew-like concoction of hamburger and a few lonely potato cubes. More like the bottom of a Shepherd's pie? In any case, it was yucky and I barely ate any of it. Eggs Benedict were served on a "Holland Rusk", which turns out to be a circular piece of wonder-bread-style toast. Eggs were poached ok, but hollandaise sauce was gloppy and not fresh tasting. Strawberry flaming dessert (aka Crepes Fitzgerald) was entertaining, but overly sweet. The sauce started its life as fresh strawberries (we saw them with our own eyes), but after being doused with butter, maraschino liquor, etc, they sadly ended up tasting like thawed frozen strawberries. The one redeeming thing we were served were the mimosas - Brennan's did an excellent job of mixing champagne and OJ.

text: I chose this spot for my birthday lunch yesterday after reading about the $9.99 lunch special. FYI - they don't take reservations. Myself and 3 co-workers ventured over in the pouring rain. When we walked in we realized we wouldn't have had to make reservations anyways...it was pretty empty. We were immediately seated and given a ton of menus. Lunch specials, regular menu, drink menu...way too much going on! We decided on a pitcher of the frozen pineapple margaritas. These were absolutely delicious but I think they made mango instead of pineapple. We order our food and our waiter said he would bring us chips and salsa. We must have waited about 15 minutes before we got our chips. They chips were fresh made and came with 3 salsas which were pretty decent. Of course our 1st course comes out a minute later... Myself and another got the tortilla soup and the other 2 each got a salad which was given to the wrong person and the dressing was not on the side (they didn't know because you would never be able to tell which is which until you started to eat a few bites) so they had to be sent back. Another salad is brought out and she made a face after tasting it...I tried it and when I tell you it was salty oh my freaking god! I love salt but this was like a whole salt shaker was spilled on it. So it had to be sent back AGAIN. The tortilla soup was the most FOUL thing I have ever tasted or smelled, my friend that also got it agreed. I love tortilla soup and will eat almost anything but this was bad, as my friend put it it smelled like the Philadelphia Zoo (she wouldn't even taste it). (this is not an exaggeration either, I would have normally sent it back but we had already sent 2 dishes back and honestly I just didn't feel like waiting and my appetite had almost diminished) After that course we were pretty bummed out about the meal. Our second courses came out and they were better but nothing noteworthy. The chef sent out a complimentary dessert--I appreciated his trying to remedy the situation. It's a shame because I think they are really trying but I don't know... the whole place just isn't right... I left with such a sick feeling stomach and that lasted until about 8pm that evening :( I won't be back here.

text: Great selection and reasonable prices in a charming little store. The floors are hardwood, the staff is friendly, and you will likely see a golden retriever laying around in some corner of the store. This is a cozy little place to buy your provisions without having to deal with Cool Springs. It is conveniently located right next to Publix, so you can pull one of those, "well, since I'm already here I might as well go in and look". The wine selection is good and the staff is knowledgeable if you have any questions. They are known for Scotch and have quite a few to choose from. I found some great tequila prices here too. Their newest endeavor brings them into the world of beer. I love the selection. One of the beers I really missed from New York was Ommegang from Cooperstown. Their Rare Vos is an amazing Belgian White that is flavorful and delicate. This is the only place so far that I have found in Nashville that carries this product. text: Hipsters and rockers unite to drink cheap beer and dance to good music! Sometimes you can park in the lot across the street, sometimes you have to stick to the street. Come on in, sit at the bar, order a drink that is never watered down, and look around. There is a stage and a pool table, a big TV always playing some awesome movie, and plenty of seating. The best thing about this place, besides the fact that they carry my favorite vodka, is that everyone is welcome here. text: Would've given 3.5 stars but I'll give them the benefit of the doubt. 4.5 stars for the tap list. 4 stars for the food. A great amount of food but not the most well considered menu for vegetarians (though I am not!). The pizza was better than expected and the bruschetta was alright - the bread was a little too thick and dry. We also tried the sweet potato fries with the 2 different sauces. I thought the fries were great on their own and the sauces interesting, but less so. I also had the herb chicken with fingerling potatoes. I was expecting both the chicken and potatoes to have more of a crispy skin and instead both were kinda soggy. Service was really slow though and the only reason I was grateful was that it allowed me a little more time to digest the Dining Day bounty. Our waiter was knowledgeable about the menu but would make sweeps across the tables in our section and then not appear again for another half hour. Our dinner took 3 hours and it being a school night, we weren't entirely pleased. All in all though, I'm glad we tried the joint and will be back. Would love to see a few more interesting vegetarian options and more consistent service.

text: Stick with the Iron Chefs, the Food Network knows what it's doing. Went here to take advantage of the $15 lunch special and it certainly was special. The ambiance is really, well, PINK. Both were delicious, but the gazpacho with lump crab meat was more subtle and hit the right balance of pre-dessert sweet. For my entree, I got the forest mushroom and truffle flat bread. I thoroughly enjoyed my first time at Distrito and will definitely go again for a very well-thought out and delightfully pink dining experience.

Sorta similar when you order Coke at some Asian places- they bring you a can of soda and a cup of ice. Thought this was weird, but whatev. We got the broccoli rabe and some meatballs as appetizers. text: The only thing I can really say I don't like about this place is that so many of the seafood dishes look SO delicious it makes me upset that I can't eat them. The chef at this restaurant is a native of Mexico and therefore, really knows how to cook this food. He has been doing this for 25 years, so he has perfected his recipes and not one that I have had has been bad. The atmosphere is wonderful, dim but not so dim that you can't read the menu, plenty of color and the place is usually packed but not so loud that you can't have a decent conversation. Also, the mixed drinks are nothing short of fantastic. They actually put alcohol in them, but not to the point of overpowering. I love their margaritas...nothing better than washing down a plate of spicy rice and beans with a well made margarita. Oh, and the guacamole....yummy yummy yummy. It's some of the best fresh guacamole I have had in the St. Louis area. Two people won't run you a huge bill, unless you are really into the drinking either. Perfect place to grab a decent meal on a weeknight or to start your weekend off. AWESOME!

The bad news, Pizzology is in Carmel. That means I had to drive there. I think this place needs to be in the city of Indianapolis and not in a strip mall off of a roundabout. text: Like the Food Network Show, I can say that this is the best Southern food I ever ate! No joke. If you are ever in Nashville, you MUST go here! What is great is the place is historic. The wait can be long, but it was worth it for my group of 12. We waited outside in the really nice garden area, and we were soon seated in the front part of the building, which is brick on the outside. I've only had the dinner, so that's the only thing I can comment about, but it was amazing. The spread of family style servings of food will make your mouth water. You definitely need to come hungry, or at least practiced stretching out your stomach for a week to be able to eat the amount of food that will be placed on your table! I loved the family style buffet style dinner. We had our own table, but the table next to us had 3 different groups. It really proves that meals are a social treat. You get to pass around huge plates and bowls of food. Everything from the salad to the banana pudding (yum) are really great. The chicken is just how you'd imagine, cooked to perfection, and the mac and cheese makes you feel right at home. The green beans, mashed potatoes, and coleslaw are more then acceptable, and once you thing you've had enough, the servers will ask if you would like anything more. We politely declined to more main courses, but we had to have another bowl of the banana pudding. They weren't lying when they said we would want another bowl! I won't say too much about the food because it changes from night to night, but any review that is positive is probably correct. It is that good! You will feel as if you need to "roll out" of there, literally. I have to say, the atmosphere is fun, inviting, warm, and lively. The people around you are into the meal, feel as if we were in someone's home rather then the restaurant. So, come to Monell's for great food, great company, and great service! The price of dinner (or any other meal) can't be beat when you're hungry! You won't be disappointed...unless you dislike eating awesome food!

text: Debreaux's is a little restaurant located in the Overbrook train station in the Wynnfield section of Philly. I have been going here for Delicious soul food for years. They have a small dinning room with hand painted orchids, the owner's favorite flower, on the tables I went there with Peggy, a friend from Zimbabwe for dinner. We both ordered the Fried Chicken, Collard Greens and Baked Macaroni & Cheese. A plate of hot, buttery Cornbread came out first. It was absolutely Delicious.! The Cornbread was moist and a little sweet and I it felt like I was having dessert first. It was so good, I had to give it the "fat man's napkin" you know, finger licking good! The entrees came out and the chicken was so crisp, when I tried to penetrate the skin, you heard a loud crunch. Then when my fork and knife got past the skin, juices squirted out of the chicken! It was a crunchy, savory experience. The Collards had that smokey, old time flavor and the Mac & Cheese was excellent. Everything I've tried here was indeed excellent, but as usual with most Soul Food spots, it takes a long time to get your food. text: I just bought my first bicycle! Weeee! I haven't ridden since I was 12 so I sort of just wanted to buy a $20 beater off of craigslist and re-learn to ride. text: To be honest I would say this place was very disappointing. I would recommend that it apply for help from "Kitchen Nightmares" because it is confused and sub par for the image it is trying to portray. Its a modern building with interesting architecture and simple designs. The fact that my appetizer plate was crusted with something and my napkin had lipstick on it really didn't bother me. I was still willing to give the food a chance. Things were looking good when the corn fritter appetizer arrived. It was the highlight of the meal. The waiter was completely pretentious and distracted. He literally walked away mid-sentence while telling us the specials and came back 5 minutes later to finish. I ordered the spicy noodles with chicken and my wife ordered pad thai, both traditional dishes that didn't offer much risk. My dish was completely over salted and had an overpowering taste due to the excessive amount of sliced lime leaves in the dish. It was not even mediocre, it was way to strong and salty to enjoy. Then it got even worse when I tasted my wife's dish. It looked like a traditional pad thai but half of the noodles tasted as if they had been cooked and then dried out offering a stale texture with the rest of the overcooked soft noodles. It was not in any way pleasing to the mouth. She ate a few bites and gave up. I have to say that this place gets very low scores for food. The menu is way too complicated and includes lamb, pork, duck, chicken, beef, seafood and veggie sections. There is just too much going on. For a place that only has about 10 tables and clearly was not going to turn over each one on a Friday night I don't know how you can justify having so many meat options. You have to question the freshness of any of the ingredients. The most ridiculous part of the menu is the dessert. There must have been 10 items on the dessert tray that included chocolate souffle and other items you would see at a nice french restaurant. Again, even if they were good, you don't need 10 of them and they certainly cant be made fresh every day. I finish with the waiter. He introduced the predictable bottle of Ferrari-Carano Cabernet Sauvignon as going well with any of the three specials (three specials, are you serious?) that included filet mignon and seafood. It was clear he knew nothing about wine and that this place is struggling with identity like a freshman in high school.
label: NEG

text: I have ordered hot ham and cheese subs there twice. They make them with French bread. A very good sub. It's a nice change from the chain sub shops. The food has a noticible Greek flavor to it. text: The Seattle take, as I'm a transplant from the java city: Park Ave - It has a quaint location, which offers a lot of potential, though it seems they're wasting it. Also, what's with all the gooey cake reviews when this is a "coffee house"? Let's talk about the coffee, because that should be the main interest here. On our last and only visit, the Mrs. and I both ordered coffee drinks, mine being an Americano, as that is usually my preferred drink for getting a sample of the quality of any shop's espresso. We were both disappointed. It was just as burnt as *$'s. The baristi were sociable and helpful, but I didn't go there for that. If I pay over $1.50 for any coffee drink, I expect satisfaction in the cup. I want to sip that sweetness and drift off to some foreign port, not cringe and regret the expense. I would encourage Park Ave to get involved with the SCAA and maybe get some tips to better their business. Perhaps, sample some coffees from another roaster, though there aren't many in StL. It's great to support local roasters, but it's no good to lose customers over bad tasting coffee. I wish them the best!

text: Maybe it's because I'm a bit Italian, maybe it's because I've been to a ton of family owned Italian restaurants or maybe it's because I know how to cook, but for whatever reason, after my second visit to Ralph's, I feel I can do better. First the good points, the place seems to get a good crowd The decor and staff are what you'd expect at an Italian American restaurant. And that's really about it. I ordered the veal "marsala." I was intrigued by the use of sherry instead of the traditional Marsala wine, from which the dish gets its name. Absent was the prosciutto and light brown sauce you'd expect. In their place was a strangely fatty creamy broth into which were placed a few veal slices along with the expected mushrooms. If you're going to call a dish something, then for the love of God and all that's holy, use the correct ingredients. Sherry comes from Spain and Marsala comes from Sicily. They don't even taste the same. The broccoli and escarole as a side dish was much better. However, it doesn't take much effort to properly steam something and then season it. Now about the server, when I asked which RED wines they had by the glass, the server listed Pinot Grigio and one or other whites,..huh? Also, five minutes after you've served the food don't come back and ask if we need anything. Obviously not, you just served the food. Also it's 2009, learn how to run a credit card machine. That's perhaps acceptable at a BYOB but not at places that charge PA restaurant prices for a bottle of wine. Most people don't carry around more than $50 in cash with them and it's just tacky to have an ATM on the premises that you're making money off with fees.

text: I'm not one for reviewing chain restaurants, but this service situation seriously warrants warning. I, for one, make a point to park and go into a restaurant rather than using the drive through. Unfortunately, our culture has trained these places to serve the drive through. We stood at the counter for 5 minutes before anyone even acknowledged us. The lady working the drive through window was moving the fastest of anyone in the place. Finally someone stepped up to the counter, but just stared at us for another minute before asking to take our order. By the time we ordered, there was quite a line behind us (it was noon, and definitely peak ordering time). We waited significantly longer than usual to get our food, though I won't quantify the amount of time, because when you're hungry and smelling French fries, time definitely slows. text: I decided to visit the Philadelphia portion of Yelp just to give kudos to Blarney South. We came for a pre-season Eagles game and bummed around Philadelphia a bit. I found a gift certificate for Blarney South on Restaurant.com that was a really good deal. 50% off your order for $3. We came on a Thursday night and hesitated a bit in the doorway because the bar is actually situated near the front and we brought our 8 and 12 year olds along with us. They brought us right in and took us to the back, which was set up more like a restaurant. My husband had the most beautiful bacon bleu cheese burger I've ever seen. It was huge with no less than four thick slices of bacon and plenty of bleu cheese crumbles. I honestly don't know how he got his mouth around it, but he managed and it was gone (every last crumb) in no time flat. My older son had a chicken cheese steak, which he said was good, and I had a crab cake sandwich, which was good and filled with crab, but I was yearning for a bite of hubby's burger. My youngest, who just got braces put on a week before and had mouth sores, had potato soup. He told me that I HAD to learn to make it. The fries were great. They were all we had left at the end of our meal and we packed them all into a styrofoam container and took them back to the hotel with us. Service was great. The waitress seemed taken with my younger son (I'm sure it had nothing to do with him playing to her sympathies by refusing to talk and answering with a simple thumbs up or thumbs down) and gave him some extra bread and butter to take back along with some extra soup. We're craving that burger... I just wish it weren't so expensive! ($8 for the burger, $400 for the plane ticket!)

text: My roomate is constantly raving about the breakfasts she gets from here and I thought it'd be a perfect place to take my bf who loves ordering mexican style dishes at brunch.We made it there by 12, but they stopped serving the breakfast menu already. text: Went here for dinner and must say it was one of the better PF Chang's that I have been to. It is a little smaller than most PF Chang's in bigger cities (NYC and Washington DC for example) but was nice either way. For a Sunday evening, there was no wait at all . One plus was the Prix fixe dinner menu. This was new to me. So the other half and I went with it. You get a choice of (2) soups : egg drop or hot and sour, one appetizer, (2) main entrees and (2) mini desserts for $39.99 I had the hot and sour soup which was very tasty and the egg drop was good as well. For the appetizer we went with the shrimp dumplings which were cooked just right and not too salty. For the entrees I chose my usual which was the crispy honey chicken. I never get anything else when I hit up this place and I was not disappointed. I love the crispy white noodles that it is served on and they do give you plenty which was a PLUS for me. I have been to some PF Chang's that are very stingy with that stuff for some reason. We also had the Kung Pao Chicken which was just the right spiciness although there were plenty of red peppers dispersed among the chicken pieces that we had to pick out. The only negative thing about my dinner was the white rice. I know it's being very picky, but I am asian and do love my white rice. For an asian fusion place, they need to work on their white rice. My rice was dry and did not seem fresh at all. For the mini desserts, we had the red velvet and oreo chocolate cake. Both were very yummy. We initially asked for the Lemon Tres Leches, but they had unfortunately run out. Oh and for those who like to drink green tea, I had the Tropical Green tea and it was delicious. It tasted like green tea with a hint of fruitiness.They serve it in a cast iron tea pot which made it feel very authentically Asian. Our server was great and very friendly. I am glad that we have this PF Chang's close by so I can visit when I crave me some crispy honey chicken ( and you cannot beat that its right next to the mall)

text: While I feel other hotels are nice for other reasons, this one was nice in an "upscale" way. It's probably one of the nicest hotels I have ever stayed at. I am from Louisville, KY, and I booked this trip using a weekend getaway package on an Indy tourism website. The room was about $200 and I received a $100 Simon Mall gift card as part of the package. You can't beat that. FYI: I'd probably stay here again... even if I didn't get the gift card. I love the fact that this hotel was in a historic building. I'm nostalgic about those things. I was impressed with the pool and hot tub area in the basement, which must have been recently remodeled... it looked great! My partner and I enjoyed the pool very much.... we were the only ones in it the whole time... probably 1.5 hours... must have been a slow night. The decor of the whole place was beautiful. The location, Monument Cirlce in downtown Indy, was also great. It was a neat area with some brick streets and great architecture. We were within walking distance of a TJMaxx, Steak'n'Shake, and the Cirlcle Center Mall (a Simon Mall). The Indy zoo was about 6-8 blocks away... we were going to walk it, but it was a rainy day. The check in was decent. I can't really rate the hotel staff because I really didn't need much of their service. All in all... a great place.

text: Ok, so I just got married about 6 months ago. That whole "nesting" thing has genetically programmed me to want to buy some furniture for our house. We found a rockin' awesome couch and loveseat set at Ethan Allen. Boo to their prices, but yay for the awesome leather couch and loveseat set we found back in March of 2008. So, we go in and meet with a designer (Katherine Pitts). She was pretty good. She helped us also pick out some additional furniture for our living room and helped us with rug shopping (not at Ethan Allen, those rugs are too gramma-like for us). We place our furniture order and learn that our couch and loveseat are being discontinued, so we'll have to wait for the manufacturer to get a bunch of orders for the "last run" of that furniture, meaning it will take 4+ months to get it. We said ok, that's fine. We put down our down payment and are on our way. Six weeks later, we get a letter in the mail saying our designer is "no longer with Ethan Allen." We are assigned a new designer, Christine Bhe. She never calls us. She doesn't care about us. We get a call from the warehouse a few weeks later, saying our furniture is in, all but the couch, and do we want it delivered? We were never supposed to be called directly from the warehouse. We explicitely wanted everything delivered together, even if it meant we had to wait longer to get it. So, we call the store and tell them that we want to know when everything is in, and we don't want to be called by the warehouse staff. A few more weeks go by, we're talking June 2008 by now. The store (not our designer, BTW), calls us to tell us the furniture is in and we need to pay the balance on our furniture. Let's just say that we could have bought a small car for the amount of furniture we ordered. We go into the store on Saturday, June 14th to pay our balance. We look kind of scrubby because we've been working in our yard. Apparently our "look" does not impress anyone at Ethan Allen who seem rather annoyed when asking us "can we help you". We pay our balance (so we think) and are on our way. We learn we are scheduled for delivery on Saturday, June 21st. We are supposed to be called on Friday, June 20th, to get a two-hour delivery window for Saturday. We let most of Friday go by and we didn't hear from Ethan Allen about our delivery time. So, my husband calls them at about 3pm. They tell us we have a "balance due." I was like, WTF! Turns out that when they rang up our deposits (way back in like March) they forgot to put a side table on the receipt. So, they rang that up separately. So, when we went in to pay our balance, the "bored and annoyed" woman at the cashier area didn't realize we had a second open ticket for this one table and we hadn't paid the balance on that table. Ok, fine, we have a balance. My husband pays it over the phone. We learn we are scheduled for an AM delivery. The designer (Christine or whatever her name was), is supposed to come over at the time of delivery to bring lamps, accessories, etc., so you can see how they work in your house with the furniture. Does she show up? Nooooooo. She did, however, call us about 12:30pm and say, "has your furniture been delivered yet?" Well, it was delivered around 9am, so that was an easy answer. She asked us "Well, do you want me to come over?" as though it would be a pain in her ass. We declined her coming over. Apparently I'm not old enough, or not dressed appropriately enough, to receive respect from Ethan Allen. I wil NEVER buy furniture from them again, even if I love it and drool on it and determine I can't live without it. The reason for this is that I can live without the disrespect and lack of customer service we received when making a substantial purchase from them. Ethan Allen can suck it.

text: Cunetto's be damned! It's Maya Cafe that just might be the most overrated restaurant in St. Louis. When ordering, we were a bit surprised that they only came in a corn hardshell or a soft flour tortilla. No soft corn tortillas in sight. We were undeterred, though, as we'd heard such good things about the place. Once our food arrived, however, we were shocked. The beef tacos were reminiscent of the Mexican fare I downed in the school cafeteria. The meat was ground, oily, and seasoned with flavors not unlike Old El Paso. I was at least expecting strips of grilled flank steak, especially judging by the prices on the menu. Sorely disappointed. I think my money is better spent and my tastebuds better served at places like Lily's or La Vallesana. Maya did have some good things going for it: great, friendly service, kitschy and fun decor, and really good pico de gallo. But these things are not enough for me to make a return visit.

text: Restaurant Week Review: The problem with going to a high end restaurant during restaurant week (normal PF is 3+ times more than RW PF), is they want to get you out the door ASAP to seat their "real" customers. I hate that that happens, but it does, I can understand it, and it's universal, not just unique to Le Bec Fin. That said, we definitely experienced it to a greater degree at LBF. My girlfriend and I had a 7:15 reservation. We showed up on time, were seated immediately in the ante room which is more cramped, less decorated, and clearly meant for the lesser crowd. Things I didn't like: 1. We had a table which was wobbly, which, when I asked to be fixed, was told by the waiter "Sorry, this isn't our usual table so I don't know how to fix it." He tried anyway, and was mildly successful. 2. We weren't automatically given the wine list, I had to ask for it. Granted we got two glasses of the cheapest red they had, but still I should be offered the list. 3. I got the pate and my girlfriend got the soup. Both were decent, nothing mind-blowing. It bothered me how insanely quickly they came out after we ordered them. Clearly pre-made. 4. For entrees, I had the Short Ribs with Steak while my girlfriend had the scallops. I know food pretty well. I've frequented many Micheline/Bruni starred restaurants, and let me say my entree left something to be desired. The texture was far too malleable, (more than just come off the bone), and the sauce must have been prepared at least twelve hours ago. 5. As I mentioned above, there was a clear delineation between the RW people and the other people. There were three small tables lined up right by the entrance, and each was a young couple such as ourselves doing the RW menu. The service was good, sure, but almost too efficient. We slowed things down a bit, but the table next to us came after and left before (turnover of less than 45 mins). Things I did like: 1. The service was good. Not condescending, not rude. The waiter was polite and responsive. 2. The part of the main room that I could see from my table looked beautiful. 3. The deserts were absolutely incredible. I had the gateau; I would venture to say it was probably the best cake I've had in my life. My girlfriend said "the desert made it all worth it." In short, if you've lived in Philadelphia for years and are yearning to experience LBF, go for it. Your tab during RW will obviously be several factors lower than on a regular night. But, so will your experience. If you're just looking for a good meal and a good time, go somewhere else. I truly don't feel like I got my money's worth, both in terms of experience as well as quality of the food.
label: NEG

We walked in, and the hostess was very nice and sweet to us. She sat us at a table, not a booth. I must say that the chairs were VERY uncomfortable. I was not going to complain about it. The only other patrons we could see near us were in a booth right across from us. These two ladies were talking at the top of their voices. We were very uncomfortable, so we asked to be moved, and were moved down the row. The waiter was very understanding, and agreed with us under his breath that they were indeed very loud. I ordered the mixed grill and a dinner salad. My husband ordered two appetizers - the coconut shrimp and the diablo on horseback. The salad was nice, but I was surprised to see chopped black olives from the can on my plate. Hmmm.... I have mixed feelings about my meal. The shrimp were plump and juicy and delicious. The salmon was delicious. The halibut was good in the center, but on the outside it was hard and dry. My husband liked his coconut shrimp, and the diablo on horseback were also really good. He let me try one, and I have to say a definite yum. We did not stick around for dessert or coffee, as the two ladies had a bottle of wine, and the volume continued to go up. Why don't people understand this is semi-fine dining, and keep their voices down? Anyway, the service was very good, and the decor was a nice feel - dark polished wood. If you go, insist on a booth. Not sure if we will return - we may not. I should have gone with my gut and not taken the advice of a mediocre talk show guy.

text: I was NOT impressed with my experience w/ CineBistro. I was so excited to go because my friends had gushed about it... First of all, i have to say that the facilities themselves are very impressive. They have a wine sampling station (the kind that uses the prepaid cards); a beautiful, fully-stocked bar; and a lush waiting area. The cinema itself is very nice as well: large leather seats, lots of leg room, huge screen and great speaker system. However, I have to say, not sure if paying $15 was worth all that. The seats are actually a little uncomfortable. The back of the seat moves but doesn't actually stay in the reclined position. Both my husband and I kept pushing back to see if maybe there was a locking mechanism or if we were just not heavy enough... And the only seats with a footrest is the front row which is way too close to the screen to be comfortable. So we ended up sitting in a slightly upright slouch through the movie. Also, the way the seats are, it's kind of awkward if you come in odd numbers. My hubby and i brought a friend and it seemed like she was very far away. The tables for your food are little swinging slabs attached to the armrest. Reminds me of the desks in school where the writing surface was attached to the chair and had exactly enough room for either your notebook or your textbook but not both. But the worst was dinner. The three of us ordered a chips and guacamole appetizer, the Salmon, the Churrasco steak, and the portabello lasagna as our entrees, and two desserts. THEY BROUGHT OUT ALL THREE COURSES AT THE SAME TIME. Did i mention that the "tables" are small?!?!?!?! My husband had to have his dinner placed on a table for an empty seat and our desserts had to go to another table. The food was what, in the end, totally ruined the experience for us. My "lasagna" was literally four big mushrooms stacked with a slice of cheese inbetween. The steak was five thinly sliced pieces of beef arranged around a mound of mush that was supposed to be beans and rice. it looked like the beans were cooked with the rice and then ran through a food processor. NOT GOOD. The salmon was probably the best of the three but still, nothing spectacular. Our desserts were okay, again, nothing to write about. By the end of the night, we had spent over $150 for a night we wish we spent somewhere else.

text: I was very disappointed with this steak house. Since I've gotten here, I've heard so many rave reviews about this place, but the only thing that stuck out to me course after course was, "What a let down..." We started off the evening with their seafood appetizer platter, tuna tower, and oysters rockefeller: Seafood Platter - One lobster tail, 4 shrimp, 4 king crab legs, 4 oysters on ice with an assortment of sauces - cocktail, horseradish, and something else. This was okay, but nothing I haven't eaten before. Tuna tower - A tuna tartar with a crispy sesame crisp. I thought the tuna was alright, but the crisps that came along with it were very sweet and I didn't think it went with the overall dish... Oysters Rockefeller - Again, so-so at best... oysters with a bit of spinach underneath and baked with what looked like and tasted like mayonnaise on top =/ By the time we were midway through our appetizers, the live music started. I LOVE live music and think it's a great way to perk up the atmosphere of any restaurant. The piano player wasn't bad, but he had his speakers turned up WAY too loud. It was very difficult to hear the conversation even from a couple feet away across the table. After the first act, the second act with a sax and piano was better - the guy definitely turned down the piano so we could talk without shouting. I ordered a limousine salad after seeing that they had Roquefort Bleu Cheese. The description looked awesome - the bleu cheese, spicy cashews, crispy shallots, garlic croutons and a Roquefort Vinaigrette. What I got was a whole head of lettuce with maybe five cashews, a small smattering of fried shallots, and extra crunch (read over-toasted) croutons. =/ hmm... definitely not what I was expecting. Taste-wise it was okay when I got a bite together with the shallots, cashews, and cheese... but the lack of the other ingredients made it just feel like eating a head of lettuce. Take a look at the picture I posted - seriously, you can only count three cashews on that whole head of lettuce - trust me, there weren't that many more hidden elsewhere =/ As for the main entree, I was trying to decide between the scallops and the cowboy steak - I decided to go for the latter since I was feeling especially hungry that night. I ordered it medium-rare and was pleased by how it looked when they first brought it out - however, after slicing into it a bit, I realized that it was way under cooked. I added a picture of it and if that's medium rare, every other restaurant I've been to up til now has served medium rare much more cooked (see the picture). =/ It took me about fifteen minutes to get the attention of the waiter even though he dropped by our table two or three times during that wait - he would never come to my side of the table and when I finally got his attention, he agreed it was rare before sending it back. I asked for another beer while I waited and it took another ten minutes for my beer and another fifteen on top of that for my steak. By that time the rest of my table had finished and after a couple bites, I just decided to call it quits... I would have to make due with the potatoes au gratin I ordered as a side - good thing I did. The au gratin was decent... again, nothing spectacular... The Chocolate soufflé was ordered for dessert... was it good? I guess it was okay... they collapsed the souffle and filled it with some cream and drizzled it with chocolate... unfortunately, that made everything a soggy mess and it tasted like a wet cake =/ I dunno man... really? Finally, the after dinner drink... I ended up getting a McClellan 18 neat which came in a decent sized glass. I asked the waiter if they had Oban 14 and if they did, what the price was. He said he would return shortly with the answer - he didn't. In fact, when I asked a second time after he left and revisited the table twice to drop off and pick up the check, he said he hadn't been able to ask yet... he didn't return after grabbing the check. =/ Overall, I really expected a lot more from this place. Maybe their cooks and wait staff were having a bad night, I'm not sure... but I wasn't impressed. I've come here for drinks before and I'll say they make a decent Gin and Tonic - ask the bartender and he'll give you a history of Gin and Tonics and recommend a good one to you based on what you like. As for dinner, I probably wouldn't pay the prices they ask for the mediocre food and less than stellar service... good thing this was a business meal.

text: My first visit to this establishment was on a very busy Saturday night in April 2010, so I let things slide because it was a wall-to-wall crowd. However, my visit on 9/6/10 was embarrassing for me as a customer and part of the food service industry. 1) Drink service. Our table ordered draft two draft Nimbus beers, a bottled beer, three iced teas, and a water between four people. The beers and first round of beverages showed up quickly, minus one tea. Understandable, no big deal really. However, throughout our one hour lunch our waters and teas were only ever re-filled once after asking multiple times. We noticed other exasperated patrons helping themselves to the pitchers of tea and ice water, despite five or six Nimbus employees walking the floor or standing around chatting to each other at their stations. My brother made it a point to repeat the phrase, "well, at least their beer is good!" One big plus for celiacs or gluten sensitive people: they have bottled Red Bridge! The down side: it is $5 a bottle. :( 2) The food. Nothing to write home about. Don't get me wrong, my group enjoyed their food but it wasn't impressive by any means. The veggie pizza had a nice crust and ample toppings. The fish & chips had good tasting pieces of cod that were rather small. If you're looking for a hefty serving of slaw & frozen fries I would stick to the local grocery store. The steak & fries I ordered was well cooked, but I felt like I was paying for the focus of the dish: a towering pile of garlic fries. 3) Details. As I said before drinks were not being re-filled after multiple requests, and other diners had similar issues remedied only by taking it upon themselves to pour from the pitchers at the staff stations. Our server seemingly disappeared for a good thirty minutes so we had to beg help from other Nimbus staff walking around. The serving tray and tray stand used to carry our food our to us was left sitting by our table until we had finished our meal. Overall, the staff seemed to be aloof and drifting through their shift. Our table did not demand nearly as much attention as the ten or twelve guys sitting together in the corner, but even they were ignored for a good part of their stay. On Labor Day, I get it, you'd rather be at a BBQ or at the pool with a six-pack instead of serving people at work. But other reviews have sang the same song; slow or poorly attentive service, "meh" food, and a general sense of laziness... so the holiday hangover blues are not an excuse. We have seen plenty of restaurants close in and around Tucson, but yet Nimbus still pulls in a decent Monday afternoon lunch crowd... and this is how they serve them? Disappointing at best. Strike two, yer out.

text: Texas Roadhouse in Royersford is a weekly pick for my family. The wait staff is always friendly and helpful. They give off the impression that they really want you to enjoy your time spent there. The food is always delicious and flavorful. Only once out of the many, many times that I've dined there, was 1 of my sides brought out wrong. So, in my experience they have a 99.9% accuracy rate. I've never had a bad dish at Roadhouse. I highly recommend trying their award winning ribs, which are truly fall off the bone. No need to worry about dirtying your hands on this meal. You can literally pull the meat off with your fork. The bbq sauce has a nice, sassy flavor to it. Also, the chicken fried chicken with white gravy is an inexpensive dish and definitely yummy. The salads are always crisp and the most fresh tasting I have ever had anywhere. And a plus for me, I don't have to pick one thing out of their house salad. (I'm a VERY picky eater) Fresh iceberg, chopped tomatoes, hard boiled eggs, shredded cheese--a must have salad. A little tip-you can save yourself the $3 or $4 on this salad, if you get it as one your sides. If you get it as a side choice, it's the same size as ordering it as a separate item. You can also pick out a larger steak before they seat you at your table. The steaks are grilled to perfection, whatever your choosing (rare, medium, well, etc.). The flavor is good enough you don't even need A1. Another recommended choice from their appetizer selections would be the rattlesnake bites. A bit like a jalapeno popper, but sooo much better. So delicious! Or you can try their combo platter which comes with chicken fingers, potato skins, and rattlesnake bites and your choice of 3 dipping sauces. Some other info: For parents, they do have a children's night once a week (Tuesday, I think??) and they offer a 2 meals for $20 deal from 4-6 P.M. at least Mon-Thur, maybe Friday too (not sure on that one). Now to be fair, there are a few cons. They don't open until late during the week. So you can't go there for lunch. Even though this one attests to their good standing, it's still a con for some people. Depending on what time you go, the wait time can get ridiculous. However, they do have call ahead seating so really I guess this one isn't so bad if you remember to grab the number or have it in your phone or something for those spur of the moment times you want to head over and don't want to wait for a table. This place is ALWAYS packed, but it does show they really are that good. All in all, I've been a customer of this establishment since it's opening and not once over the past few years have I had a bad experience or meal here. The best part, you don't need to like country music to enjoy your visit. ;)

text: Chocotrauma. Is that a word? It should be. Like carbicide. Both can easily take place at this monument to an alopecic chocolatier. Menu items are sinfully rich. Mexican Hot Chocolate with its chile spice, Golden Heart cake with its melting caramel center, S'mores, churros. All good, and expensive, which isn't necessarily a bad thing as even one dessert will overload your taste buds and nudge anyone toward type II diabetes, if, of course, they actually make it to the table. Case in point- sat down with a date, jovial server showed up in brown overalls, took the order for two mexican hot chocolates with Kahlua and a Golden Heart Cake. Drinks were served within 10 minutes. Perfectly acceptable. Except for the Kahlua, which came in a separate shot 10 minutes later. The hot chocolate in a "hug mug" was by then a spicy yoohoo in an Ikea gravy boat with a side shot. Great. 30 minutes later, the server idly asked how everything was, slid the brown metal pencil box containing the check onto the table. I was suddenly disturbed by the stylized sketch of the bald man himself staring down from the wall, with the cryptic message "EA MO CHO LAT" written in bold letters nearby. The decor almost distracted me from the bill, which showed the cake order and charge, but alas, no cake! I rarely make a fuss at restaurants, but draw the line when it comes to items charged and not served. I diplomatically pointed this out to the server, who sent over the manager. He removed the charge from the check and offered to give us another order on the house, but I declined, noting that we didn't have the time to wait for another. The server apologized, came back with the corrected check and cake order to go, on the house. I'm sure it was exactly the same as what usually came off of the line, but a chocolate blob oozing caramel in a white styrofoam box just didn't have the same appetizing presentation. I'd imagine that any restaurant themed like Willy Wonka's would have similar hiccups. Oompa loompas on strike, sugar crashes, changes in management, counterfeiting, chocolate pipes clogged with overweight German children, etc. I can't imagine the difficulties in daily operations of such a place. All in all, the absurdity of the place is worth one visit.

text: City Museum deserves 20 stars. It is my favorite place in the country. Maybe even in the whole world!! (really, I'm not exaggerating and I've seen a whole lot of cool things on this planet.) It's kinda like burning man in that way. It's not a museum in the traditional sense. It's an entirely interactive jungle gym experience. Artists have converted the HUGE warehouse space into a gigantic network of passageways and play grounds for both children and adults using entirely found materials and recycled objects. ... you spend your time moving down slides, through tunnels, between secret passage ways, into ball pits, over trees.. You could be there for hours climbing over, under, around, up down in and out.. EVERYWHERE. There's also a bar for adults. There's another little room with old school carnival machines, fun house mirrors, games and a photo booth. Everyone, no matter where you live in the world, should visit the City Museum at least once in your life. You won't regret it, i promise.

text: I rented a car from Dollar at the Nashville airport and departed at night with a snow storm bearing down. About 30 minutes from the airport, I noticed that the window washer didn't function, which was a major safety problem - the windshield was obscured by road salt and dirt and it was nighttime and snowing hard at this point . I had to pull over a few times to manually clean the window with melted snow. I finally found a store and bought a gallon of anti-freeze washer fluid. And I found that the washer reservoir was completely empty - it took the entire gallon to fill it. Which means that Dollar didn't properly inspect the car before releasing it. The washer still didn't function so I called for Dollar roadside assistance. They told me that they'd come out to my location with a towed replacement car, but if they found that the washer was working I'd be liable to pay for the large expense of towing the replacement car. I told them that wasn't fair - but was told "that's the way it is". I went back to the car and tried the washer again and found that it worked. I figure that frozen lines may have thawed from the engine heat . All told, I spent an hour on the side of the road, searching for a store that sold washer fluid in rural Tennessee on a Sunday night and on the phone with Dollar Roadside. When I returned the car, I told the agent of my experiences and asked for some restitution for the fact that Dollar had rented me a car that was not properly inspected and ready for use - I figured a free rental for a day or two would be fair. The agent offered me a $10 rebate! That's right, $10 to pay for all my troubles. I told her to keep the $10 and that Dollar had lost a customer. When you have a choice, I recommend renting with anyone but Dollar.

text: :: the birthday kid, part III :: hating on starr restaurants is like cobra kai beating up on daniel-san. just because all the kewl kidz are doing it, don't mean it's for me...at least when it comes to alma de cuba. i'd previously only been to alma for drinks - probably about 5 times in as many years - and each time i enjoyed sipping sangria in the swanky downstairs lounge. this past december, lucky me got to head upstairs for more than just a trip to the ladies room when the boy took me here for a day-after-my-birthday birthday dinner. it was a bitter cold nite outside, tho you'd never know it inside the invitingly warm alma interior with lights low...candles aglow... were we instantly transported to cuba? not even close. but the mood was perfectly set for a budding romance on a special occasion. drink orders placed - mojito for him, dark & stormy for me - we diverted our gaze from one another and towards our respective menus. my selections were easily made as, in typical restaurant fashion, the veg options are limited. while the boy continued to peruse, i dug in to the warm mini rolls placed before us by our server. only a little tho, as to not ruin my appetite for the black bean soup (topped with crema fresca & 3 rice croquettes) that would soon be my first course - and good thing for that, as i savored every thick, soupy spoonful! meanwhile, the boy was gushing over each bite of his yellowtail ceviche. he pleaded with me to change my non-meat-eating ways...assuring me that i wouldn't regret my decision upon tasting the other-worldy magnificence upon his plate. 'A' for effort, but i of course declined, to which i believe he was secretly grateful in that he did not have to relinquish a mere morsel of his new-found heaven on earth. his second course, the vaca frita, was destined to pale in comparison to the ceviche, of which he continually wished he had ordered a double portion of instead. my entree, the pionono, was a puerto rican sweet plantain roulade of zucchini, basil-tomato sauce & queso fresco served with roasted garlic & broccoli rabe - and it delivered. the flavors and textures of each ingredient meshed perfectly, altho i refrained from cutting into the stinking rose on date nite...instead pushing it to the side to be wrapped up with my uneaten half for lunch the following day when the promise of a kiss was not in my immediate future :) dessert, having been skipped the nite before, was inevitable, however, when our banana tres leches was brought to the table, it arrived sans candles, despite the boy having made mention of my birthday when he made the reservation. shame, shame, alma! all in all, a small hiccup in an otherwise stellar birthday celebration.

text: I don't do country yodeling, although I think I could try. Singing in the shower and in a choir, but I could sing. I could sing at least a few country music songs when my mood gets me into country vibe. Getting tickets and touring Music City Nashville's "Country Music Hall of Fame" included a tour to the "Historic Studio B" with transportation to the studio, in a bus. It took me with the "tour group" to a quiet neighborhood into this recording studio. A small building. No fancy-schmanzy looking building. This is where famous country music artists have recorded their music-still-unkown-but-became-a-hit. These country music legends includes Elvis Presley, Roy Orbison, Johnny Cash, Willie Nelson, Dolly Parton to name a few. Most of the music made here hits the music charts and gain music awards. Displays of famous country music artists' photos on the wall are mostly in black and white photos. Recording award plaques are on the walls to take you back in the time such artists were given deserving musical recognition. I imagined a famous artist recording his country music hit behind glass windows in the recording room. It is a recording studio in the times of old. The design of the studio including the recording equipments remained in the style and fashion like it has been in the early days of Country Music Recording. The sound system here is quality. A sample music was played for us to hear. Even the early versions of the first tape machines can be appreciated in this studio. The well-spoken hospitable tour guide also showed us to a room where a large black grand piano sits almost off-center to the right side of the room. This is where Elvis Presley rehearsed and played the piano. That was his piano. It is in the main tracking room. He played the piano with his fingers on it! The tour guide eventually asked for anyone who could play the piano. I volunteered and sat and played a short music piece. I felt like Elvia Presley (note the "a" instead of the "s" at the end of the name for "Elvis" because I am a girl playing on his piano and I imagined I was him.) I played on Elvis' piano!!! Whataaaaah feeling!! I got a photo taken by one of the other tour friend who couldn't help to document it on the camera. I was a little embarassed after that. I am no Elvis! But then others started to follow after me and took their turns on the piano seat and "played" the piano for photo opportunity. That was fun for all! Step back in time of Country Music Recording history of Country Music Legends. This is a must see when in Nashville!
label: POS

The little dishes are reasonably priced, and on Wednesdays, rolls are half-off. Another Wednesday night special is $2 for a light beer. While they have the typical complement of sushi dishes, they also have tasty soups (udon, soba, miso, etc.), yakitori (shishkabobs), and special Japanese snacks like takoyaki (fried octopus balls) and okonomiyaki (a crepe). It's all very tasty and reasonably priced. The servings are small, so you can try many things. I feel that Yakitori Boy has a better selection of non-sushi items than most places in Philadelphia.

text: Walking tour?! With a guide? Bah. All my past experiences have led me to believe that walking tours were the worst things in the world, typically headed by bitter teenagers mid-puberty, who don't care whether you can understand a damn thing coming out of their angst-ridden mouths, especially about the tourist trap you just paid $20 to see.... Not on this tour! This is one of the BEST things I did as a tourist in NOLA. The tour costs $20 for adults ($10 for kids), and runs about 2-3 hours. It's a walking tour, so bring decent shoes, water, a camera, and your good listening ears. There are 2 tours per day, one starting at 10 am if you want to beat the southern heat, and one at 1:15 pm. They supply tour groups with little fans as a "portable a/c device"- trust me, you'll need it. Our tour guide was a guy named Ernie Sylvester- I highly HIGHLY recommend that you try to get on any tour he's leading, as he is extremely knowledgeable about the history of St. Paul's Cemetery #1, the French Quarter, and Storyville. He's friendly, a NOLA native, loud-spoken, and hilarious, so on top of his well versed and rehearsed tour, he makes the tour a fun learning experience. This tour starts at Rev. Zombie's Voodoo Shop, and walks you down St. Peter street, and directly toward St. Louis Cemetery #1. You will see the tomb of Voodoo Queen, Marie Laveau, as well as many other well known (Easy Rider) mausoleums. Tour groups cap out at 20 people, and during busy seasons it is recommended that you make reservations. The tombs are placed haphazardly, with no rhyme or reason, so it IS advised that you go in a tour group to view them. Apparently, because so many tourists frequent these areas, muggers are known to hide out and prey on anyone in groups of 1-2, as the tombs provide excellent hiding spots. Yet another great reason to go through the haunted history guide company- you won't lose your crap (at least not at the hands of someone else anyway...)! This tour company provides 4 other tours on top of the Cemetery tour - A French Quarter Ghosts and Legends Tour (6 pm and 8 pm), French Quarter Vampire Tour (8:30 pm), New Orleans Voodoo Tour (7:30 pm, Saturday only). If you get an excellent tour guide, these walking tours are some of the best ways to learn about the sordid history of NOLA in a short period of time. Even if you get a bad guide (which I don't believe you will), look on the bright side. At least you're walking off all that buttery goodness, and bananas foster you ate the night before!

text: Definitely The Spot For Any Celebration! This restaurant is gorgeous - big fan of the artwork and jazzy tunes! Whether it's for a romantic dinner, ladies night out, or with your family this is a unique dining experience you won't forget. I was with a group of 8 people and we had a huge, awesome booth seat -I loved the dark wood, and high seats..it made us feel like the only people in the place. The sound quality is nice too..there were people seated throughout the space and we heard virtually nothing. I hope they didn't hear us..we were probably a bit on the rowdy side. Our waiters, Kristen, and Darren were very sweet and accommodating. Never pushy, but personable and knowledgeable without being generic. Coming from an Asian culture and perspective, presentations and live cooking is a normal, fun production (sushi, spring rolls, Vietnamese pancakes, Hibachi, etc), so the fondue presentation is the perfect American representation. It makes dinner a bonding experience - a time for great food and conversation. Our table shared the Spinach Artichoke and Fiesta fondue, it was fun to watch them prepare the cheeses and watch it cook. The apples were not small nor seemed "bagged". They were large square chunks vs. thinly sliced apples you often find pre packaged. Our Fiesta dip also came with fresh, festive color tortilla chips. This is the type of establishment were it's expected that you're in for a leisurely dinner (which is normal in other parts of the world), so sit back and relax. I got my own entree' versus the 3 course meal or the 2 person share. They have tons of options for entrees with reasonable prices ranging from $21-26, which includes a salad of your choice, a side of veggies for cooking and broth of your choice (which they also prepare fresh in front of you). My friends tried an array of salads, and they all looked appetizing as well as filling. They come served on chilled plates which was a good touch. I had the Caribbean Mojo broth infused with spices, herbs and lime..delicious..esp. with my broccoli. My platter came with hefty chunks of salmon, cajun marinated shrimp (I requested it vs. the white shrimp), and scallops. It was plenty to share with others, and delicious. Dessert was also affordable, 4 of us were able to split a small portion just fine. The various sauces are interesting to try out as well. I liked the curry one best. But others double dipped food, and enjoyed those combos too. We got the S'mores chocolate fondue, and it came with a nice platter of graham crackers, bananas, rice krispee treats, strawberries, cheesecake, shortcake, and oreo/graham covered marshmallows...wooow. There were many interesting dessert option, and I think it would be ideal to take a few friends, have a few cocktails and try them all out one at a time! http://picasaweb.google.com/SimplyHuyen/MeltingPot?feat=directlink

text: Chew Man Chu just opened this week, and it is obviously still smoothing out the kinks. The entire restaurant filled up quickly at 5pm on Saturday, however there were only two waiters, and so service was incredibly slow. Luckily, my friend and I arrived before the majority of the diners filed in, however, there were couples at our table who waited upwards of 20 minutes before ordering their first round of drinks. Understaffing is most likely a temporary problem, and so my rating is definitely not based on service, but rather on the food itself. The first thing we noticed was that everything on the menu was basically exactly the same as what you would expect to see at any restaurant in Chinatown with price and size being the only exceptions. Most items on the menu were about double what you would expect to pay for decent fare at a restaurant with less frills and about half the size. For instance, the orange beef, which I unfortunately ordered, was $16.50, and was EXACTLY the same in taste and content as the take-out I often get from smaller Chinese restaurants around the city. The beef, however, was incredibly tough and chewy, and so both my friend and I found it to be inedible and inexcusable. We also ordered a semi-bastardized version of pad thai that was unremarkable and laden with bacon of all things. This was still better than the orange beef in that we were actually able to eat it. After we had started eating our entrees, our appetizers came out. My friend chose the crispy crab won ton, which consisted of four very tiny and overly greasy pieces. These were flavorful but simultaneously disgusting. Is that even possible? It is at Chew Man Chu. The saving grace was our second appetizer, the pork and shrimp potstickers. Again, these were not too far off from what you can get at a cheap Chinese take-out place, but they were still quite tasty. Everything we ordered was underwhelming and overpriced. The only flare this restaurant has is its loud décor, which I felt we were all paying for. While, I doubt I will ever return to this restaurant, I would suggest to anyone who is interested in trying Chew Man Chu to wait a month or longer when at least the problems with service will more than likely be straightened out.

text: We support local restaurants, not only in our home town, but when we travel. So, we decided to try Giovanni's after reading a chef profile in the newspaper. One martini. One glass of red wine (sold at another local restaurant for 40 percent less). One fried fish/veggie appetizer. Two half orders of pasta. (one with angel hair with spicy marinara, the other with wide pasta noodles with roasted eggplant and feta cheese and each topped witth three bit-size slices of Italian sausage). Two coffees. And the total? $81 before tip. Forget about the current economic downturn, who can afford this? The least expensive item on the menu was the house salad that rang in at over $9. Savvy and picky diners should spend their money elsewhere. It's too bad because the waitstaff shouldn't have to be punished by greedy owners or poor pricing. text: I actually want to give three-and-a-half stars ONLY because I think the prices are a little steep. However, this place is lovely, the food was really very good and damn creative. This is NOT a place to go if you are starving. Pull a Scarlet O'Hara and eat before you go, but save room for some of the very special small plates they offer. The mussels? We could have eaten a hundred. the sauce was awesome. We ended up dipping our fries in it. Feta fries? Tasty, but honestly it's not like feta sticks, so you do end up with a bowl of cheese when all the fires are gone. Coconut shrimp were a winner (what fried shrimp is bad?) and there was some sort of frittery sweet potato thing (or was it butternut squash?) that was lovely. Not heavy and oily but truly light and fluffy inside. Pork belly sliky and rich. And a terrific lemon icebox pie. text: I'm sorry to say, this place is very average at best and not worthy of the raving reviews on Yelp. I am from San Francisco and I have ate great sushi around the USA. This cannot be the best in St. Louis. Why am I giving this place the thumbs down you might ask??? Here's why.... - Sushi rice was a total dud. The person in back does not understand you need to add rice vinegar, a bit of sugar and salt. This was the most flavorless rice I have ever put in my mouth. Wake up St. Louis! Rice should not taste like rice when you eat great sushi. Get a Japanese "mama-san" in there to show you how to do it right. Also, make smaller rice under the fish....your out of alignment! Should be more fish and less rice. - Miso soup was the worst ever. Miso soup should be made with fresh white miso, bonito, some silken tofu, and sliced scallions and some seaweed. I have no idea what this was....it was a bowl of brown flavorless water with a few sliced mushrooms (not even japanese mushrooms!). Seriously, this was half hearted effort to make soup. - The fish was tasteless and not fresh IMO. They should torture their seafood supplier. How can you botch Unagi? Spicy scallop was spicy something. Tuna was AWOL for flavor. I bet most of their fish is frozen before they get it. Come on guys, quality is everything when your in the sushi business. - Sushi chefs looked like they were "doing time" and hated every minute on the job. I could not get any of these guys to crack a smile, even after wanted to buy them a round of beers/sake to make my night enjoyable. Part of going to a great sushi bar is interacting with the chefs. These guys need Viagra to get excited. - Waiter for some reason could not remember I ordered Sake. I had to beg for my Sake from three different people. Ended up going to the Dubliner Pub down the street for after sushi disaster drink. - The decor was dated, kinda cheesy, yet there was plenty of "cool cats" eating and drinking like it was a five star establishment. I took the bait as I walked up Washington and should ate at Mizu Sushi. They were not as busy, but I did stop in and it had a better vibe, nice space, and people that appeared to be interested in me as a customer. I will give them a try next time I am in town. Bottom line, this place is overrated and you should try somewhere else because the food is not cheap and the value is not there. I would strongly recommend scrutinizing the Yelp reviews and look for a out-of-town person to weigh in with an opinion. This out of towner says "thumbs down". May the force be with you all!!!

text: One of the most reliable restaurants that I have found out in West Country, good old Chesterfield, is the Hunan Empress. The moo shu pork is addictive and it takes a lot for me to order something else off the menu. But when I do, I am not disappointed. Their seafood dishes always taste great. Never is the food too chewy or have some strange texture to it. Any place that has good seafood out here in the mid west basically automatically becomes a favorite place to eat for me. The Hunan Empress has a nice seating arrangement as well. There are the booths, small tables, medium sized, and then the larger tables that can accompany a sizable group. If you happen to be out in West County and have an itch for some Chinese food, then go to the Hunan Empress. The Hunan Empress is a small little independent restaurant that will be sure to make you happy.

text: For the most part I enjoy Fatburger for its greesy all American style burgers at reasonable prices. It's location was convenient, but the bathroom situation and the ridiculously high prices absolutely ruined the whole experience for me. $6 for a burger or $5 for a baby burger (which was smaller than the burger in a mcdonalds kids meal folks), no fries no drink. Two combos ran us about $15 for the baby fat meals. Absolutely an utter waste of money. At this point I was ready to give this location 3 stars just for the money to quantity ratio vs. the overall appearance of the place (which was high profile). Once I ventured to use the state required facilities I come to realize the women's facilities were not only out of order, but in the middle of construction and had been for weeks without another option for use and no warning up front otherwise. Minus a star. So I go to use the only bathroom available for use, the mens bathroom - and what a huge mistake. This place looked like it had not been cleaned in months. Graffiti on the walls, the stench appauling, trash, stains and piss everywhere, absolutely NO protective seat covers (not even an empty container for one), no soap, nothing hygeinic or usable about the bathroom and if someone had cleaned it that week, let alone that day, it would not have been that horrible. Another star gone. You cannot run a restaurant in the state like this, and being a tourist in town that was a huge let down for the City of Santa Barbara tourism. Visitors are going to frequent places they are familiar with elsewhere and when those places are sub-par in state required bathroom facilities it's a huge STAIN (no pun intended) for the area. text: Q.T. Vietnamese Sandwich is where it's at! If you don't believe me, believe their customers. They just expanded their already small "dining room" over Thanksgiving to accommodate more people. I would say.... maybe 8 people can eat here at a time now. I first discovered Q.T. this summer in my ever-continuing-quest to find the best banh mi anywhere. As of yet, this is still my number 1 banh mi locale, in terms of delicious flavor, bread, and customer service. My only squabble is... at $4.95 a sandwich, you are paying double the price of many other locations. But this IS a much better sandwich. The Lemongrass Tofu is heaven -- so lightly flavored, yet filling. That's my suggestion (and I'm a meat eater too). The bread is baguette style. Forget those hoagie rolls. This bread is warm, crispy, and flaky... which means, when you're done you have all those bread bits to pick up with your fingers. Yes! And oh yeah, don't forget to try the soup. You won't be disappointed. My favorite is the tomato soup with noodles. It's not tomato soup like you would eat with a grilled cheese sandwich. But rather, it's made from real tomatoes and has bits of pork and soup noodles and cilantro... and it's to die for. The mushroom and tofu soup is also good, and it takes a nice second place. The shrimp roll appetizers -- get them! They're so cheap, and the lovely ladies cook them up for you while you wait. The decor is cute and charming. The orange painted walls make a warm atmosphere. The younger and older ladies that work as a team make this place so inviting. They are polite, engaging, and generous. There really is no reason not to try this place. Everybody I have taken here loves the banh mis. I really want this shop to succeed.
label: POS

For our main course we split the Pizza with Anchovies, Oregano, Mozzarella, and tomato. Our only complaint with this pizza was the misuse of the Anchovy which totally overpowered the pizza. They used whole chunks of Anchovy which gave the pizza a very very fishy flavor. I don't know many people who appreciate whole anchovy chunks. A better use might be grinding the anchovy with garlic and using is as a spread so you get the nutty flavor without the fishy. text: For our last evening of the ski trip, we wanted to have a nice dinner, but the steakhouse at the Atlantis Casino had a 1 hour wait. Our party of four got scallops, pork chop, hunter's stew over pasta, and prime rib. The side dishes are very large and we got lobster mac & cheese, wild mushrooms and a twice baked potato to share. Our server and bus person must have checked on 15 times to make sure that we were happy, that we had enough water, that everything was cooked to our liking, and to make sure we had the appropriate cutlery. We ordered a wine by the glass, and they don't just bring you a glass already poured. No no no - that's not fancy enough. The server brought a small carafe, and then poured it at the table into the wine glass. (Some poor person in the back probably has to wash a million of these things.) We ended up not ordering dessert, but if carrot cake had been on the menu I would have been all over it. However, I cannot stress enough what great service we got from John. Every aspect of the meal was handled so nicely. When I ordered a salad but didn't want the blue cheese dressing, he got me a dressing that is made on premises with Riesling, and it was fantastic! I ordered the prime rib, and he was nice enough to ask if I wanted horseradish. I know that not everyone likes that stuff (I do). When the entrees came out, we were missing 1 thing, and I said, "Do you know if we have 1 more side dish coming? I'm looking for the twice baked potato." I guess some people pull attitude and feel that-if-the-server-wasn't-on-his-game-enough-to-bring-it-then-I-don't-want-it. So he was nice enough to ask "Do you still want it?" I answered, "Absolutely!" and I guess the kitchen had it ready but forgot to put it on his tray, because he returned with it a minute later. I saw him with dessert menus in his hand at least once, but it was clear that we were still working on our food, so he left us alone. And even though we didn't end up ordering dessert, he gave us 2 small dishes of cotton candy, which lets out the inner child in you after a fairly fancy meal. This was a really great meal that ended up less than $50 per head. If you're sitting in John's section, you're in good hands and I'm certain that you will enjoy your meal. 4.5 stars.

text: What could I possibly say about the Garfield Park Conservatory and Sunken Gardens that would do it justice? I think I can safely say that it is a big, fat jewel in the crown of my city's Indy Parks department. It is a place of Zen. This place has 136 acres and is located on the near southeast side. (Am I thrilled that this place is near my new home...? Why, yes!) Their facilities are open to the public for workshops, gardening demonstrations and they invite guests to lecture on horticulture and landscaping. The conservatory itself is a truly magnificent place to see, smell and hear. Despite the fact our conservatory is smaller in comparison, I am super proud to say that this place gives the DC Conservatory a run for it's money. (I've been there twice, for several hours - both instances I lost track of the time!) There was a horticulturalist working the day I went in and he had me climbing up on rocks near the waterfall because he insisted that I smell this particular orchid! It was a wonderful interactive experience and all the while the sounds of birds and ambient music filled the air. At the other end of the conservatory is a gorgeous koi pond and waterfall with chairs for sitting and watching them swim or just to relax and read for a spell. Outside the conservatory are the sunken gardens, which are nothing short of eye candy. There are rules here about taking photographs, particularly wedding or professional shots so you do want to call in advance before planning a shoot here. They don't mind pictures for your own enjoyment, of course! The gardens are formal - European and absolutely gorgeous. There is an insane amount of information on their website about it's history, so do check it out! I sat down in a great little bench on the far end of the gardens under a pine and proceeded to take my shoes off and read for awhile. A little slice of heaven is there if you are looking for it. I will miss this place when the cold weather comes...but hey, wait, I can go into the humid conservatory and hang out with the orchids and the koi! OM... Winter hours for the Sunken Gardens are 10 am to 5 pm / locked during inclement weather Dogs are welcome here only on a controlled leash within the park. Also see: www.indyparks.org

text: Here's a rundown of Chifa's chef tasting menu from my birthday. Please keep in mind that this was my first ctm, so I'm a little biased and over excited. We had a great time! The restaurant was very dark and trendy with modernist Asian design. I recommend requesting a booth as the tables toward the front of the place are cramped quite close together. Our waitress was friendly, and really on the ball. We ate for 2 solid hours, but it felt like 20 minutes. First plate - Duck Ceviche: duck confit with foie gras, cherry puree on toasted brioche with corn nuts. Each serving was presented in a Asian style soup spoon which you ate in one bite. The ceviche was very smooth with a surprising crunch. Second plate - Snapper Ceviche: snapper sashimi with a wasabi and ? dressing and roe garnish. Served on a round glass tray. The snapper was perfectly seasoned, the taste of the wasabi was only a quick tang. I ate the entire dish, which went really well with the white wine I was drinking. Third plate - Pan: four small, slightly sweet buns with a reddish spread. I have no idea what the hell I was eating, but hot-damn it was good! The bread alone was delicious, but the spread had a tangy, sweet flavor. Fourth plate - Simple Green salad. A mix of tomato and feta cubes with string beans, edamame, and garlic dressing. The feta gave the salad a fantastic, creamy finish. Fifth plate - Oyster "leche de tigre" served on the half shell in a cream sauce. I wish there had been more then just the one. Sixth plate - Braised oxtail, layered on top of a potato-ish disk with a tiny little egg and a flake of bacon. This was my least favorite dish, but I've never been a big fan of oxtail. Seventh plate - Pork Belly Buns. Apparently this is Chifa's specialty and I can see why. Two fatty pork belly slices layered on small sticky buns. Eighth plate - Rack of Lamb. Two rare cuts of spicy bbq lamb with ginger quinoa and pickled cucumber and cabbage. I loved the lamb, which was very gamey and the quinoa. Boyfriend found the smell of the cabbage a little overwhelming. Ninth plate - Stir Fried Rice with Scallops. A nummy soy glazed scallop resting on a bowl full of rice with mango, edamame, ginger, and egg. Great taste! Tenth plate - Aji Mushrooms with a pastry puff top. The taste of the mushrooms was a little overwhelming on its own. But the ahi cream sauce would taste perfectly over a white fish. Dessert - Banana Picarones. Pumpkin banana funnel cake with honey anise lace, spicy peanut sauce and banana sorbet. The funnel cake was tiny but delicious, however I did not like the sharp flavor of the anise. It detracted a little too strongly from the sweet.
