text: Paraiso, or it's full name El Pueblo De Paraiso, is another hole-in-the-wall Mexican spot on the West Marshall strip in Norristown. I stopped in as part of my mission to eat at every Mexican joint in Norristown (read some of my other reviews!). Paraiso is very similar to most of the other Mexican eateries in Norristown. The service speaks very little English, and the menu is in Spanish, so a basic idea of what most common Mexican dishes and the words for meats in Spanish (i.e. pollo, bistek, asada, carnitas, etc) is helpful, but not required. The waitress was very kind and friendly and helped me with some of the Spanish I did not know or was mispronouncing (apparantly the j in Jarritos is an h sound!) I ordered a chicken burrito and my compatriot ordered a chicken taco (he's 10, so a taco is a full meal). The burrito was solidly tasty, very large, filled with lots of tender shredded chicken, beans, rice, cheese, and a little lettuce and onion. It came with a big bowl of green salsa, which was mild but added good flavor. With some Valentino hot sauce, this was a top-notch authentic burrito. My associate tells me his taco was also quite good. Prices are low and about standard for the area (a burrito, a taco, a jarritos soda and a mango juice was $11.50 total). Place is clean. I recommend this place for anyone looking for good Mexican in the Norristown area!

text: Absolute hidden gem! This restaurant is in a lttle yellow house on the edge of an industrial area of Antioch Pike north of Harding. It's tucked away on the left two or three buildings up from the motel - it's easy to miss. I've driven by it for almost two years every time we went to lunch at Siam Cafe and I always wondered about it because of the location and it never looked busy. But today I discovered the trick, there is parking around back and that seems to be where everyone parks. Inside is clean and neat with a gallery of photos by a local photographer for your enjoyment or purchase. There is a deck out back but I did not venture out to investigate it this trip. First let me say this place was neat and clean - they scored a perfect 100 on their Metro Health Inspection! The owners are very friendly. I talked with them to get their story. He has been baking since he was in his teens and in fact, his bakery back in Bosnia is still going strong. They moved here 10 years ago and like most people from that region, they always tell you how appreciative they are for this country and the opportunities they have had here. I wasn't sure what I wanted to try first. She had a Chevapi plate that she had prepared in the past for another customer that she thought I might like it - it was fiveor six pieces of chevapi with a sauce on top of vegetables and rice with a piece of homemade pita bread. I also couldn't resist the cheese filled burak as I have had a Russian dish that was similar at Taste of Russia and miss it now that they are closed. She brought the burek out first along with ShangriLa tea - I had it somewhere the other day but don't remember it being this good. I only ate about a third wanting to save room for my chevapi plate. It is wonderful. The cheese is rolled up in a sort of phyllo or layered dough and then baked. The outside is crispy, the inside dough chewy and the cheese wonderful. Next came the chevapi plate. Chevapi is a minced meat/sausage like food from Bosnia. Everything on the plate ws wonderful including the homemade pita that is a cross between the traditional pocket pita and the more breadlike pocketless pita. Knowing that he was a baker, I had to try the baklava and it was some of the best I have had without a doubt and it was a nice large serving (almost too much considering how rich baklava is) and fresh. And to balance it out, I had a cup of Turkish coffee that was a perfect way to balance out the richness of the baklava. This is so close to work that I will be a regular here. The prices are good and serving sizes good for the price. I can't wait to try several other things on the menu. They have chicken livers and rice. She told me to call ahead so that they can make sure they have fresh liver when I want to come try them. And they have gyro and Euro burgers both your choice of beef or lamb. She highly recommended their tiramisu. And the bowls of soup looked nice and hearty. Beside the pastry case is another case with a small but interesting selection of imported food items. They also had various sausages vacuum packaged for sale also.

text: I actually had a table at the Super Flea for many months. First off, to get this off of my chest, the place is controlled by the big market guys who own the cd place, dvd place, t-shirt and patch place and bunch of other small booths. This means that 'free market' essentially doesn't exist. I had 'too many DVD's' on my table that were 'too cheap' and undercutting the big guys. They told me I had to limit my selection to 25. This defeats the purpose of a free market I think. Anyways now that that is off of my mind the market itself is actually an amazing place to shop full of knick-knacks and you-name-its. You can get a fair deal for the most part although I think alot of things were overpriced. When I first came in other vendors were buying stuff off of my table to upcharge on their own. The best deals, in my opinion, were the low priced hemming (Only $5) and the handmade custom items (check out Ally Gators for custom pillows, etc.) There are a ton of different things available there - i'd stay away from knock-off Ed Hardy clothing and stuff cause it's usually Chinese and not authentic. You can even sell your unwanted gold or get a haircut! The hot dogs are cheap and a good bargain but the mini donuts were a bit off in my opinion. There are alot of collectors items for cards, stamps, coins, etc. So take it as you will, there will always be excellent finds and deals there but in my experience it sucks that you can't just sell anything for any price. If I want to sell my movies and games for 5 bucks less than the other guys I should be allowed to! But I guess those guys own half the place so of course the managers are going to look after them to get their rent payment. And its NOTHING compared to American flea markets (The next time you're South be sure to check one out - but leave a whole day to visit). Thanks for taking the time to read my review.

text: Note: This rating/review is for their Bikram class. I didn't attend any other classes, so maybe they are good at teaching other kinds of yoga. This isn't a real licensed Bikram studio, and they don't follow a lot of Bikram's rules (e.g.: Bikram doesn't allow wood floors because they're too slippery/dangerous, but this place has them). My biggest problem was that the room was not NEARLY hot enough. It could not have been hotter than 90, when a real Bikram class should be at least 105. Also, the instructor deviated a lot from the standard Bikram instructions, so instead of giving lots of details about what you should be doing in each pose, he talked about things like finding your inner peace. That's nice and all, but I noticed a lot of people in the class doing the poses completely wrong because the instructor wasn't being fully informative. I guess this class is fine if you're into "gentle" yoga, but I'm pretty hardcore about Bikram and this was a disappointment for me. I come to Bikram classes to get an intense workout and to be pushed to the limits of what my body can do -- NOT to be told I can just take it easy and meditate on my goals in life. text: So like most tourist, I couldn't help myself and had to do the Philly cheese steak challenge. First off note that both locations take cash only, and that you probably will not be able to get a table. We got our Philly cheese steaks with onions and whiz, since I was under the impression that was what a true Philly cheese steak was. We decided on Pat's first due to the fact that the line appeared to be shorter and moving faster (haha shorter). It took about thirty minutes to get through the line, and we were ready having observed the sign that said to have our order and cash ready, so we step up to the first window and order our Pat's Philly and realize there is another separate line for ordering soda's and fries, which I promptly ran to while my boyfriend waited for the sandwich, two lines 30 minutes. We walked a crossed the street and ate our sandwich on the street like animals. My first thought upon eating the cheese steak was I've made a better one at home. The meat lacked any flavor and I felt there wasn't enough whiz (which is strange since whiz actually makes me very sick...taking it for the yelp team today though). So now, not hungry, and realizing we stopped making these at home because whiz makes me sick, we stumble a crossed the street to Geno's and for consistency's sake ordered the same sub after waiting another 20 minutes in line. Geno's cooking area is open to the public, as we waited we watched the workers make the subs in a surprisingly clean kitchen. They cranked them out. When ordering we did note the Geno's guy said thanks, and he seemed in a better mood. Geno's meat as most people noted is sliced, rather than shredded, which I did think made it taster. Though it was gawdy as all get out, Geno's in my opinion produced a better sub. The bread at both seemed the same, though my boyfriend thought Pat's bread was better less bready. I also felt Geno's was a better cheese to meat ratio, cheesier, and the meat tasted as if it was seasoned or just a better quality of meat. But having now completed the challenge, I wouldn't go back to either.

text: I don't know which reason I have for loving this place so much. It might be the unassuming presence, or the way you open the door and it's so cozy and warm even on a cold, blustery night. It might be that in the summer the patio is open, and the beer is cold, and my favorite beer is on tap (Red Seal) and I can pull up on my bike and savor a great meal after a long ride. It might be the way the kitchen is set up and you can watch meals being made. It might be the giant bin of pretzels at the bar that you scoop yourself, take to the table and eat with mustard. Maybe it's the spicy lamb grinder that you dip into the succulent sauce, and maybe it's that the lamb now comes from Lava Lake Lamb, so it's all natural. There is the old standby, though, that might be the reason. Croquetas, the little butter balls, full of cod or chicken. I love the garlic soup, too, which is just incomparable. I really enjoy the vegetable shish ka bobs, even, which are marinated so nicely. There's the flan, and, oh, of course the mouth watering beef tongue Saturdays. There is the clientele, and the dimly lit room, and the fun, and the Cheers like atmosphere. Gernika was the first place that made me feel like I really lived somewhere when I moved to Boise, and even when it changed owners to Jeff May, nothing changed for me. I feel more at home there than anywhere other restaurant. Gernika is simply everything I could ever want in a restaurant. If I am to ever move from Boise, I believe that I will always look for, and never find, all of these just-perfect elements in any other restaurant. Closed Sundays.

text: I ate at Distrito on Saturday night for my friend's birthday party. First of all, I love the decor because it's extra girly! Sean, our waiter, was pretty attentive. I ordered a Strawberry Boing, which was ok, nothing spectacular though. Now on to the food. The food at Distrito is *sigh* GLORIOUS! I ordered the Queso Fundido, which is like this duck and cheese bake. They give you these mini tortillas and you can either spoon the QF out and put it on the tortillas or just eat it directly from the baker. Keep in mind, they serve tapas, so the portions are small. I also ordered the Platano y Crema (sweet fried plantain with cheese), which doesn't sound all that hot, but it tastes ABSOLUTELY delicious! My friend ordered the Esquites, which is like this sweet corn, cheese and lime parfait - again doesn't sound too appetizing, but I tasted it and it was fabulous! We also shared the Encarnacion nachos which were also really good. It's rare that you go to a restaurant with a large group and EVERYONE enjoys their food. Seriously though, I could go back to Distrito to-night! So for glorious food and fun decor, Distrito gets 5 stars!

text: When I first visited Philly in 2004, I ate at Soho almost every night of my vacation. It was delicious and made the perfect end to a day of walking around the city or going to a ball game. It was always somewhat busy but organized and comfortable. The pizza was flavorful, with garlic salt on the crust and delicious toppings. When I moved here in 2007, the place seemed to have changed hands. The place was a little slower and the pizza was a little less flavorful and a little less consistent but it was still pretty good. I still stopped by once in a while. I'm moving away now and hadn't been in for a while so I thought I'd stop in one last time. It seems the place has changed hands yet again. The place was DEAD and the pizza was terrible. It was really bland, there was hardly any cheese or sauce on the slices and no flavor to speak of! I don't know how this place is going to make it - even with it's amazing location. Sad.
label: NEG

text: I have lived in philadelphia on and off, mostly on, since 2001 and I avoid the train like the plague. After riding public trans in other cities like Portland and DC whos public trans systems are pristine and beautiful I feel bad giving philly even one star - its too much! On the few and far between times I ride the train when it rains, snows or I'm traveling places with my friends who don't bike, it has been pretty lame. It smells, its dirty, people are rude, 50% of the time the trains are late and don't seem to run on any sort of schedule. Once I got on the train and the seats were covered in blood...then newspaper was covering the blood and the blood was seeping through the newspaper Mmm... Do they ever clean the trains, ever? Additionally you can't buy tokens at most subway stops, you have to have exact change if you don't have a token because people working at the windows don't give change - also the people that work at the windows at the subway and el are the rudest most unhelpful people I've ever dealt with. Don't bother going to them if you have a question because its hard to find one that will actually help you even if you are nice...though I know there are diamonds in the rough, maybe you'll get lucky. The only good thing I can say about the trains is the local flavor that gives me entertainment...its annoying entertainment, but entertainment none the less. I know that its a lot of the local people making the train rides hellish but seriously, Septa....you're doing a really poor job...not to mention your strike sucks.
label: NEG

text: yum yum yum. this place is delish. my cousin took me here while i was in town. she raved about the soups and the dinner but unfortunately they no longer serve dinner here. nonetheless, the soup and salad were great. broccoli chedder - first time having this soup where it's so thick and hearty. it's usually more watery and cheesy at other places. chicken tortilla - soup with a zing. toasted veggie - lots of ingredients but i wish it was more toasted/crispy and warm. came with a strawberry salad that was really good. crab and shrimp salad - this was really good. large portions with lots of crab meat. came with some cheesy poppyseed bread which i ate with my soup. the cookie that came with the soup was delicious. more cookies please! large portions. great taste. friendly laid back atmosphere. i would definitely come back if i lived in the area. come early because they seem to run out of food. we got there around 7 and they were already out of the pesto turkey, chicken and white balsamic vinagrette. that just about knocks off half the items on the menu.

text: I've driven by this place about a zillion times on 611 and really had no idea anyone ever went there because the parking and 'front' door are in the back. I was finally convinced to stop in by a neighbor and its really great. Vintage is a perfect alternative to any of the crappy chain restaurants that have gobbled up the business from the independent places. After having a meal at Vintage you would never, never, ever bother trying your luck at the Chilli's, Outback or Olive Garden in that area again. Food is great. Atmosphere is very tavern like and has a lot of wood. Music is better than any alternative (I was there during dinner hours). Kid friendly during dinner but it changes over to more of a bar scene so probably not the best late dinner place with the kids. Great staff too! and the fillet mignon for $20 is a kick-ass deal!

Both my man and I were hungry when I got there, and when the bread came out we descended upon it. Dude that crusty, chewy awesomeness was gone so fast we had to ask for more. We ate so much bread we were almost too full for our meal! Seriously. So. Good. I ordered antipasto which was decent, and spaghetti pomodoro which was lovely (and even better as leftovers!). Jack had the orechiette with duck and the veal, both of which were incredible but having had too much bread were left unfinished. Next time, we won't order seconds on the bread. Yum.

text: Sunday night dining options, at least nice ones, can be limited. So when the hunger arrived and we were wanting something out of the ordinary, we turned to Yelp, and Yelp set us on a course for Sarah Street. Terrene did not disappoint. Never has. Special mention for our server, Elizabeth, who was the epitome of good service: personable, professional, prepared, with good sense of pacing. Extra star for creativity in the drink menu. I enjoy trying new combinations. From a number of appealing suggestions I went with a Killer Buzz: Three Olives vanilla vodka, espresso, sweetened condensed milk. Delicious, refreshing, unusual. It was 8-ish and I was starving when we arrived. A plate of frites appeared with haste; fresh, hot, salty, fried to perfection. Again, star for creativity. I generally shrink from anything mayo-based but the pickled onion mayo drew me in; and the spicy horseradish ketchup holds its own as the alternative. My "big plate" was the pork shoulder w/ mole, sweet potato fries & hominy. Thank you for choosing combinations that entice me and challenge my assumptions! Hominy is not a starch I would gravitate toward but as prepared by the chef I found it appealing. I might suggest that my pork could have retained a bit more moisture, but the flavor was excellent. I'm a huge fan of color on my plate - orange, brown, yellow, green - colors of the earth. The baby cilantro was a super accent. Great with a glass of Hogue (?) Sauvignon Blanc, Columbia Valley. The quail was not on offer for the evening, so Peter went with the chicken, but his appetite disappeared between the door and the entree :/. Not me, though. Panna cotta? Yes please! Espresso? Definitely. So satisfied, really. Excellent food, excellent service, excellent ambiance. It does make for an expensive meal, but for locally-sourced items prepared well, I will feast and enjoy.

text: The problem with rockstar doctors is that they don't actually have time for patients. Dr. Taylor comes highly recommended from both publications, television, and even my girlfriends internist, however, there isn't really a way to verify how good she actually is because she more than likely doesn't have time for you. I've been to her office three times now, and I'd say the average wait time is one hour, and the average time spent with the doctor is five minutes. There is all this build up to trying to get yourself some care and trust that your issue will be resolved and then she comes into the room, asks you a few questions and dismisses you with a few disappointing instructions. Her prescription for me hasn't been working but she encouraged me the last time that at least it improved and we'll just keep seeing what happens down the road. Then she was out of the room within 4 minutes. The last time my girlfriend went for an appointment she had to wait over an hour and half for a five minute visit which didn't result in anything. Doctor Taylor is overbooked, and sure that is a great way to make money, but I doubt she is making the kind of impact with her patients that will keep them loyal. I'm currently looking for a new dermatologist.
label: NEG

text: Is it really a battle between Amada and Tinto for the best tapas in Philly when both restaurants are owned by Jose Garces? Interestingly enough, my experience at Tinto was quite different from that at Amada and Chifa. Not only did I appreciate the chef's lack of obsession with salt, I thoroughly enjoyed the wine selection and its location (gelato shop is right across the street if you still have room for dessert). Among the best I've tried on the menu: the bocadillos (especially the short ribs), the chicken with garbanzon puree (served in a shot glass), the pork belly with shaved apples, truffled chestnut soup (although can be a tad creamy), and its seasonal gazpacho (with just a right amount of spicyness and 'kick'). [TIP: if you make a reservation, try to request one of their booths/tables with regular-height seats. It can get quite inconvenient to sit and eat at a bar-level.] -pinkposy

text: I've had their crab fries at Phillies' games, and despite being not amazingly impressed, I've always wanted to try Chickies and Pete's. Let me also mention that I am a HUGE seafood fan. I think my head computed the fact that they have crab fries and a seafood heavy menu to mean that I would enjoy this place. Well...wrong. I came here for a snack, and I ordered the crab fries and the calamari. The crab fries were overly seasoned. They're crinkle cut fries, and they aren't awfully meaty. Therefore, when you slather on a lot of seasoning, it stubbornly adheres to the fry which has more surface area than your typical fry due to the ridges created by the crinkles. Now take into consideration that there isn't a whole lot of potato in each fry, and you are basically hit with an absurdly salty and seasoned taste in your mouth with each bite. Unfortunately, the calamari was even worse. Calamari is supposed to have a certain chewiness and resistance with each bite. This calamari, however, was mushy and fishy. It definitely did not taste very fresh. The dish came out far too fast, which suggests that it may have been sitting around for a while after it was cooked. I noticed that other people were complaining about their food being cold right after it was brought out, so I don't doubt that they cooked their food too far ahead of time. Fast forward a few hours. I was eating the leftover food as I was driving. If I thought the food was bad before, well the food was now a cold limp mess. If the calamari did not have that extremely fishy taste, it was have been impossible to differentiate the limp overly seasoned fries from the mushy calamari.
label: NEG

text: After hearing all the rave reviews about this place from my boyfriend and his friends, I decided to check it out for myself. Well, with him, but for myself. There are giant cans (trash can sized) filled with whole peanuts, free for the taking. They promote throwing the peanut shells on the floor, and as a result there are shells all over the floor. All over the floor. Real low class country feel (I like my country to be upscale, thank you very much). The waitstaff was a little disoriented (I had 3 meals brought to our table before the right one came), but towards the end of our visit the restaurant got quieter and our waitress was spot on with everything. There's a balloon man that walks around the tables and makes balloon animals/hats for the kids/kid-hearted. They play the same music that you would find at country western clubs, but I didn't see anyone get up and line dance :( DRINK AND BREAD They had something called a Strawberry Cowboy Cooler which I intended to get, but at the last minute asked for a Cherry Limeade instead. It was good, tasted like something Red Robin would make. The complimentary bread was amazing: super moist, kind of doughy, and the butter they serve with it is whipped with cinnamon. The bread comes out incredibly warm and the butter melts almost immediately after spreading. If this bread was a menu item I would get it. Luckily you can ask for more (no charge) even after the main dishes come out. APPETIZER We kicked off our meal with a baby cactus blossom, which is like an awesome blossom from Chili's. This was $2.99, and together we were only able to eat about half of it. It wasn't as greasy as at Chili's, you be the judge as to whether that's good or bad. ENTREE We both ordered ribs, the boy also got chicken. His ribs were overcooked, the BBQ sauce on top of them was crackly, and his chicken was dry. I gave mine a reluctant try, and it was the most moist, most tender slab of ribs I have ever purchased for less than 15 dollars ($11.99 for 1/2 slab). I picked up the first rib bone and the meat fell off. I tried it again, taking a second rib bone off the plate in an attempt to eat the meat. The meat fell off the bone, again. I picked up a piece with my fingers and could not stop grabbing at the remaining meat. Very tender, very good.

text: Hotel Review: another listing on Yelp says that the hotel is CLOSED. Well, not unless it happened last week! Coming from LA for a conference at which my husband spoke, I scheduled the travel on Travelocity (which gave the hotel 3 stars, and travelers there rated it 3.5. I suspect ownership fabricated its own reviews). This hotel sounded quaint: "Ben Franklin room, fresh flowers, breakfast, private bath in historic downtown" ...ok. At $120 a night plus tax, I was expecting a small clean room with no frills. If the room had been $35 and had only 2 stars on Travelocity, I would have KNOWN what I was getting into. A NIGHTMARE!!!! We cab it to the front door with a grimy note saying "Check into Hotel at the Bar". Ok, a red flag # 1. The bartender looks at a piece of paper and hands us a key on a cheap keychain (from which the key fell). He opened a back door behind the bar and told us to climb to the 3rd floor. OK... RED FLAG # 2. Up we climbed some unkempt stairs and hallways that became more dilapidated with each floor. I started to feel a little sick but remained optimistic. Once we reached our floor we noticed a missing ceiling panel with electrical wires hanging down. GULP! The front door was some cheap hollow patched door I could have put my fist through. The rickety lock made my husband curse. Once inside I knew immediately we would not stay. Forget red flags, this is a total bait & switch. The walls were cracked and disgusting. The furniture had scratches and looked like someone's leftovers from a street corner. I looked everywhere for some redeeming quality. Outside the window was an awning torn into a million pieces... dirty and unrecognizable as an awning at all - I wondered why no one had removed it since the wire frame it once hung on screamed RUN!!!! I saw dirt on the floor and windowsills. The bathroom was scary. I can't imagine it had been cleaned in a long time since there was black mold everywhere. A hairdryer was stuck to the wall with a piece of plywood. Upon entering the bedroom it was noticely visible that the mattress was bumpy and uneven. Like a dark and dreary dungeon, the "Ben Franklin Room" at The Society Hill Hotel has an incredible view of a 3 foot space between buildings that was the dirtiest location in Philadelphia. On the dirty window stuck a grimy file folder label which read in pen "Do Not Open Window!". We opened the closet and on the floor we found a disgusting window air conditioner. We didn't bother turning it on. After my husband found a sign which read "Not responsible for Theft" he made a comment about being shanked in our sleep by a crack head. He was furious, and I felt responsible. Why Travelocity? WHY?!!! Back down to the bar to return our keys and refuse to stay. The bartender explains that the restaurant is separate from the hotel, and that we would have to come back tomorrow as no one from the hotel was there. Then why did the bar hand us our keys and then accept them back when we left? And why is it that for two days Travelocity tried repeatedly to contact the hotel with no answer? And why is it that our credit card was charged for the entire 3 days for which we had booked? We could not cancel. We could not reach anyone. We had to find another hotel to stay in at the last minute. Everywhere nearby was booked. We took a $60 cab ride to Laurel, New Jersey and stayed in a Beautiful HYATT 2 bedroom suite with a full kitchen. We were quoted $149 a night, and they reduced it to $99 to make up for the cab ride. The Society Hill Hotel is a scam that will be reported to the BBB of Philadelphia. Our credit card will eventually refund us the money, but it will take a few months. PLEASE! Do yourself a favor and do not stay at THE SOCIETY HILL HOTEL. I cannot speak for the food, drink or anything else at the "Bar - Restaurant", but I have some advice for them: Do not take keys, give out keys, share the same name or serve breakfast for the hotel if you are not affiliated. Personally, I do not believe the claim that they are not the same since every aspect was linked to them. I believe it is just how they avoid unhappy customers and rip them off. I feel so bad for the people who show up and do not have the money to go somewhere else. Always check YELP first.

text: I wish them luck and success, but have to be honest in my review. I had breakfast and lunch here, and an assortment of pastries and baked goods. Including setting out a huge tray of assorted cookies for those waiting in line. They had us place orders at the counter and then fight it out for the few available tables. 3 of us squeezed into a tiny 2-top because that's all that was available, and we were lucky as others stood around with confused looks at the lack of seating. I tried a bearclaw and the pastry dough was top notch, tender and buttery. The filling was very dry and I scraped most of it out anyway since I didn't realize bearclaws were cinnamony not almond paste. I had a breakfast burrito and I have to say it was the worst breakfast burrito I've ever had. Dry tortilla ( steamed tortillas are a must for burritos IMO, or at least warmed) The filling was sausage, ham, cheese, scrambled egg, and salsa. The eggs were runny and not scrambled, they appeared to be a badly fried over easy egg that was broken up with a spatula. The salsa was very thin and watery and added the the wet mess of the filling but didn't add any flavor. The sausage they used was very bland, no zestyness or spice and the ham was devoid of flavor too. The burrito would benefit greatly from some veggies, maybe bell pepper or lightly sauteed onions, something to add flavor and texture. The homefries served along side were seasoned nicely, but a bit too al dente for my liking. Still, the staff were friendly and remained calm through the chaos of that sunday morning rush. I decided to give them another try. Brought a friend in for lunch, this time it was fairly empty and they had tableside wait service. I had a specialty sandwich, the lamb shoulder with a side of fries. My friend had a turkey avocado something with a side of soup. The soup looked really good and the presentation was nice, but her sandwich was lacking any avocado. She had to ask the waitress for some avocado, and the waitress said "oh you want to add on?", we had to show her that it was supposed to come with. My sandwich suffered from dry meat and very very dry bread. Sometimes light grilling or toasting can revive old bread, but this bread was beyond saving. It must have been several days old. The strips of lamb were well seasoned, but also very dry. The potato wedge fries that I added for $1.50 were seasoned with a lot of lawrys seasoning salt and again, a bit undercooked. The waitress came by and poured coffee into our waters. oops. She caught it and was sweet and funny though. I have no complaints at all about the service, they are hardworking and very earnest. I do believe they have a little polishing up to do in the kitchen though. I wont give up on them quite yet despite 2 mediocre/bad experiences, I tend to try new restaurants early while they are working out kinks.

text: After seeing this place mentioned on a Yelp list for their beef barley soup, I decided to stop in and try the place since it was close to my bank on the Hill. Michael was at the counter and navigated me through the menu as well as their frozen offerings. He couldn't have been nicer or more helpful! I decided to go with their 1/2 soup and 1/2 sandwich combo for 6 bucks. I got the salsiccia sandwich (split salsiccia with marinara and provolone) and their salsiccia chili. The chili alone is worth going out of your way to try. I thought it was a perfect blend of meat, red beans (not kidney beans), sauciness, and just enough spiciness; everything seemed well balanced and proportionate in both flavor and size of ingredients. A hearty champion indeed! The bread the sandwich came on was so freaging good; chewy and soft all at the same time, and you could actually taste the sesame flavor the seeds lended. The piece of split salsiccia was fresh, had plump texture, and authentic Italian seasoning (plenty of fennel seed!). Provolone cheese and a drizzle of marinara topped it off. The cheese was good, as was the marinara, but I would have liked to have a little more sauce on my sandwich (totally personal preference). I think the balance would have been just right for most people. Important to note, is that they have a list of 11 cheeses to choose from, as well as a whole host of "toppings" I could have added as well--a customizable meal! I got my order to go and everything was still warm by the time I got back to the office, which was very much appreciated on this chilly winter day. I ate the half sandwich and part of the chili and was too full to continue. Needless to say, I am REALLY excited about the leftover chili I'll be having for lunch tomorrow! They have a good sized menu of sandwiches, both cold and hot, as well as salads, pasta, and sides. They carry Coke and Fitz's beverages, as well as brew fresh iced tea. You can get Dad's oatmeal cookies and a few other treats, including frozen Snickers bars. This is probably not the place to go if you are watching carbs or calories. There are a few vegetarian options, but I didn't see anything vegan-friendly. They also have frozen pastas, speidini, pizzas, etc. and provide options for catering. I did happen to purchase a whole frozen brusilone they made in-house for only about $8.50. Stay tuned on how it turns it!

text: What a great surprise for my first visit to Indy! I popped onto Yelp trying to figure out what to grab for dinner after a rough day of travel and work. Staying by the airport, there wasn't a ton around... Luckily for me, Bosphorus was only 12-15 minutes away. Just S.E. of downtown, the restaurant is a small 15 table or so business run by a nice family. At 7PM on a Wednesday there were a half dozen parties when I got there. I decided to have lentil soup, Doner, and rice pudding with Efez Dark Turkish beer and Turkish coffee to wash things down. I thought the bright yellow lentil soup was good although could have used a pinch more seasoning for me. The Doner was flat out awesome! As a frequent traveler to Germany, I used to eat a lot of Doner and struggle to find it in the states. For the uninitiated, Doner is seasoned lamb shaved from a rotating roasting spit. Bosphorus served it with a fresh green salad, vegetables, sauce and pita. The Efez Dark was a nice beer that I would best refer to as Turkey's answer to Negro Modelo. The second one was even better than the first. I questioned whether or not I wanted to spring for dessert but the thought of Turkish coffee and rice pudding was too much to resist. I am SO glad I did; the rice pudding was a perfect consistency and flavor. Each spoonful of the large bowl was "heaven". And the coffee was "black as midnight" and "strong as love". The atmosphere was casual yet nice enough to use for a birthday party (which was the reason two tables were there). The service was attentive and pleasant without being smothering, which can sometimes be the downside of being a party of one. At the end of the day, if you like middle Eastern cuisine, you can't go wrong with Bosphorus. Great stuff!

text: I'll start with the good: It's Applebee's, you can tell from the name on the front of the building and from the name on the menus. I went there for lunch a couple times and the food came out quickly and was hot. The service was also great, I was surprised because difference between my lunch experience and my experiences in the evening. But, if you are working in the area, the lunch experience seems just fine. But... The evening/dinner experience is completely different. First you'll notice they have security at night, they have a police officer to watch over the customers. They already have more cameras in the ceiling than your local bank branch. With the police as security, multiple cameras and big "No Firearms" sign on the front door; you would assume it's a rough place, but I have never seen in violence there, but this is not your father's Applebee's. Next you'll notice at night it's more of a sports bar experience (and not a family restaurant). I've heard it nicknamed "Club Applebee's" or another name that I will not say here, but don't get me wrong, this in itself is not a problem. In fact, I went and enjoyed the interesting people and lively conversations. At night, you are more likely to socialize and meet new people. So, if you want a sports bar type place, in North County, Applebee's might be the place. The fact that it's so lively at night, is why I gave it two (2) stars instead of one (1). Again, the lively crowd is kinda cool, and I've gone there just for that experience. If there is a football or basketball game on, it can be a fun place to drink a beer. My problem with the place is the service, food and lack of cleanliness. The last three times I've gone there, the gave me menus sticky with food or have dried up food on them, and that's just nasty and disgusting, decaying food contains germs and I don't like having my hands touch old decaying food right before I eat. Also, the silverware they gave me had dried up food on it, each time I had to send my silverware back several times, the last time they gave me 5 sets, and told me to just pick the clean set. I order a draft beer and had lipstick on my glass, so I sent it back and got a glass with dried up wing sauce fingerprints on the outside, the third glass I got was clean, but by that time the bartender made me feel like I was being a pest for wanting a clean glass. Also, the food at night is hit or miss. It might be cold, or the same dish may be half cold and half hot (which is strange). Evening meals there are interesting and lively, but if you want higher quality and service, there's a Applebee's on Lindbergh that's better. If you want a quick good lunch go here. If you want somewhere to watch the game and talk with other people, visit this locations. If you want higher quality and service, I haven't see it at this location at night.
label: NEG

text: I basically lived at this hotel for about a month when I was in town for a long term job so I got reeeally familiar with the ins and outs of the place. In short? It was awful. Let's start at the beginning: the front desk staff is basically clueless. They're very nice, just clueless. At most other hotels this wouldn't be too much of an issue, but since the magnetic key for my room wouldn't work at least once a day, I kept having to go back to the front desk every day to get a new card - it gets old fast. Especially when each elevator ride takes approximately 5-10 minutes with wait time. There is also a lot of false advertising. For example, they advertise wifi availability, but what they mean is that it's available, but you have to pay to use it. If you get a package delivered here, there is a fee - a big one. I think one fee I had was about 25 bucks. The business center is also very pricey. Oh! And make sure not to accidentally take something out of the mini-bar, because it will automatically show up on your bill when you check out, regardless of whether or not you consumed it. Parking is also very very expensive. You must valet - and sometimes when I would go to pick up the car, calling ahead would not be an option and I would have to wait 10-20 minutes in the valet area while the poor over-worked valets would be servicing large wedding and conference parties. All the rooms below the 42nd floor (I think) have not been redone and just look...tired. Ask for a higher floor. Also, on each floor there are two rooms that are right next to the elevators, separate from the rest of the hallway. If you find yourself to be in either of these rooms, asked to be moved IMMEDIATELY. Otherwise, you will not be able to get any sleep thanks to the constant stream of drunken revelers that come home (or depart) after midnight. I would not recommend this for business travellers (or really anyone, frankly). Maybe if you're one of the drunken revelers you won't notice how everything's overpriced.

text: This restaurant is "sushi boat" in name only. Yes, they have boats going around. After watching the boats sail by for one full circuit, to see what was available, I reached for a little plate and it stuck to the boat. I thought I hadn't had a firm enough grip. Another appealing item came by, and it, too, would not come off the boat. The sushi chef noticed how I was trying to take the boats apart. And he told me that what is ON the boats is "only for display." It was on the dark side at the sushi bar, and I hadn't been paying that much attention, but I then realized the food in the boats, in pretty arrangements, looked shellacked! WTF and how. The whole point of "sushi boats," to me, is that aside from the charm of the things, the food is prepared and ready for you to pick up. You don't have to wait while the chef gets to your order. After you eat, the waitstaff counts the types and numbers of plates you've picked, and lunch is finished. So I marked up some maki on the paper slip and it was fine--but really, really small--a too-narrow, too-thin strip of tuna atop (and not stuck very well to) a too-dry bit of rice. The tuna was fresh and good, but the pieces were skimpier than any I've ever had, yet at a price comparable to the big juicy maki at, say, Kokopelli at Circus Circus. My companion, who ordered AYCE, had a mountain roll and said it was "adequate." I did enjoy the appetizer served with each meal (mine was a la carte)--a little boat-plate of edamames, ginger and wasabi. I also liked that they had light soy sauce right there; I usually have to ask for it. The sushi chef was fast and attentive, though it was hard to talk to him through the ingredients shelf between us and him. The wait-staffers who took care of water, tea, etc. were attentive and pleasant. Sushi portions too small (one star off), "adequate" rolls (one more), price too high for what we got (another). Mostly I'm just disappointed that the boats aren't "live" and don't carry anything ready-to-eat. "Sushi Boat" Restaurant is a misnomer, period.
label: NEG

text: I love this park. I love how much there is to do in this park. I love how much parking there is in this park. I absolutely love the playground. Also, it's fenced in, so it's very easy to watch your kids while they play. Also, they have the ground covered in foam so there's none of that rocks in your shoes cutting up your knees when you fall, problem. As for the Christmas light display, I love this one. You can rent out horse carriages and ride through with a blanket over you and whoever you choose to ride through with. You can drive through too and turn your radio to the local Christmas station that the park uses during the Christmas season. The lights are gorgeous and not really tacky the way that Jellystone Park tends to be. text: Ugh. My boyfriend and I had an hour to kill before the 9:30 viewing of Black Swan at the Ritz Saturday night. She pointed to the corner where there was a two-top, right next to the bathroom. I shrugged. She handed us two menus and we sat ourselves. Hungry and ready to order, it had been almost ten minutes before anyone even acknowledged us at the table. No water, no silverware. I flagged down that same woman twice before she came over. We ordered one soup and one entree (chicken and eggplant). It was 30 minutes before they came out. We scarfed down our food and told the woman we had a movie to get to. text: Oh Qdoba, I do love those giant burritos so. There is not much I can say about Qdoba that you will not already know. They are known for their giant burritos like another chain restaurant, but they have more than just burritos. They have a Mexican Gumbo that is very tasty as well as tacos, quesidillas and nachos. For me what sets Qdoba apart is their fiery habanero salsa. It is a spicey salsa, but it's not hot for the sake of being hot, the taste of the habanero is great and I normally ask for a second helping of the salsa on whatever I get. As usual the staff was friendly and courteous and a few minutes after entered the store I was walking out with a giant burrito on my way home to enjoy the tasty goodness of the chicken queso burrito.

text: I feel like Channel City is hidden little secret of Goleta. With Home Depot just down the road in the Costo Shopping Center, and their secretive location at the end of Aero Camino next to the tracks and 101, I'm suprised that they're still in business. They are a ma and pa type hardware store with a huge drive in lumber yard in the back. Sometimes I go to home depot out of convenience for all hardware/home repair needs, but 3 times now, I've gone to Home Depot looking for a specific piece of hardware (screws nuts bolts), or something needed to do a basic home repair, and home depot has been out of it...or their stock was in such disorder that I gave up trying to find it after digging through the unopened boxes of stuff. I go to Channel City, am greeted by a friendly howdy at the counter and what do you know, they have exactly what I'm looking for exactly where it should be. The staff is ma and pa shop friendly. The support contractor accounts. You can drive your vehicle right up to the stacks of lumber in huge yard in back...no more loading it on to a cart, dragging it up to the front counter, having them awkwardly look for the barcode on the end of each piece, then rolling out to your car in the lot. The guys who work in back will even give you a hand and help you tie it down or secure it. Channel City is a great local business, I support them any day over home depot.
label: POS

text: Recommended by a co-worker, I thought I would give it a try. The restaurant looked quite nice from the outside with private and street parking available. The atmosphere inside was very nice, comfortable and cozy. Prices are reasonable for the quality of food served. Started off with a half dozen Blue Point raw oysters, $1.50 each. Awesome. Fresh. Delicious. Ordered 3 more right away. Wow! Next dish was a Sundried salad, $8, baby spinach, argula, sundried tomatoes, pine nuts, crumbled gorgonzola and herb Dijon dressing. Delicious, nice balanced taste. Since my co-worker mentioned that steaks were very good, my main course was naturally a nice piece of steak. I ordered the 12oz New York Strip, medium-rare. The dish came with veggies and potatoes. The steak was awesome, cooked the right way and at the right temperature. My friend ordered the special Pork tenderloin wrapped with bacon and served with fried polenta. The Pork tenderloin was so juicy and tender, impressive. For dessert I had the Classic Creme Brulee. There were so many other dishes on the menu that I would've like to order but that will just make it that more enticing for my return. Service was par excellance! Service was professional and fast. Will definitely be back to try other items on the well-stocked menu.
label: POS

text: Absolutely RUDE! I made my 6:30 reservation on time, the place was about a quarter full, MAYBE 15 tables occupied- we could see clean ones right in front of us. I was told by a very surly hostess- who had no record of our reservation and rolled her eyes when I said it was through Opentable -that they were short a server and we would have to wait. No offer to sit at the bar, no estimate of how long, acted like all this was our fault! Fine, but 20 minutes later and we still had people ahead of us, we're still standing there while she brings people their beers who were already seated, and in no hurry about it. I was wondering to my friend whether we could just grab the menu in front of us and go sit at the clean table that was 8 feet away which had been ready to go the whole time we were there when a server jumps into my conversation saying "you can't do that" and said they were BUSY. Then he turned his back on me mid-conversation as I was trying to politely explain that we were hungry and had been waiting for a 15-second interaction that would enable us to at least take off our coats. Needless to say I freaked out- I never make scenes but that was the last straw. He told me to have a nice day as I stormed out. I have been in the restaurant business. People call out. You have a server MIA the customer should not even notice anything is different much less be told the backroom details by two members of staff. A manager should have been out there comping drinks and making soothing noises if his staff couldn't handle a little glitch like that. And the hostess should be taking care of the duty she is paid for first. You can't have people looking like they are waiting for a bus in your vestibule at the expense of some guy having to wait 2 minutes longer for suds. Inexcusable.

text: While the Santa Barbara Hotel has an impeccable reputation, great location, and plenty of history, it does leave a lot to be desired. The rooms are very small and awkwardly designed, something attributing to the design of buildings at the time when it was seen as more desirable to have access to a window than a spacious room. The toiletries seemed the equivalent of a motel six despite the Hilton styled cost. The towels and bed linens, likewise, were not on par with expectations. And in general, the countryside choice of furniture doesn't seem to fit this obviously Spanish styled city. The rooms are clean and nicely kept, thank god. And the lobby and staff are more suited to the image of Santa Barbara. If you've picked out this hotel looking for value or budget friendly accommodations, I suggest you go elsewhere. There's a Holiday Inn Express a block away that has recently been renovated and fully furnished with great big new mattresses at similar prices.
label: NEG

text: Usually when the fam drags me to a festival 5 or 6 times a year to look at wild flowers or nick knack patty whack craft type stuff I have to wade through the b.s. to find the handful of food and beverage booths. Not in this case. It's AAALLLLL about the food. We went to Baton Rouge to visit our youngest at LSU and catch a football game on Saturday. A buddy of mine told me that the Oak Street PoBoy Festival was the following Sunday and suggested that we check it out if we had time. Sunday morning with some encouragement the wife and youngest agreed to appease me and we arrived at the festival as it opened at 11:00 a.m. The first hour or so the crowd was pretty thin and we were able to either walk right up or wait in a small line for whatever we wanted. By the time we left about 1:30 the place was slammed. There were probably fifty or so restaurants from all over New O that had booths and offered Po Boys, soups, desserts, or something awesome. Our favorites were the Roast Beef from Parkway Bakery and the corn n crab bisque from can't remember. We will be back but we will time it so we can stay in New O after the festival and so we can stay longer and drink. (had to drive back to Baton Rouge after).

text: Chaucer's is the only bookstore I've been to where the shelves are incapable of containing the multitude of books. While the resulting feel is a little bit hectic, I can't say that I don't like it. The selection is huge, with books of every kind and a happily robust fiction section. The aisles are narrow and the shelves overflow with books, so that even the floor boasts a hefty display of titles. The atmosphere is homey with a sense of comfortable chaos that befits a bookstore named for the author of the Canterbury Tales. I like that it's a large and comprehensive independent bookstore, and I'm happy that it appears to do pretty well. If I lived in the Santa Barbara area, I'd be at Chaucer's all the time.

text: Forget the overblown steak mills of Pats and Geno's, Cosmi's unassuming corner deli is quietly delivering the best cheesesteak experience in Philadelphia bar none. Cosmi's takes the personal approach and the proof is in the pudding. Nom nom. -Bread - their standard roll is soft and delicious, but don't hesitate to try their sesame-seeded roll for a firmer, nuttier twist on the steak. Simply awesome. -Staff - these guys are chill and friendly and love to talk about the Phillies or whatever other breeze you feel like shooting while you're steak is cooking. The leading brands push 'hostility' as part of the authentic experience, but I prefer the peacenik approach at Cosmi's. Cons -Not a dang one.

text: Four of us went for Lunch on Monday. Started with the Charred Tomato soup, which was tasty, but the coriander sour cream was lost on us/ Also tried the Tuscan bean soup, and expected there to be beans floating in a bean soup, but it was more bean broth with a pasty glob of mushrooms and barley floating in the middle of the soup. The bean broth was nice, but not the soup we expected. Ordered the Almost Classic Cobb. It was nothing like any Cobb salad I had ever had, and not in a good way. The Pancetta crisp was so thin and tasteless. The roasted chicken was, I think, still in the kitchen because it wasn't on the salad. There were plenty of olives, and a smathering of cucumber and not enough white cheddar cheese to be counted as an actual ingredient. There were 2 hard boiled egg halves, but the kind of hard boiled eggs that arrive in 5 gallon buckets in a brine solution. The cherry tomatoes we cold, so they had absolutely no taste, and the creamy oregano dressing was totally unremarkable. Somebody had the Sirloin burger and was totally happy with it. There was a beautiful think slice of tomato on the burger, but since it had been refrigerated, it was mushy and tasteless.....(don't restaurants know not to refrigerate tomatoes?) The shave lettuce slaw was wet and unexciting. Another ordered the Open face crab cake sandwich. It was tasty, but the Old Bay Slaw tasted like wet Savoy cabbage with precious little dressing of any kind for flavor. Lastly, the 4th party was very happy with her Citrus pork Panini with Manchego cheese and BBQ glaze. The presentation was great on everything. The Garlic fries came in little mini fry baskets ( these look like they came from Dollar Tree) and were hot when they cam to the table, but cooled rather quickly. They were also a little too greasy and garlicky for our taste. Dessert was the Banana Beignet. They were a great hit in their oun little bag fresh out of the fryer with the creme anglaise, with a hint of hazel nut (more like a secret). Also for Dessert was the Peanut butter Mousse. There was a plate with "stuff" on it but nobody was quite sure what was supposed to happen with the "stuff". It required some assembly. Well if I didnt get the directions to this place I wouldnt have happened by it. Walking down the side street behind Rouge (Chancellor St.), and a couple feet down in front of a dumpster is a door on the left that says "Stir." We got to the place and I was like "okay." But when we walked in I was like "okaaaaay." I was quite surprised. The shady looking exterior was transformed into a swank, cool interior. Walking in you are right at the main bar which has plenty of seating and nice, friendly bartenders who are very attentive. Lots of nice art and cool decor. Walking down a ways from the front are the restrooms a small seating area and then another cool bar area surrounded by bench style seating, and some more cool art. I would have preferred that the seating directly in front of the bar were not there since it gets cramped if people are seated there and the bar area is crowded. There is a small dance floor to the left of the bar and the Dj is there as well. This seems to be a cool, place to have a few drinks and hang out with friends, but not a pick up place if thats what you are looking for. The crowd is mixed, gay, straight, bi, what have you. But all are friendly, fun and not as pretentious as some places on the Square. Nice to see some diversity on the Square!

text: I booked this room here because it was close to my parents house. I got a good deal through Expedia's site (bad mistake) but I should have done more research on the place before booking. Pulling up I knew it wasn't going to be great. The motel is in the JB's parking lot (JB's is a Denny's type restaurant). It's an old nondescript building. When we checked in the woman taking care of our reservation was eating takeout noodles at the same time. She continued to chew and wipe her mouth with her sleeve as she checked us in. None of the employees wore name tags or uniforms so it looked as though they were guests who decided to hop behind the counter. We got our room keys which had advertisements for Domino's pizza on them, not a very classy impression. Our room was small but it was clean. There were no lamps at all so the only lights were florescent lights. The bed was so bad it bounced with every move we made no matter how small. They put us on the first floor next to a jr.high sports group which took up about 5 rooms around us. They only stayed one night but I was shocked the motel didn't consider that when we checked in...perhaps she was too busy eating. We did finally get good service when we requested new pillows the second time. The first time we got this lumpy pathetic pillow. When I returned to the front desk the next morning the woman (again no name tag) was apologetic and informed me she'd ensure we got better pillows (which we did that night). When we returned late one night the gentleman at the front desk greeted us nicely and gladly helped us when our keys weren't working. These two employees made up for the horrible experience checking in with the hungry employee and the bad room. If it weren't for them it would have been a horrible trip. So thank you to both of them - too bad they didn't have name tags or I could have been more specific. We won't be staying at the Sandman again because it wasn't a comfortable room nor a relaxing nights sleep and isn't that what matters most when you stay in a motel?

text: I looked at the waitress on my first day and said, "I feel like I'm cheatin' on my mama." I honestly believed my mom was the best homecooking expert until this day. While I expected (especially on Trinity Lane) a Old Time Pottery clearance basket with a napkin in it holding bread slung at me, I was surprised to to see a asian inspired long plate of gourmet home-style breads brought promptly to the table with my drink served in a Mason jar. The biscuits, rolls and cornbread make for enough to deserve a 5-star rating here. The REAL food though...I can't even put into words (as a fat man). The pot roast, mac and cheese, mashed potatoes, corn fritters, green beans, all are amazing. The fried chicken is great...and how can you make fried chicken better...no clue...but they did. I really don't like creme brulee. I'll eat it, but prefer something else. They have won me over on this stuff now. It's thick, generous and perfectly torched. The have a listserv to alert you to the daily specials, tons of space and ridiculously friendly wait staff. Go eat. Let's keep this place alive and well in Nashville!

text: I've been a regular staple on South street since I was one of those annoying noisy think I'm so cool high schoolers. For Starters we had the Sante Fe Salad w/ grilled Chicken [which I stated in my order, but the waitress did not take our order correctly and had to come back twice to check we had ordered exactly]. The salad was AWESOME but a bit pricey at $9 for a very small serving. It came with tortilla strips, jack cheese, and a really yummy bbq ranch dressing. Our waitress though very nice was clueless, the lady refilling the water would come by and fill one our of our 3 glasses. There was always an empty glass for some odd reason she would not fill. I guess if you want to try this place. On a nice afternoon, it's always a Nice place to grab a drink and sit out on the patio with appetizers, but if you want to sit down for a meal. text: A nice n' quaint place out in the country...worth a look! Dinner and drinks at the Washington, show at the Theater, fun time had by all. It is the very definition of "old school", mostly in terms of ambiance. If it looks like a holdover from colonial days...well, it is. The interior is warm and inviting, and the staff is most friendly. Even if you are just getting drinks, you'll know the name of your bartender in short order. The food is inventive and changes with the seasons, and on certain days every month they have wine and beer tastings. Different happy hour specials every day as well (both food and drink). You can just do the bar food thing if you want, from wings to crab chips (godlike)! Cheaper (but no less good) sandwiches and the like round out the bar menu if you don't want to do the full dinner experience. If you find yourself fighting traffic to get downtown weekend after weekend, and wonder why...well, don't. Turn around and come here. Find something that interests you at the Theatre and make it a complete evening. Its different, to be sure...but worthy of your time.

text: Pirrone's is right down the street from my house and is the perfect neighborhood restaurant. Let me start with their salads... I don't know what it is about their salads, but they are amazing! They are incredibly basic with only lettuce, tomatoes, Provel cheese, and dressing, but they are so good. The portions are gigantic. The child's size salad is equivalent to any other restaurant's basic side salad. Eat the small salad and you probably won't have much room for your entree. Eat the large salad and you have enough food to feed a family of four for a week. I recently bought two of their large salads to take to a pot luck and it filled up a large mixing bowl. Unlike other reviewers, I'm not a fan of their pizza. If I want St. Louis pizza, I'm going to Imo's, sorry. I'm also really picky about red sauces and meat sauces. Pirrone's meat sauce doesn't get me excited. I'll eat it, but there are other restaurants with better sauce, in my opinion. Their chicken parmesan is really good. It comes with a side and if you get the pasta with red sauce, it is almost enough for another meal. Like I said about the salads, the portions are huge. I also really like their pasta con broccoli. The staff is usually very friendly. They offer a lunch buffet during the week. This is great way to sample their various dishes.

It was a traditional italian dressing (perfectly tangy) with provel cheese, lettuce, and pimentos. Oh so very tasty!! Not redeeming enough for the restaurant as a whole, though. I got the fettucini alfredo with chicken. First of all, the sauce wasn't spectacular. It was a little thick and somebody over there REALLY loves pepper. It was all over my dish. In fact, my husband had a side of white sauce cavatelli noodles and it was all over his too. There wasn't just a dash of pepper, either. Oh no, someone was clearly standing over my fettucini for a few minutes really grinding that stuff on. In my opinion, if the sauce is that good, you don't need to put ANYTHING on it. I wouldn't even think to put salt or pepper on my alfredo dish. The chicken also wasn't very good. It seemed like it was the pre-chunked chicken you'd buy in a package at the store. It has those fake grill marks on it? The grill marks you can practically peel off? I expected more from this place. For dessert I had a strawberry cheesecake cupcake. Mostly it was just a tiny cupcake-shaped piece of cheesecake with a strawberry on top. It was tasty, but not worth a trip back. Hopefully my experience was an anomaly and someone else was able to taste a better meal with better service.

text: Pat's IS the quintessential cheesesteak joint in Philly. Whenever one of my friends even utters the word "Pat's" I usually just put my shoes on because we're going. We've gotten to the point where we'll just look at each other and say, "You know where we SHOULD go..." Winter, summer, spring, or fall - it is my understanding this place is open 24/7. No questions asked. There's usually a line at 3:00 a.m. and my brother bought one at 8:30 a.m. once on his way to a business meeting. Yummy any time of day. Geno's is across the street, and they apparently make a very similar steak, but I refuse to eat one. The line at Pat's is always longer, so that must mean it's better, right? We've dubbed Geno's "The Circus" due to their over zealous neon lights. It's ridiculous, actually. There's a homeless guy who wonders around Pat's cleaning up and giving people napkins if they need them. He's awesome. We usually give him a couple bucks. Don't be nervous. He's polite and friendly. The steaks: Order a heart attack. It's Whiz, provolone and American cheeses. It's delicious. The rolls are on the softer side, and the cheese and grease will drip so exercise caution. My friend always orders a "pizza pepper with" that has hot peppers and pizza sauce. He loves it. They have a few specialty steaks like that one on the menu, but you should really go with something standard like a "whiz with" for your first time. Steaks are like $6 or $7 these days. My brother decided he was going to eat five heart attacks in one sitting. It was December. I left after he put three down because I was freezing my ass off. (The seating is all outside.) He ate five, didn't swallow the last bite til he was going over the Ben Franklin Bridge. I don't think he returned for over one year. The cheese fries are bangin'. Order EXTRA cheese fries and get the "swimmers" at the bottom using a fork. So much cheese. So much delicious. After years of Coke products, they recently switched to Pepsi. I was sorta upset but I'm over it now. They still have a good variety of sodas to choose from. You can bring your own bottle of water or something. No big deal. Be discreet if you are drinking alcohol. I'm pretty sure it's illegal. Bottom line, Pat's is the place you should go if you are from out of town and want to get the "Philly cheesesteak" experience.
label: POS

text: Went with my mom last Thursday for a dinner meeting for her work. She went to join her group, and I asked the host to seat me at a table or booth big enough for two, since she'd be coming back to join me when she was finished. Then they left me there for about ten minutes without asking if I wanted something to drink or some chips and salsa...nothing. It wasn't even busy! When a server did come around, he acted confused when I said I'd like to order while waiting for my mom. Maybe it seemed like bad manners to eat before my party arrived, but I was hungry! The ambiance where I was seated was very suffocating. No windows, black walls, dark carpet, confining booths with black plastic table cloths... Even with the lights, it felt less like a romantic dimness and more like I was eating in a converted basement. I kept asking myself, "What are they trying to hide?" I'd just placed my order when my mom showed up bearing her own plate of food, which she'd ordered in the meeting. She'd just recently had a tooth extraction and was eating something unidentifiable fried in egg. I asked what it was, and with a weak smile she replied, "Bland," and reached for the salsa. Speaking of which, the chips and salsa were pretty "meh." The chips looked and tasted sort of stale, and I prefer a chunkier salsa. The mild one was pretty forgettable, and the hot one had more spice than flavor. I had been torn between ordering the carnitas and the beef/chicken combo fajitas. I had decided to go with the latter, since it sounded like it came with more veggies. (Radishes? What?) But when it arrived, it wasn't quite what I'd been expecting. The meat had been sliced extremely thin, almost julienne, and unless I squinted, I couldn't really tell the difference between the two. There was no difference in taste, either, which as Mom had said, was pretty bland. The Spanish rice was fluffy and flavorful enough. The refried beans were typical. And for the price, they only give you two tortillas which didn't even get me through half my plate. (I hear you can get three if you order corn tortillas, though I assume that's because they're smaller.) I usually try to clear everything on my plate, but I just couldn't. I picked out what I thought was most edible and left the rest, I was so disappointed. The only highlight was the flan. It was thick and sweet, with a slight cinnamon grittiness to it that was appealing. It was big enough to share with Mom, so I did. I left feeling unsatisfied and wanting a real dinner to make up for this one. It wasn't horrendous, but it wasn't anything to shout about, either. I doubt I'll return unless Mom has to have another meeting there.

text: Please if you are thinking of taking your pet here..go somewhere else! I just came back from the worst experience of my life. After having problems and seeing Dr Rose 2 weeks ago(he is excellent) ,over the past several weeks the difficult decision to euthanize my 11 year old dog was made by my family. I had called and also asked in person several times as to how this would work. I asked for charges and how it would be handled on the day of, I even asked if I could pay in advance so I could just take my dog and not have to deal with anything else but her that day. I was told it would cost around $205, we would come in, be put in a private room and we would pay in advance and have all that done then they would euthanize her. We could stay as long as we wanted and leave by a separate entrance. Okay so we braced ourselves for what we had to do. Today we get there before they start appointments and are put in one room and told the dog will have a catheter put in place and receptionist will be in for paperwork. 10 minutes goes by and then we are taken to another room where Dr. Michelle Parker goes through a whole spiel of why we don't have to do this now.. I understand they need to protect themselves. I have to explain her health situation and my reasons and tell her again and again the decision has been made. She spoke to us as if we were too stupid to understand what we were about to do, because there were still options left. It took time and thought for me to get to this point and I explained how I no longer wanted to do anything that I know would only delay the inevitable. They then finally take my dog to have the catheter put in. The receptionist comes in to get payment. It is now $250 and we're told thats because Dr Parker never saw my dog before. Well if you told me during the many times I called or asked that there would be that charge, I would have waited to do this when a doctor who had seen my dog before was there. Next they send the Office Manager to come in to speak to us. This is turning into a total nightmare. I just want to do what I came for and get out of there. Next the doctor comes in. And talking down to us again about how this is how veterinary medecine works, my daughter explains to her that we asked again and again about how this day would go and nowhere did anyone say that we would be charged for a new doctor to examine her. Had we been told I would have been prepared and not minded paying the fee. Dr Parker finally snapped at us and said "Oh so I'll just take off my fee is THAT what you want?" She then turned to the receptionist and in a disgusted voice told her take off the fee and as she walked out the door snottily said you can either have this done or go elsewhere. We paid and the dog was brought in to us and within a minute the doctor came back in and abruptly asked us did we want the dog on the table or the floor. We had to ask if we could have five minutes with her. Each time I spoke with someone today from receptionist to doctor, I explained to them how they were making the worst day of my life even more difficult. They did not care. All they cared about was that they get their money. So now here I sit and instead of being able to recall fond memories of my dog, all I can think about is what a disaster her last moments were. We were poorly treated last year with our other dog in trying to get paperwork done for her to be allowed to live in Hawaii. (Pets being brought into the islands have to have all kinds of extra shots and complicated paperwork). Thats another long story, but basically were told if you don't like it here, good luck finding another doctor in Delaware County who does this paperwork. I only stayed on with them because my other dog was old and I didn't want to switch her around at that point. PLEASE if you don't want to be treated like dollar signs, find someplace that has compassionate staff and doctors.

Normally, I would discourage this practice, but these people are doing something so simple, yet so special, it begs to be shared with the world. They use fresh, high quality, delicious ingredients, and more veggies (and more unique veggies) than most taquerias. To simply call it a chicken quesadilla is sort of an insult, because that's what they make at Chevy's or El Torito, and this was something so much better. La Super-Rica is closed on Tuesdays, so plan accordingly! You don't want to get your heart broken.

text: The Venture Inn has been a tradition in the somewhat seedy world of the Gay-borhood of Philadelphia. With more and open acceptance of different life styles, however, new, upscale, expensive and even outstanding eateries have popped up all over the place in the Washington Square area that cater to mainly a gay clientele, and therefore some of the old places have been left behind. The Venture is one of them. Although a "grand dame" of the community, it nonetheless has been left behind and nowadays caters to mainly an adult community, from which the moniker "The Denture Inn" has emerged. Although unjust, its reputation continues despite new management and what seems to be an honest effort at changing its character. The small side street where Venture is Camac Street, one of the numerous alley-type streets all over the older part of Philadelphia. These small streets have become more pricey and upscale, however, Camac has maintained a sort of seedy reputation due to its commercial employment. We went to the Venture Inn just to see how things had changed. I'm afraid they haven't sufficiently to go there again. In four categories, service, food, ambiance, and price, it loses to the neighboring establishments. First the service. Our waiter was obviously used to the older crowd and seemed to want to be our friend from the start. Frankly, if I wanted to be friends with a waiter, I'd make it outside of a restaurant. His overtures seemed pedantic, especially compared to the mediocre service we got which included forgetting a round of drinks we ordered with dinner. Second, the food. The mussels I ordered came in a tasty sauce. However, there were several unopened, bad ones. That is something any good restaurant would be able to screen. The food was generally good, although the presentation was "homey", not what you would expect for the price. No espresso. Third, the ambiance. On a beautiful cool summer evening in Philadelphia, al fresco seating would have been a plus. The Venture Inn restaurant sits in a building where the smoke stench has permeated the walls over decades and decades. The yellowish walls attest to the nicotine and tar of the pre-smoke prohibition in Philadelphia. Frankly, I was gasping for breath after an hour. Fourth, the price. We spent forty per person including a glass of wine each. Right around the corner, I can get the same at an upscale, new, saucy Mixto restaurant that features Cuban/Colombian infusion with knock-your-socks off service and outstanding ambiance and food. It is obvious by the clientele surrounding us that the Venture is happily within its core clientele of tired gay men in their 60s to whom a disrespectful out-of-shape waiter and mediocre food is a compliment.
label: NEG

One last drawback: for a brewery that specializes in ales, I can't for the life of me figure out why they don't have an IPA on tap as a staple. Pale Ale is good enough though. They also now sell wine, but do not expect to order a Bud Light here--they don't serve it (thankfully!). Go "find" Nimbus for youself!!

You have to be strategic about where you park and where you want to shop, or else you will end up being hounded by every salesman at those worthless kiosks of crap that litter the place. To end on a positive--there are two huge restaurants there--Aquarium and Rainforest Cafe, neither of which I have been to, but they seem like they are decent for families with kids. If you are a tourist staying out at Opryland Hotel, this is a restaurant option outside of the hotel. The IMAX theater is pretty cool too, but that is totally separate in my eyes. But it is there. If you decide to go, beware the traffic, the crowds, and the crappy stores. Want some really good shopping in town?
